   101→def subjective_score_value(item: dict[str, Any]) -> float:
   102→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
   103→        detail = detail_dict(item)
   104→        return float(detail.get("strict_score", item.get("subjective_score", 100.0)))
   105→    return float(item.get("subjective_score", 100.0))
   106→
   107→
   108→def build_issue_items(
   109→    state: StateModel,
   110→    *,
   111→    scan_path: str | None,
   112→    status_filter: str,
   113→    scope: str | None,
   114→    chronic: bool,
   115→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   116→    scoped = path_scoped_issues(state.get("issues", {}), scan_path)
   117→    subjective_scores = subjective_strict_scores(state)
   118→    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   119→
   120→    for issue_id, issue in scoped.items():
   121→        if issue.get("suppressed"):
   122→            continue
   123→        if not status_matches(issue.get("status", "open"), status_filter):
   124→            continue
   125→        if chronic and not (
   126→            issue.get("status") == "open" and issue.get("reopen_count", 0) >= 2
   127→        ):
   128→            continue
   129→
   130→        # Evidence-only: skip issues below standalone confidence threshold
   131→        detector = issue.get("detector", "")
   132→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   133→        if meta and meta.standalone_threshold:
   134→            threshold_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(meta.standalone_threshold, 9)
   135→            issue_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(issue.get("confidence", "low"), 9)
   136→            if issue_rank > threshold_rank:
   137→                continue
   138→
   139→        item = dict(issue)
   140→        item["id"] = issue_id
   141→        item["kind"] = "issue"
   142→        item["is_review"] = is_review_issue(item)
   143→        item["is_subjective"] = is_subjective_issue(item)
   144→        item["review_weight"] = (
   145→            review_issue_weight(item) if item["is_review"] else None
   146→        )
   147→        subjective_score = None
   148→        if item["is_subjective"]:
   149→            detail = detail_dict(issue)
   150→            dim_name = detail.get("dimension_name", "")
   151→            dim_key = detail.get("dimension", "") or slugify(dim_name)
   152→            subjective_score = subjective_scores.get(
   153→                dim_key, subjective_scores.get(dim_name.lower(), 100.0)
   154→            )
   155→        item["subjective_score"] = subjective_score
   156→        supported_fixers = supported_fixers_for_item(state, item)
   157→        item["primary_command"] = primary_command_for_issue(
   158→            item,
   159→            supported_fixers=supported_fixers,
   160→        )
   161→
   162→        if not scope_matches(item, scope):
   163→            continue
   164→        out.append(item)
   165→
   166→    return out
   167→
   168→
   169→def _natural_sort_key(item: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple:
   170→    """Compute natural (non-plan-aware) ranking for queue items."""
   171→    kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
   172→
   173→    # Initial-review subjective items: highest priority
   174→    if kind == "subjective_dimension" and item.get("initial_review"):
   175→        return (_RANK_INITIAL_REVIEW, 0, subjective_score_value(item), item.get("id", ""))
   176→
   177→    # Triage stage items: stage order, blocked after unblocked
   178→    if kind == "workflow_stage":
   179→        blocked_penalty = 1 if item.get("is_blocked") else 0
   180→        stage_index = int(item.get("stage_index", 0))
   181→        return (_RANK_TRIAGE_STAGE, blocked_penalty, stage_index, item.get("id", ""))
   182→
   183→    # Workflow action items (e.g. create-plan)
   184→    if kind == "workflow_action":
   185→        return (_RANK_WORKFLOW, 0, 0, item.get("id", ""))
   186→
   187→    if kind == "cluster":
   188→        # Clusters sort before individual issues, ordered by action type
   189→        action_pri = ACTION_TYPE_PRIORITY.get(
   190→            item.get("action_type", "manual_fix"), 3
   191→        )
   192→        return (
   193→            _RANK_CLUSTER,
   194→            action_pri,
   195→            -int(item.get("member_count", 0)),
   196→            item.get("id", ""),
   197→        )
   198→
   199→    impact = item.get("estimated_impact", 0.0)
   200→
   201→    if kind == "subjective_dimension" or item.get("is_subjective"):
   202→        return (
   203→            _RANK_ISSUE,
   204→            -impact,
   205→            subjective_score_value(item),
   206→            item.get("id", ""),
   207→        )
   208→
   209→    detail = detail_dict(item)
   210→    review_weight = float(item.get("review_weight", 0.0) or 0.0)
   211→    return (
   212→        _RANK_ISSUE,
   213→        -impact,
   214→        CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(item.get("confidence", "low"), 9),
   215→        -review_weight,
   216→        -int(detail.get("count", 0) or 0),
   217→        item.get("id", ""),
   218→    )
   219→
   220→
   221→def item_sort_key(item: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple:
   222→    """Unified sort key: plan position first, then natural ranking.
   223→
   224→    When ``_plan_position`` is stamped (by :func:`stamp_plan_sort_keys`),
   225→    planned items sort first in plan order, then existing items by natural
   226→    ranking, then newly-discovered items by natural ranking.
   227→
   228→    When no plan fields are stamped, falls back to pure natural ranking.
   229→    """
   230→    plan_pos = item.get("_plan_position")
   231→
   232→    if plan_pos is not None:
   233→        kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
   234→        # Triage stages: even when explicitly planned, maintain the
   235→        # blocked-before-unblocked invariant for correctness.
   236→        if kind == "workflow_stage":
   237→            blocked = 1 if item.get("is_blocked") else 0
   238→            stage_idx = int(item.get("stage_index", 0))
   239→            return (_TIER_PLANNED, blocked, stage_idx, item.get("id", ""))
   240→        return (_TIER_PLANNED, 0, plan_pos, item.get("id", ""))
   241→
   242→    is_new = item.get("_is_new", False)
   243→    group = _TIER_NEW if is_new else _TIER_EXISTING
   244→    return (group, *_natural_sort_key(item))

   247→def item_explain(item: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   248→    kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
   249→    if kind == "workflow_stage":

   252→            "stage": item.get("stage_name"),
   253→            "is_blocked": item.get("is_blocked", False),
   254→            "blocked_by": item.get("blocked_by", []),

   256→            "ranking_factors": ["blocked_penalty asc", "stage_index asc"],

   259→    if kind == "workflow_action":

   262→            "policy": "Workflow items sort after triage stages, before issues.",
   263→            "ranking_factors": ["id asc"],
   264→        }
   265→
   266→    if kind == "cluster":

   270→            "action_type": item.get("action_type", "manual_fix"),
   271→            "member_count": item.get("member_count", 0),

   273→            "ranking_factors": ["action_type asc", "member_count desc", "id asc"],

   287→            ),

   289→        }
   290→
   291→    detail = detail_dict(item)
   292→    confidence = item.get("confidence", "low")

   294→    is_review = bool(item.get("is_review"))
   295→    ranking_factors: list[str]

   303→            "count desc",
   304→            "id asc",
   305→        ]
   306→    else:

   308→    explain = {

   311→        "confidence": confidence,
   312→        "confidence_rank": CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(confidence, 9),
   313→        "count": int(detail.get("count", 0) or 0),
   314→        "id": item.get("id", ""),
   315→        "ranking_factors": ranking_factors,
   316→    }
   317→    if is_review:

   319→    if is_subjective:

   327→def group_queue_items(
   328→    items: list[dict[str, Any]], group: str
   329→) -> dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
   330→    """Group queue items for alternate output modes."""
   331→    grouped: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
   332→    for item in items:
   333→        if group == "file":
   334→            key = item.get("file", "")
   335→        elif group == "detector":
   336→            key = item.get("detector", "")
   337→        elif group == "cluster":
   338→            plan_cluster = item.get("plan_cluster")
   339→            key = plan_cluster["name"] if isinstance(plan_cluster, dict) else "(unclustered)"
   340→        else:
   341→            key = "items"
   342→        grouped.setdefault(key, []).append(item)
   343→    return grouped
   344→

1→"""TypeScript fixer loader utilities."""
     2→

     4→

     6→
     7→__all__ = [
     8→    "fix_debug_logs",
     9→    "fix_unused_imports",
    10→    "fix_unused_vars",
    11→    "fix_unused_params",
    12→    "fix_dead_useeffect",
    13→    "fix_empty_if_chain",
    14→]
    15→
    16→_EXPORT_MODULES = {
    17→    "fix_debug_logs": ".logs",
    18→    "fix_unused_imports": ".imports",
    19→    "fix_unused_vars": ".vars",
    20→    "fix_unused_params": ".params",
    21→    "fix_dead_useeffect": ".useeffect",
    22→    "fix_empty_if_chain": ".if_chain",
    23→}
    24→
    25→
    26→def __getattr__(name: str):
    27→    module_path = _EXPORT_MODULES.get(name)
    28→    if module_path is None:
    29→        raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")
    30→    module = importlib.import_module(module_path, __name__)
    31→    value = getattr(module, name)
    32→    globals()[name] = value
    33→    return value
    34→
    35→
    36→def __dir__() -> list[str]:
    37→    return sorted(set(globals()) | set(__all__))
    38→

   107→def fix_debug_logs(entries: list[dict], *, dry_run: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
   108→    """Remove tagged console.log lines and clean up aftermath (dead vars, empty blocks)."""
   109→    entries_by_file: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
   110→    for e in entries:
   111→        entries_by_file.setdefault(e["file"], []).append(e)
   112→
   113→    def _transform(lines: list[str], file_entries: list[dict]):
   114→        lines_to_remove: set[int] = set()
   115→        for e in file_entries:
   116→            start = e["line"] - 1
   117→            if start >= len(lines):
   118→                continue
   119→            if _is_logger_wrapper_context(lines, start):
   120→                continue
   121→            end = find_balanced_end(lines, start, track="parens")
   122→            if end is None:
   123→                print(
   124→                    colorize(
   125→                        f"  Warn: skipping {rel(e['file'])}:{e['line']} — could not find statement end",
   126→                        "yellow",
   127→                    ),
   128→                    file=sys.stderr,
   129→                )
   130→                continue
   131→            for idx in range(start, end + 1):
   132→                lines_to_remove.add(idx)
   133→            _mark_orphaned_comments(lines, start, lines_to_remove)
   134→
   135→        dead_vars = _find_dead_log_variables(lines, lines_to_remove)
   136→        lines_to_remove |= dead_vars
   137→        new_lines = collapse_blank_lines(lines, lines_to_remove)
   138→        new_lines = _remove_empty_blocks(new_lines)
   139→        tags = sorted(set(e.get("tag", "") for e in file_entries))
   140→        return new_lines, tags
   141→
   142→    raw_results = apply_fixer(entries, _transform, dry_run=dry_run)
   143→    return [
   144→        {
   145→            "file": r["file"],
   146→            "removed": r["removed"],
   147→            "tags": r["removed"],
   148→            "lines_removed": r["lines_removed"],
   149→            "log_count": len(entries_by_file.get(r["file"], [])),
   150→        }
   151→        for r in raw_results
   152→    ]

   155→def _normalize_wrapper_name(raw: str | None) -> str:
   156→    if not raw:
   157→        return ""
   158→    return raw.strip().strip("'\"").lower()
   159→
   160→
   161→def _is_logger_wrapper_name(raw: str | None) -> bool:
   162→    return _normalize_wrapper_name(raw) in _LOGGER_WRAPPER_NAMES
   163→
   164→
   165→def _line_logger_wrapper_name(line: str, patterns: tuple[re.Pattern[str], ...]) -> str | None:
   166→    for pattern in patterns:
   167→        match = pattern.match(line)
   168→        if match:
   169→            name = _normalize_wrapper_name(match.group("name"))
   170→            if name and name not in _CONTROL_FLOW_NAMES:
   171→                return name
   172→    return None
   173→
   174→
   175→def _previous_non_empty_line(lines: list[str], idx: int) -> str | None:
   176→    j = idx - 1
   177→    while j >= 0:
   178→        stripped = lines[j].strip()
   179→        if stripped:
   180→            return stripped
   181→        j -= 1
   182→    return None
   183→
   184→
   185→def _is_logger_wrapper_context(lines: list[str], start: int) -> bool:
   186→    """Return True when console logging is part of a named logger wrapper."""
   187→    current = lines[start].strip()
   188→    inline_name = _line_logger_wrapper_name(current, _INLINE_WRAPPER_PATTERNS)
   189→    if _is_logger_wrapper_name(inline_name):
   190→        return True
   191→
   192→    if not re.search(r"\bconsole\.(?:log|warn|info|debug|error)\s*\(", current):
   193→        return False
   194→
   195→    prev = _previous_non_empty_line(lines, start)
   196→    if prev is None:
   197→        return False
   198→    prev_name = _line_logger_wrapper_name(prev, _PREV_LINE_HEADER_PATTERNS)
   199→    return _is_logger_wrapper_name(prev_name)

   202→# ── Orphaned comment cleanup ──────────────────────────────
   203→
   204→_DEBUG_COMMENT_RE = re.compile(
   205→    r"(?:DEBUG|TEMP|LOG|TRACE|TODO\s*.*debug|HACK\s*.*log)", re.IGNORECASE

   208→
   209→def _mark_orphaned_comments(
   210→    lines: list[str], log_start: int, lines_to_remove: set[int]
   211→):
   212→    """Mark up to 3 preceding comment lines as orphaned if they contain debug annotations."""
   213→    for offset in range(1, 4):
   214→        idx = log_start - offset
   215→        if idx < 0:
   216→            break
   217→        if idx in lines_to_remove:
   218→            continue
   219→        prev = lines[idx].strip()
   220→        if not prev.startswith("//"):
   221→            break
   222→        if _DEBUG_COMMENT_RE.search(prev):
   223→            lines_to_remove.add(idx)

   229→_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"\b([a-zA-Z_$]\w*)\b")
   230→
   231→_IGNORE_IDENTS = frozenset(
   232→    [
   233→        "console",
   234→        "log",
   235→        "warn",
   236→        "info",
   237→        "debug",
   238→        "error",
   239→        "const",
   240→        "let",
   241→        "var",
   242→        "true",
   243→        "false",
   244→        "null",
   245→        "undefined",
   246→        "if",
   247→        "else",
   248→        "return",
   249→        "function",
   250→        "new",
   251→        "this",
   252→        "typeof",
   253→        "length",
   254→        "toString",
   255→        "JSON",
   256→        "stringify",
   257→        "Date",
   258→        "now",
   259→        "Math",
   260→        "Object",
   261→        "Array",
   262→        "String",
   263→        "Number",
   264→        "Boolean",
   265→        "Map",
   266→        "Set",
   267→        "Promise",
   268→        "Error",
   269→    ]
   270→)
   271→
   272→
   273→def _find_dead_log_variables(lines: list[str], removed_indices: set[int]) -> set[int]:
   274→    """Find variable declarations that were only used in removed log lines."""
   275→    referenced_in_logs: set[str] = set()
   276→    for idx in removed_indices:
   277→        if idx < len(lines):
   278→            for m in _IDENT_RE.finditer(lines[idx]):
   279→                ident = m.group(1)
   280→                if ident not in _IGNORE_IDENTS:
   281→                    referenced_in_logs.add(ident)
   282→
   283→    if not referenced_in_logs:
   284→        return set()
   285→
   286→    decl_lines: dict[str, int] = {}
   287→    for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
   288→        if idx in removed_indices:
   289→            continue
   290→        m = _VAR_DECL_RE.match(line)
   291→        if m and m.group(1) in referenced_in_logs:
   292→            decl_lines[m.group(1)] = idx
   293→
   294→    if not decl_lines:
   295→        return set()
   296→
   297→    dead: set[int] = set()
   298→    for ident, decl_idx in decl_lines.items():
   299→        used_elsewhere = False
   300→        pattern = re.compile(r"\b" + re.escape(ident) + r"\b")
   301→        for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
   302→            if idx == decl_idx or idx in removed_indices:
   303→                continue
   304→            if pattern.search(line):
   305→                used_elsewhere = True
   306→                break
   307→        if not used_elsewhere:
   308→            dead.add(decl_idx)
   309→
   310→    return dead
   311→
   312→
   313→# ── Empty block cleaner ────────────────────────────────────
   314→
   315→_EMPTY_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
   316→    r"""
   317→    ^(\s*)
   318→    (?:
   319→        (?:if|else\s+if)\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{\s*\}
   320→        | else\s*\{\s*\}
   321→        | \}\s*else\s*\{\s*\}
   322→    )
   323→    \s*$
   324→    """,
   325→    re.VERBOSE,
   326→)
   327→
   328→_EMPTY_CALLBACK_RE = re.compile(
   329→    r"""
   330→    ^\s*
   331→    (?:
   332→        \.then\s*\(\s*\(?[^)]*\)?\s*=>\s*\{\s*\}\s*\)
   333→        | \.catch\s*\(\s*\(?[^)]*\)?\s*=>\s*\{\s*\}\s*\)
   334→    )
   335→    \s*[;,]?\s*$
   336→    """,
   337→    re.VERBOSE,
   338→)
   339→
   340→
   341→def _try_remove_empty_use_effect(
   342→    lines: list[str], i: int, new_lines: list[str]
   343→) -> int | None:
   344→    """Remove empty useEffect(() => { }). Returns new index or None."""
   345→    stripped = lines[i].strip()
   346→    if not re.match(r"(?:React\.)?useEffect\s*\(\s*\(\s*\)\s*=>\s*\{", stripped):
   347→        return None
   348→    end = find_balanced_end(lines, i, track="all")
   349→    if end is None:
   350→        return None
   351→    body = "".join(lines[i : end + 1])
   352→    inner = extract_body_between_braces(body, search_after="=>")
   353→    if inner is None or inner.strip() != "":
   354→        return None
   355→    if new_lines and new_lines[-1].strip().startswith("//"):
   356→        new_lines.pop()
   357→    return end + 1
   358→
   359→
   360→def _try_remove_empty_callback(lines: list[str], i: int) -> int | None:
   361→    """Remove single-line .then(() => { }) / .catch((e) => { })."""
   362→    if _EMPTY_CALLBACK_RE.match(lines[i].strip()):
   363→        return i + 1
   364→    return None
   365→
   366→
   367→def _try_remove_multiline_callback(lines: list[str], i: int) -> int | None:
   368→    """Remove multi-line empty callback: someFunc(() => {\\n})."""
   369→    stripped = lines[i].strip()
   370→    if not re.search(r"=>\s*\{\s*$", stripped):
   371→        return None
   372→    if not re.search(r"\(\s*(?:\([^)]*\))?\s*=>\s*\{\s*$", stripped):
   373→        return None
   374→    j = i + 1
   375→    while j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip() == "":
   376→        j += 1
   377→    if j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip() in ("});", "},"):
   378→        return j + 1
   379→    return None
   380→
   381→
   382→def _try_remove_multiline_block(
   383→    lines: list[str], i: int, new_lines: list[str]
   384→) -> int | None:
   385→    """Remove multi-line empty if/else/else-if blocks."""
   386→    line = lines[i]
   387→    stripped = line.strip()
   388→    if not stripped.endswith("{"):
   389→        return None
   390→    j = i + 1
   391→    while j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip() == "":
   392→        j += 1
   393→    if j >= len(lines) or lines[j].strip() not in ("}", "});"):
   394→        return None
   395→
   396→    if re.match(r"\s*else\s*\{", stripped):
   397→        return j + 1
   398→    if re.match(r"\s*\}\s*else\s*\{", stripped):
   399→        indent = line[: len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
   400→        new_lines.append(f"{indent}}}\n")
   401→        return j + 1
   402→    if re.match(r"\s*(?:if|else\s+if)\s*\(", stripped):
   403→        return j + 1
   404→    return None
   405→
   406→
   407→def _try_remove_single_empty_block(lines: list[str], i: int) -> int | None:
   408→    """Remove single-line empty block (if/else/else-if with empty {})."""
   409→    if _EMPTY_BLOCK_RE.match(lines[i].strip()):
   410→        return i + 1
   411→    return None
   412→
   413→
   414→def _remove_empty_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
   415→    """Remove empty blocks left behind after log removal.
   416→
   417→    Handles: empty if/else, empty useEffect, empty catch, empty callbacks.
   418→    Makes multiple passes until stable.
   419→    """
   420→    _handlers = [
   421→        lambda lines, i, out: _try_remove_empty_use_effect(lines, i, out),
   422→        lambda lines, i, out: _try_remove_empty_callback(lines, i),
   423→        lambda lines, i, out: _try_remove_multiline_callback(lines, i),
   424→        lambda lines, i, out: _try_remove_multiline_block(lines, i, out),
   425→        lambda lines, i, out: _try_remove_single_empty_block(lines, i),
   426→    ]
   427→    changed = True
   428→    while changed:
   429→        changed = False
   430→        new_lines: list[str] = []
   431→        i = 0
   432→        while i < len(lines):
   433→            new_i = None
   434→            for handler in _handlers:
   435→                new_i = handler(lines, i, new_lines)
   436→                if new_i is not None:
   437→                    break
   438→            if new_i is not None:
   439→                changed = True
   440→                i = new_i
   441→            else:
   442→                new_lines.append(lines[i])
   443→                i += 1
   444→        lines = new_lines
   445→
   446→    # Final pass: collapse double blank lines
   447→    result = []
   448→    prev_blank = False
   449→    for line in lines:
   450→        is_blank = line.strip() == ""
   451→        if is_blank and prev_blank:
   452→            continue
   453→        result.append(line)
   454→        prev_blank = is_blank
   455→    return result
   456→

    11→def fix_unused_imports(entries: list[dict], *, dry_run: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    12→    """Remove unused imports from source files."""
    13→    import_entries = [entry for entry in entries if entry.get("category") == "imports"]
    14→
    15→    def transform(lines: list[str], file_entries: list[dict[str, object]]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    16→        unused_symbols = {str(entry["name"]) for entry in file_entries if "name" in entry}
    17→        unused_by_line: dict[int, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    18→        for entry in file_entries:
    19→            line = entry.get("line")
    20→            name = entry.get("name")
    21→            if isinstance(line, int) and name is not None:
    22→                unused_by_line[line].append(str(name))
    23→
    24→        new_lines, removed_symbols = process_unused_import_lines(lines, unused_symbols, unused_by_line)

    26→        for entry in file_entries:
    27→            name = str(entry.get("name", ""))
    28→            if name in removed_symbols and name not in removed:
    29→                removed.append(name)
    30→        return new_lines, removed
    31→
    32→    return apply_fixer(import_entries, transform, dry_run=dry_run)

    11→import logging
    12→from datetime import UTC, datetime

    26→
    27→def impact_label(weight: float) -> str:
    28→    """Convert weight to a human-readable impact label."""
    29→    try:
    30→        numeric = float(weight)
    31→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    32→        return "+"
    33→    if numeric >= 8:
    34→        return "+++"
    35→    if numeric >= 5:
    36→        return "++"
    37→    return "+"
    38→
    39→
    40→def list_open_review_issues(state: dict) -> list[dict]:
    41→    """Return open review issues sorted by impact (highest first)."""
    42→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
    43→    review = [
    44→        issue
    45→        for issue in issues.values()
    46→        if issue.get("status") == "open" and issue.get("detector") == "review"
    47→    ]
    48→
    49→    def _sort_key(issue: dict) -> tuple[float, str]:
    50→        weight, _impact, issue_id = issue_weight(issue)
    51→        return (-weight, issue_id)
    52→
    53→    review.sort(key=_sort_key)
    54→    return review
    55→
    56→
    57→def update_investigation(state: dict, issue_id: str, text: str) -> bool:
    58→    """Store investigation text on a issue. Returns False if not found/not open."""
    59→    issue = state.get("issues", {}).get(issue_id)
    60→    if not issue or issue.get("status") != "open":
    61→        return False
    62→    detail = detail_dict(issue)
    63→    if not detail:
    64→        detail = {}
    65→        issue["detail"] = detail
    66→    detail["investigation"] = text
    67→    detail["investigated_at"] = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    68→    return True
    69→
    70→
    71→def expire_stale_holistic(state: dict, max_age_days: int = 30) -> list[str]:
    72→    """Auto-resolve holistic review issues older than max_age_days."""
    73→    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    74→    expired: list[str] = []
    75→
    76→    for issue_id, issue in state.get("issues", {}).items():
    77→        if issue.get("detector") != "review":
    78→            continue
    79→        if issue.get("status") != "open":
    80→            continue
    81→        if not detail_dict(issue).get("holistic"):
    82→            continue
    83→
    84→        last_seen = issue.get("last_seen")
    85→        if not last_seen:
    86→            continue
    87→
    88→        try:
    89→            seen_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(last_seen)
    90→        except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
    91→            logger.debug(
    92→                "Skipping holistic issue %s with invalid last_seen %r: %s",
    93→                issue_id,
    94→                last_seen,
    95→                exc,
    96→            )
    97→            continue
    98→
    99→        age_days = (now - seen_dt).days
   100→        if age_days > max_age_days:
   101→            issue["status"] = "auto_resolved"
   102→            issue["resolved_at"] = now.isoformat()
   103→            issue["note"] = "holistic review expired — re-run review to re-evaluate"
   104→            expired.append(issue_id)
   105→
   106→    return expired

   196→def _classify(detectors: set[str], signals: ConcernSignals) -> str:
   197→    """Pick the most specific concern type from what's present."""
   198→    if len(detectors) >= MIN_DETECTORS_FOR_MIXED:
   199→        return "mixed_responsibilities"
   200→    if "dupes" in detectors or "boilerplate_duplication" in detectors:
   201→        return "duplication_design"
   202→    if signals.get("monster_loc", 0) > 0:
   203→        return "structural_complexity"
   204→    if "coupling" in detectors:
   205→        return "coupling_design"
   206→    if signals.get("max_params", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_PARAMS:
   207→        return "interface_design"
   208→    if signals.get("max_nesting", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_NESTING:
   209→        return "structural_complexity"
   210→    if "responsibility_cohesion" in detectors:
   211→        return "mixed_responsibilities"
   212→    return "design_concern"

   215→def _build_summary(
   216→    concern_type: str,

   221→    if concern_type == "mixed_responsibilities":

   276→        summary = f.get("summary", "")
   277→        if summary:
   278→            evidence.append(f"[{f.get('detector', '')}] {summary}")
   279→
   280→    return tuple(evidence)
   281→
   282→
   283→def _build_question(
   284→    detectors: set[str], signals: ConcernSignals
   285→) -> str:
   286→    """Build targeted question from dominant signals."""
   287→    parts: list[str] = []
   288→
   289→    if len(detectors) >= MIN_DETECTORS_FOR_MIXED:
   290→        parts.append(
   291→            f"This file has issues across {len(detectors)} dimensions "
   292→            f"({', '.join(sorted(detectors))}). Is it trying to do too many "
   293→            "things, or is this complexity inherent to its domain?"
   294→        )
   295→
   296→    funcs = signals.get("monster_funcs", [])
   297→    if funcs:
   298→        parts.append(
   299→            f"What are the distinct responsibilities in {funcs[0]}()? "
   300→            "Should it be decomposed into focused functions?"
   301→        )
   302→
   303→    if signals.get("max_params", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_PARAMS:
   304→        parts.append(
   305→            "Should the parameters be grouped into a config/context object? "
   306→            "Which ones belong together?"
   307→        )
   308→
   309→    if signals.get("max_nesting", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_NESTING:
   310→        parts.append(
   311→            "Can the nesting be reduced with early returns, guard clauses, "
   312→            "or extraction into helper functions?"
   313→        )
   314→
   315→    if "dupes" in detectors or "boilerplate_duplication" in detectors:
   316→        parts.append(
   317→            "Is the duplication worth extracting into a shared utility, "
   318→            "or is it intentional variation?"
   319→        )
   320→
   321→    if "coupling" in detectors:
   322→        parts.append(
   323→            "Is the coupling intentional or does it indicate a missing "
   324→            "abstraction boundary?"
   325→        )
   326→
   327→    if "orphaned" in detectors:
   328→        parts.append(
   329→            "Is this file truly dead, or is it used via a non-import mechanism "
   330→            "(dynamic import, CLI entry point, plugin)?"
   331→        )
   332→
   333→    if "responsibility_cohesion" in detectors:
   334→        parts.append(
   335→            "What are the distinct responsibilities? Should this module be "
   336→            "split along those lines?"
   337→        )
   338→
   339→    if not parts:
   340→        parts.append(
   341→            "Review the flagged patterns — are they design problems that "
   342→            "need addressing, or acceptable given the file's role?"
   343→        )
   344→
   345→    return " ".join(parts)
   346→
   347→
   348→# ── Generators ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   349→
   350→
   351→def _file_concerns(state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   352→    """Per-file design concerns from aggregated mechanical signals.
   353→
   354→    Flags a file if it has 2+ judgment-needed detectors OR a single
   355→    detector with elevated signals (monster function, high params,
   356→    deep nesting, duplication, coupling, mixed responsibilities).
   357→    Bundles ALL issues for that file so the LLM sees the full picture.
   358→    """
   359→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   360→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   361→
   362→    for file, all_issues in by_file.items():
   363→        judgment = [
   364→            f for f in all_issues
   365→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   366→        ]
   367→        if not judgment:
   368→            continue
   369→
   370→        judgment_dets = {f.get("detector", "") for f in judgment}
   371→        elevated = _has_elevated_signals(judgment)
   372→
   373→        # Flag if 2+ judgment detectors OR 1 with elevated signals
   374→        # OR 1 judgment detector + 2 mechanical issues from any detector.
   375→        mechanical_count = len(all_issues)
   376→        if len(judgment_dets) < 2 and not elevated:
   377→            if not (len(judgment_dets) >= 1 and mechanical_count >= 3):
   378→                continue
   379→
   380→        signals = _extract_signals(judgment)
   381→        concern_type = _classify(judgment_dets, signals)
   382→        evidence = _build_evidence(judgment, signals)
   383→        question = _build_question(judgment_dets, signals)
   384→        summary = _build_summary(concern_type, judgment_dets, signals)
   385→
   386→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(f.get("id", "") for f in judgment))
   387→        fp_keys = tuple(sorted(judgment_dets))
   388→        fp = _fingerprint(concern_type, file, fp_keys)
   389→
   390→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   391→            continue
   392→
   393→        concerns.append(
   394→            Concern(
   395→                type=concern_type,
   396→                file=file,
   397→                summary=summary,
   398→                evidence=evidence,
   399→                question=question,
   400→                fingerprint=fp,
   401→                source_issues=all_ids,
   402→            )
   403→        )
   404→
   405→    return concerns
   406→
   407→
   408→def _cross_file_patterns(state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   409→    """Systemic patterns: same judgment detector combo across 3+ files.
   410→
   411→    When multiple files share the same combination of detector types,
   412→    that's likely a codebase-wide pattern rather than isolated issues.
   413→    """
   414→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   415→
   416→    # Group files by their judgment detector profile.
   417→    profile_to_files: dict[frozenset[str], list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   418→    for file, issues in by_file.items():
   419→        dets = frozenset(
   420→            f.get("detector", "") for f in issues
   421→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   422→        )
   423→        if len(dets) >= 2:
   424→            profile_to_files[dets].append(file)
   425→
   426→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   427→    for det_combo, files in profile_to_files.items():
   428→        if len(files) < MIN_FILES_FOR_SYSTEMIC:
   429→            continue
   430→
   431→        sorted_files = sorted(files)
   432→        combo_names = tuple(sorted(det_combo))
   433→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(
   434→            f.get("id", "")
   435→            for file in sorted_files
   436→            for f in by_file[file]
   437→            if f.get("detector", "") in det_combo
   438→        ))
   439→        # Use first few files in fingerprint so it's stable but bounded.
   440→        fp = _fingerprint(
   441→            "systemic_pattern",
   442→            ",".join(sorted_files[:5]),
   443→            combo_names,
   444→        )
   445→
   446→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   447→            continue
   448→
   449→        concerns.append(
   450→            Concern(
   451→                type="systemic_pattern",
   452→                file=sorted_files[0],
   453→                summary=(
   454→                    f"{len(files)} files share the same problem pattern "
   455→                    f"({', '.join(combo_names)})"
   456→                ),
   457→                evidence=(
   458→                    f"Affected files: {', '.join(sorted_files[:10])}",
   459→                    f"Shared detectors: {', '.join(combo_names)}",
   460→                    f"Total files: {len(files)}",
   461→                ),
   462→                question=(
   463→                    f"These {len(files)} files all have the same combination "
   464→                    f"of issues ({', '.join(combo_names)}). Is this a systemic "
   465→                    "pattern that should be addressed at the architecture level "
   466→                    "(shared base class, framework change, lint rule), or are "
   467→                    "these independent issues that happen to look similar?"
   468→                ),
   469→                fingerprint=fp,
   470→                source_issues=all_ids,
   471→            )
   472→        )
   473→
   474→    return concerns
   475→
   476→
   477→def _systemic_smell_patterns(
   478→    state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]
   479→) -> list[Concern]:
   480→    """Systemic concerns: single smell_id appearing across 5+ files.
   481→
   482→    Complements _cross_file_patterns which looks at detector-combo profiles.
   483→    This catches pervasive single-smell issues (e.g. broad_except in 12 files).
   484→    """
   485→    smell_files: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   486→    smell_ids_map: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)  # smell_id -> issue IDs
   487→
   488→    for f in _open_issues(state):
   489→        if f.get("detector") != "smells":
   490→            continue
   491→        detail = f.get("detail", {})
   492→        smell_id = detail.get("smell_id", "") if isinstance(detail, dict) else ""
   493→        filepath = f.get("file", "")
   494→        if smell_id and filepath and filepath != ".":
   495→            smell_files[smell_id].append(filepath)
   496→            smell_ids_map[smell_id].append(f.get("id", ""))
   497→
   498→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   499→    for smell_id, files in smell_files.items():
   500→        unique_files = sorted(set(files))
   501→        if len(unique_files) < MIN_FILES_FOR_SMELL_PATTERN:
   502→            continue
   503→
   504→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(smell_ids_map[smell_id]))
   505→        fp = _fingerprint("systemic_smell", smell_id, (smell_id,))
   506→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   507→            continue
   508→
   509→        concerns.append(
   510→            Concern(
   511→                type="systemic_smell",
   512→                file=unique_files[0],
   513→                summary=(
   514→                    f"'{smell_id}' appears in {len(unique_files)} files — "
   515→                    "likely a systemic pattern"
   516→                ),
   517→                evidence=(
   518→                    f"Smell: {smell_id}",
   519→                    f"Affected files ({len(unique_files)}): {', '.join(unique_files[:10])}",
   520→                ),
   521→                question=(
   522→                    f"The smell '{smell_id}' appears across {len(unique_files)} files. "
   523→                    "Is this a codebase-wide convention that should be addressed "
   524→                    "systemically (lint rule, shared utility, architecture change), "
   525→                    "or are these independent occurrences?"
   526→                ),
   527→                fingerprint=fp,
   528→                source_issues=all_ids,
   529→            )
   530→        )
   531→
   532→    return concerns
   533→
   534→
   535→_GENERATORS = [_file_concerns, _cross_file_patterns, _systemic_smell_patterns]
   536→
   537→
   538→def generate_concerns(
   539→    state: StateModel,
   540→) -> list[Concern]:
   541→    """Run all concern generators against current state.
   542→
   543→    Returns deduplicated list sorted by (type, file).
   544→    """
   545→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   546→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   547→    seen_fps: set[str] = set()
   548→
   549→    for gen in _GENERATORS:
   550→        for concern in gen(state, dismissals):
   551→            if concern.fingerprint not in seen_fps:
   552→                seen_fps.add(concern.fingerprint)
   553→                concerns.append(concern)
   554→
   555→    concerns.sort(key=lambda c: (c.type, c.file))
   556→    return concerns
   557→
   558→
   559→def cleanup_stale_dismissals(state: StateModel) -> int:
   560→    """Remove dismissals whose source issues all disappeared.
   561→
   562→    Returns the number of stale entries removed.  Dismissals without
   563→    ``source_issue_ids`` (legacy) are left untouched.
   564→    """
   565→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   566→    if not dismissals:
   567→        return 0
   568→    open_ids = {f.get("id", "") for f in _open_issues(state)}
   569→    stale_fps = [
   570→        fp
   571→        for fp, entry in dismissals.items()
   572→        if entry.get("source_issue_ids")
   573→        and not any(sid in open_ids for sid in entry["source_issue_ids"])
   574→    ]
   575→    for fp in stale_fps:
   576→        del dismissals[fp]
   577→    return len(stale_fps)
   578→
   579→
   580→__all__ = ["Concern", "cleanup_stale_dismissals", "generate_concerns"]
   581→

    21→def detail_dict(item: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    22→    """Return issue detail as a dict; tolerate legacy/non-dict payloads."""
    23→    detail = item.get("detail")
    24→    return detail if isinstance(detail, dict) else {}
    25→
    26→
    27→def status_matches(item_status: str, status_filter: str) -> bool:
    28→    return status_filter == "all" or item_status == status_filter
    29→
    30→
    31→def is_subjective_issue(item: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    32→    detector = item.get("detector")
    33→    if detector in {"subjective_assessment"}:
    34→        return True
    35→    if detector == "holistic_review":
    36→        return True
    37→    return False
    38→
    39→
    40→def is_review_issue(item: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    41→    return item.get("detector") == "review"
    42→
    43→
    44→def is_subjective_queue_item(item: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    45→    """True for subjective work items, including collapsed subjective clusters."""
    46→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
    47→        return True
    48→    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
    49→        members = item.get("members", [])
    50→        return bool(members) and all(
    51→            m.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension" for m in members
    52→        )
    53→    return False
    54→
    55→
    56→def review_issue_weight(item: dict[str, Any]) -> float:
    57→    """Return review issue weight aligned with issues list ordering."""
    58→    confidence = str(item.get("confidence", "low")).lower()
    59→    weight_by_confidence = {
    60→        "high": 1.0,
    61→        "medium": 0.7,
    62→        "low": 0.3,
    63→    }
    64→    weight = weight_by_confidence.get(confidence, 0.3)
    65→    if detail_dict(item).get("holistic"):
    66→        weight *= 10.0
    67→    return float(weight)
    68→
    69→
    70→def scope_matches(item: dict[str, Any], scope: str | None) -> bool:
    71→    """Apply show-style pattern matching against a queue item."""
    72→    if not scope:
    73→        return True
    74→
    75→    item_id = item.get("id", "")
    76→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
    77→    filepath = item.get("file", "")
    78→    summary = item.get("summary", "")
    79→    dimension = detail_dict(item).get("dimension_name", "")
    80→    kind = item.get("kind", "")
    81→
    82→    if "*" in scope:
    83→        return any(
    84→            fnmatch(candidate, scope)
    85→            for candidate in (item_id, filepath, detector, dimension, summary)
    86→        )
    87→
    88→    if "::" in scope:
    89→        return item_id.startswith(scope)
    90→
    91→    lowered = scope.lower()
    92→    if kind == "subjective_dimension":

    94→            lowered in item_id.lower()
    95→            or lowered in dimension.lower()
    96→            or lowered in summary.lower()
    97→        )
    98→
    99→    # Hash suffix: 8+ hex chars matches the tail segment of a issue ID.
   100→    if len(lowered) >= 8 and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]+", lowered):
   101→        return item_id.lower().endswith("::" + lowered)
   102→
   103→    return (
   104→        detector == scope
   105→        or filepath == scope
   106→        or filepath.startswith(scope.rstrip("/") + "/")
   107→    )

   114→def supported_fixers_for_item(
   115→    state: StateModel, item: dict[str, Any]
   116→) -> set[str] | None:
   117→    """Return supported fixers for an item's language when known."""
   118→    lang = str(item.get("lang", "") or "").strip()
   119→    if not lang:
   120→        return None
   121→
   122→    caps = state.get("lang_capabilities", {})
   123→    if not isinstance(caps, dict):
   124→        return None
   125→
   126→    lang_caps = caps.get(lang, {})
   127→    if not isinstance(lang_caps, dict):
   128→        return None
   129→
   130→    fixers = lang_caps.get("fixers")
   131→    if not isinstance(fixers, list):
   132→        return None
   133→    return {fixer for fixer in fixers if isinstance(fixer, str)}

   136→def primary_command_for_issue(
   137→    item: dict[str, Any], *, supported_fixers: set[str] | None = None
   138→) -> str:
   139→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
   140→    meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   141→    if meta and meta.action_type == "auto_fix" and meta.fixers:
   142→        available_fixers = [
   143→            fixer
   144→            for fixer in meta.fixers
   145→            if supported_fixers is not None and fixer in supported_fixers
   146→        ]
   147→        if available_fixers:
   148→            return f"desloppify autofix {available_fixers[0]} --dry-run"
   149→    if detector == "subjective_review":
   150→        from desloppify.intelligence.integrity import (

   152→        )
   153→

   155→            return "desloppify review --prepare"
   156→        return "desloppify show subjective"
   157→    return f'desloppify plan resolve "{item.get("id", "")}" --note "<what you did>" --confirm'

    54→    dim_scores: dict,
    55→    *,
    56→    threshold: float = 95.0,
    57→) -> list[tuple[str, float, int]]:
    58→    """Return assessed scorecard-subjective entries below the threshold."""
    59→    low: list[tuple[str, float, int]] = []
    60→    for entry in _scorecard_subjective(state, dim_scores):
    61→        if entry.get("placeholder"):
    62→            continue
    63→        strict_val = float(entry.get("strict", entry.get("score", 100.0)))
    64→        if strict_val < threshold:
    65→            low.append(
    66→                (
    67→                    str(entry.get("name", "Subjective")),
    68→                    strict_val,
    69→                    int(entry.get("failing", 0)),
    70→                )
    71→            )
    72→    low.sort(key=lambda item: item[1])
    73→    return low
    74→
    75→
    76→def cmd_next(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    77→    """Show next highest-priority queue items."""
    78→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
    79→    state = runtime.state
    80→    config = runtime.config
    81→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
    82→        return
    83→
    84→    skill_warning = check_skill_version()
    85→    if skill_warning:
    86→        print(colorize(f"  {skill_warning}", "yellow"))
    87→    config_warning = check_config_staleness(config)
    88→    if config_warning:
    89→        print(colorize(f"  {config_warning}", "yellow"))
    90→
    91→    print_triage_guardrail_info(state=state)
    92→    _get_items(args, state, config)
    93→
    94→
    95→def _resolve_cluster_focus(
    96→    plan_data: dict | None,
    97→    *,
    98→    cluster_arg: str | None,
    99→    scope: str | None,
   100→) -> str | None:
   101→    effective_cluster = cluster_arg
   102→    if plan_data and not cluster_arg and not scope:
   103→        active_cluster = plan_data.get("active_cluster")
   104→        if active_cluster:
   105→            effective_cluster = active_cluster
   106→    return effective_cluster
   107→
   108→
   109→def _build_next_payload(
   110→    *,
   111→    queue: dict,
   112→    items: list[dict],
   113→    state: dict,
   114→    narrative: dict,
   115→    plan_data: dict | None,
   116→) -> dict:
   117→    payload = next_output_mod.build_query_payload(
   118→        queue, items, command="next", narrative=narrative, plan=plan_data
   119→    )
   120→    scores = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
   121→    payload["overall_score"] = scores.overall
   122→    payload["objective_score"] = scores.objective
   123→    payload["strict_score"] = scores.strict
   124→    payload["scorecard_dimensions"] = scorecard_dimensions_payload(
   125→        state,
   126→        dim_scores=state.get("dimension_scores", {}),
   127→    )
   128→    payload["subjective_measures"] = [
   129→        row for row in payload["scorecard_dimensions"] if row.get("subjective")
   130→    ]
   131→    return payload
   132→
   133→
   134→def _emit_requested_output(
   135→    args,
   136→    payload: dict,
   137→    items: list[dict],
   138→) -> bool:
   139→    output_file = getattr(args, "output", None)
   140→    if output_file:
   141→        if next_output_mod.write_output_file(
   142→            output_file,
   143→            payload,
   144→            len(items),
   145→            safe_write_text_fn=safe_write_text,
   146→            colorize_fn=colorize,
   147→        ):
   148→            return True
   149→        raise SystemExit(1)
   150→
   151→    output_format = getattr(args, "format", "terminal")
   152→    if next_output_mod.emit_non_terminal_output(output_format, payload, items):
   153→        return True
   154→    return False
   155→
   156→
   157→def _plan_queue_context(
   158→    *,
   159→    state: dict,
   160→    plan_data: dict | None,
   161→    context=None,
   162→) -> tuple[float | None, QueueBreakdown | None]:
   163→    effective_plan = context.plan if context is not None else plan_data
   164→    plan_start_strict = get_plan_start_strict(effective_plan)
   165→    try:
   166→        breakdown = plan_aware_queue_breakdown(state, plan_data, context=context)
   167→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   168→        breakdown = None
   169→    return plan_start_strict, breakdown
   170→
   171→
   172→def _merge_potentials_safe(raw_potentials: dict | None) -> dict | None:
   173→    try:
   174→        return merge_potentials(raw_potentials) or None
   175→    except (ImportError, TypeError, ValueError):
   176→        return raw_potentials or None
   177→
   178→
   179→def _get_items(args, state: dict, config: dict) -> None:
   180→    count = getattr(args, "count", 1) or 1
   181→    scope = getattr(args, "scope", None)
   182→    status = getattr(args, "status", "open")
   183→    group = getattr(args, "group", "item")
   184→    explain = bool(getattr(args, "explain", False))
   185→    cluster_arg = getattr(args, "cluster", None)
   186→    include_skipped = bool(getattr(args, "include_skipped", False))
   187→
   188→    target_strict = target_strict_score_from_config(config, fallback=95.0)
   189→
   190→    # Load the living plan
   191→    plan = load_plan()
   192→    plan_data: dict | None = None
   193→    if (
   194→        plan.get("queue_order")
   195→        or plan.get("overrides")
   196→        or plan.get("clusters")
   197→    ):
   198→        plan_data = plan
   199→
   200→    # Build unified context once — all downstream consumers agree on
   201→    # plan, target_strict, and subjective visibility policy.
   202→    ctx = queue_context(
   203→        state, config=config, plan=plan_data, target_strict=target_strict,
   204→    )
   205→
   206→    # Auto-scope to focus cluster if set and no explicit scope/cluster
   207→    effective_cluster = _resolve_cluster_focus(
   208→        plan_data,
   209→        cluster_arg=cluster_arg,
   210→        scope=scope,
   211→    )
   212→
   213→    queue = build_work_queue(
   214→        state,
   215→        options=QueueBuildOptions(
   216→            count=count,
   217→            scope=scope,
   218→            status=status,
   219→            include_subjective=True,
   220→            subjective_threshold=target_strict,
   221→            explain=explain,
   222→            include_skipped=include_skipped,
   223→            cluster=effective_cluster,
   224→            context=ctx,
   225→        ),
   226→    )
   227→    items = queue.get("items", [])
   228→
   229→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
   230→    lang_name = lang.name if lang else None
   231→    narrative = compute_narrative(
   232→        state,
   233→        context=NarrativeContext(lang=lang_name, command="next", plan=plan_data),
   234→    )
   235→
   236→    payload = _build_next_payload(
   237→        queue=queue,
   238→        items=items,
   239→        state=state,
   240→        narrative=narrative,
   241→        plan_data=plan_data,
   242→    )
   243→    write_query(payload)
   244→
   245→    if _emit_requested_output(args, payload, items):
   246→        return
   247→
   248→    dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {})
   249→    issues_scoped = state_mod.path_scoped_issues(
   250→        state.get("issues", {}),
   251→        state.get("scan_path"),
   252→    )
   253→
   254→    # Extract frozen plan-start score and queue breakdown for lifecycle display
   255→    plan_start_strict, breakdown = _plan_queue_context(
   256→        state=state,
   257→        plan_data=plan_data,
   258→        context=ctx,
   259→    )
   260→    queue_total = breakdown.queue_total if breakdown else 0
   261→
   262→    _render_queue_header(queue, explain)
   263→    strict_score = state_mod.score_snapshot(state).strict
   264→    if _show_empty_queue(
   265→        queue,
   266→        strict_score,
   267→        plan_start_strict=plan_start_strict,
   268→        target_strict=target_strict,
   269→    ):
   270→        return
   271→
   272→    raw_potentials = state.get("potentials", {})
   273→    potentials = _merge_potentials_safe(raw_potentials)
   274→    next_render_mod.render_terminal_items(
   275→        items, dim_scores, issues_scoped, group=group, explain=explain,
   276→        potentials=potentials, plan=plan_data,
   277→        cluster_filter=effective_cluster,
   278→    )
   279→    next_nudges_mod.render_single_item_resolution_hint(items)
   280→    next_nudges_mod.render_uncommitted_reminder(plan_data)
   281→    next_nudges_mod.render_followup_nudges(

def _expire_provisional_manual_override_assessments(
    state: state_mod.StateModel,
) -> int:
    """Expire provisional manual-override assessments at scan start."""
    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)

    now = state_mod.utc_now()
    expired = 0
    for payload in assessments.values():
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            continue
        if payload.get("provisional_override") is not True:
            continue

    10→def fix_empty_if_chain(
    11→    entries: list[dict[str, Any]],
    12→    *,
    13→    dry_run: bool = False,
    14→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    15→    """Delete if/else chains where all branches are empty."""
    16→
    17→    def transform(
    18→        lines: list[str],
    19→        file_entries: list[dict[str, Any]],
    20→    ) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    21→        lines_to_remove: set[int] = set()
    22→
    23→        for e in file_entries:
    24→            line_idx = e["line"] - 1
    25→            if line_idx < 0 or line_idx >= len(lines):
    26→                continue
    27→
    28→            end = _find_if_chain_end(lines, line_idx)
    29→            for idx in range(line_idx, end + 1):
    30→                lines_to_remove.add(idx)
    31→
    32→        new_lines = collapse_blank_lines(lines, lines_to_remove)
    33→        return new_lines, ["empty_if_chain"]
    34→
    35→    return apply_fixer(entries, transform, dry_run=dry_run)
    36→
    37→
    38→def _find_if_chain_end(lines: list[str], start: int) -> int:
    39→    """Find the last line of an if/else chain starting at `start`.
    40→
    41→    Tracks brace depth. Chain ends when braces balance and no else follows.
    42→    """
    43→    brace_depth = 0
    44→    found_brace = False
    45→
    46→    for i in range(start, min(start + 100, len(lines))):
    47→        line = lines[i]
    48→        for ci, ch, in_s in scan_code(line):
    49→            if in_s:
    50→                continue
    51→            if ch == "{":
    52→                brace_depth += 1
    53→                found_brace = True
    54→            elif ch == "}":
    55→                brace_depth -= 1
    56→                if found_brace and brace_depth == 0:
    57→                    rest = line[ci + 1 :].strip()
    58→                    if rest.startswith("else"):
    59→                        break
    60→                    j = i + 1
    61→                    while j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip() == "":
    62→                        j += 1
    63→                    if j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip().startswith("else"):
    64→                        break
    65→                    return i
    66→
    67→    return start
    68→

1→"""Unused params fixer: prefixes unused function/callback params with _."""
     2→
     3→import re
     4→
     5→from desloppify.languages.typescript.fixers.fixer_io import apply_fixer
     6→
     7→
     8→def fix_unused_params(entries: list[dict], *, dry_run: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
     9→    """Prefix unused function/callback/catch parameters with _ to signal intentional non-use."""
    10→
    11→    def _transform(lines: list[str], file_entries: list[dict]):
    12→        removed_names: list[str] = []
    13→        for entry in file_entries:
    14→            removed_name = _rewrite_unused_param(lines, entry)
    15→            if removed_name:
    16→                removed_names.append(removed_name)
    17→        return lines, removed_names
    18→
    19→    return apply_fixer(entries, _transform, dry_run=dry_run)
    20→
    21→
    22→def _rewrite_unused_param(lines: list[str], entry: dict) -> str | None:
    23→    """Rewrite one unused param entry in-place and return renamed symbol."""
    24→    name = entry["name"]
    25→    if name.startswith("_"):
    26→        return None
    27→
    28→    line_idx = entry["line"] - 1
    29→    if line_idx < 0 or line_idx >= len(lines):
    30→        return None
    31→
    32→    src = lines[line_idx]
    33→    if not _line_is_param_context(src, lines, line_idx):
    34→        return None
    35→
    36→    if _rewrite_with_column_hint(lines, line_idx, src, name, entry.get("col", 0)):
    37→        return name
    38→
    39→    new_name = f"_{name}"
    40→    param_re = re.compile(r"(?<=[\(,\s])" + re.escape(name) + r"(?=\s*[?:,)=])")
    41→    new_line = param_re.sub(new_name, src, count=1)
    42→    if new_line == src:
    43→        return None
    44→    lines[line_idx] = new_line
    45→    return name
    46→
    47→
    48→def _line_is_param_context(src: str, lines: list[str], line_idx: int) -> bool:
    49→    stripped = src.strip()
    50→    return bool(
    51→        re.search(r"(?:function\s+\w+|function)\s*\(", stripped)
    52→        or re.search(r"\)\s*(?:=>|:)", stripped)
    53→        or re.search(r"=>\s*\{", stripped)
    54→        or re.match(r"\s*\(", stripped)
    55→        or re.search(r"catch\s*\(", stripped)
    56→        or _is_param_context(lines, line_idx)
    57→    )
    58→
    59→
    60→def _rewrite_with_column_hint(
    61→    lines: list[str], line_idx: int, src: str, name: str, col: int

**Current Structure Analysis:**

The function *does indeed* handle four independent display concerns that could be cleanly separated:

1. **Score Quartet Display (lines 206–222):** Prints the four-score comparison with deltas (overall, objective, strict, verified) in colored output
2. **Wontfix Gap Warning (lines 225–235):** Conditionally prints a yellow warning when there's a significant gap between overall and strict scores
3. **Score Legend Guide (lines 237–240):** Shows the explanation of what each score type means, triggered on first scan or when gap is significant
4. **Integrity Warnings (lines 246–248):** Displays subjective integrity warnings (penalized/warn status with streak tracking)

- Score reveal logic (lines 203–204): Delegates to `_show_score_reveal()` which handles special queue-cycle-complete scenarios
- Non-comparable reason display (lines 223–224)
- Strict target progress nudge (lines 242–244)

**Verdict:** YES, this function could reasonably be split into ~4–5 focused functions:
- `_print_score_quartet()` — just the four scores with colors and deltas
- `_print_wontfix_gap_warning()` — gap detection and warning
- `_print_score_legend()` — the guide text (already has `_print_score_guide()` helper!)
- `_print_integrity_status()` — subjective integrity warnings (already has `_print_subjective_integrity_warning()` helper!)

**Current Code Quality:** The function is already well-organized with helper functions (`_show_score_reveal()`, `_print_score_guide()`, `_print_subjective_integrity_warning()`) handling internal concerns. The main function body could be further refactored to call more granular helpers.

    47→    _print_fix_summary(fixer, results, total_items, total_lines, dry_run)
    48→
    49→    if dry_run and results:
    50→        show_fix_dry_run_samples(entries, results)
    51→
    52→    if not dry_run:
    53→        _apply_and_report(
    54→            args,
    55→            path,

    57→            fixer_name,
    58→            entries,
    59→            results,
    60→            total_items,
    61→            lang,
    62→            skip_reasons,
    63→        )
    64→    else:
    65→        _report_dry_run(args, fixer_name, entries, results, total_items)
    66→    print()

   299→        if expected is str:

   301→
   302→        if expected is list:

   318→    def normalize_runtime_options(

   324→        values = values if isinstance(values, dict) else {}
   325→        specs = self.runtime_option_specs
   326→        if strict:
   327→            unknown = sorted(set(values) - set(specs))
   328→            if unknown:
   329→                raise KeyError(

   332→        normalized: dict[str, object] = {}
   333→        for key, spec in specs.items():
   334→            raw = values.get(key, spec.default)
   335→            normalized[key] = self._coerce_value(raw, spec.type, spec.default)

    22→def _consecutive_subjective_integrity_status(
    23→    state: StateModel, status: str
    24→) -> int:
    25→    """Return consecutive trailing scans with the given subjective-integrity status."""
    26→    history = state.get("scan_history", [])
    27→    if not isinstance(history, list):
    28→        return 0
    29→
    30→    streak = 0
    31→    for entry in reversed(history):
    32→        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
    33→            break
    34→        integrity = entry.get("subjective_integrity")
    35→        if not isinstance(integrity, dict):
    36→            break
    37→        if integrity.get("status") != status:
    38→            break
    39→        streak += 1
    40→    return streak
    41→
    42→
    43→def _show_score_reveal(
    44→    state: StateModel,
    45→    new: state_mod.ScoreSnapshot,
    46→    *,
    47→    target_strict: float | None = None,
    48→) -> None:
    49→    """Show before/after score comparison when a queue cycle just completed.
    50→
    51→    This fires when the plan had ``plan_start_scores`` and the queue was empty
    52→    at scan time (i.e. the reconcile block cleared plan_start_scores).  We detect
    53→    this by checking the plan *before* the clear happened — since merge_scan_results
    54→    clears it, we peek at the ``_last_score_reveal`` stash it leaves behind.
    55→    """
    56→    # scan_workflow stashes the old plan_start_scores on state as a transient
    57→    # key when it clears them (queue empty).  Pop it here for the reveal.
    58→    plan_start = state.pop("_plan_start_scores_for_reveal", None)
    59→    if not isinstance(plan_start, dict) or not plan_start.get("strict"):
    60→        return
    61→
    62→    old_strict = float(plan_start["strict"])
    63→    new_strict = float(new.strict or 0)
    64→    delta = round(new_strict - old_strict, 1)
    65→    delta_str = f" ({'+' if delta > 0 else ''}{delta:.1f})" if abs(delta) >= 0.05 else ""
    66→
    67→    bar = "=" * 50
    68→    print(colorize(f"  {bar}", "cyan"))
    69→    print(colorize("  SCORE UPDATE — Queue cycle complete!", "bold"))
    70→    print(colorize(f"  Plan-start: strict {old_strict:.1f}/100", "dim"))
    71→    print(colorize(f"  Updated:    strict {new_strict:.1f}/100{delta_str}", "cyan"))
    72→    if target_strict is not None:
    73→        target_gap = round(target_strict - new_strict, 1)
    74→        if target_gap > 0:
    75→            print(colorize(f"  Target:     {target_strict:.1f} (+{target_gap:.1f} to go)", "dim"))
    76→        else:
    77→            print(colorize(f"  Target:     {target_strict:.1f} — reached!", "green"))
    78→    print(colorize(f"  {bar}", "cyan"))
    79→

    81→def show_diff_summary(diff: dict[str, Any]) -> None:

    83→    diff_parts = []
    84→    if diff["new"]:
    85→        diff_parts.append(colorize(f"+{diff['new']} new", "yellow"))
    86→    if diff["auto_resolved"]:
    87→        diff_parts.append(colorize(f"-{diff['auto_resolved']} resolved", "green"))
    88→    if diff["reopened"]:

    90→    if diff_parts:

    92→    else:

   146→        if streak < 2:

   148→        print(
   149→            colorize(
   150→                "    Repeated penalty across scans. Use a blind, isolated reviewer "
   151→                "on `.desloppify/review_packet_blind.json` and re-import before trusting subjective scores.",
   152→                "yellow",
   153→            )
   154→        )
   155→        return
   156→
   157→    if status != "warn":
   158→        return
   159→    print(
   160→        colorize(
   161→            "  ⚠ Subjective integrity: "
   162→            f"{matched_count} dimension matched the target "
   163→            f"({target_label}). Re-review recommended.",
   164→            "yellow",
   165→        )
   166→    )
   167→    streak = _consecutive_subjective_integrity_status(state, "warn")
   168→    if streak < 2:
   169→        return
   170→    print(
   171→        colorize(
   172→            "    This warning has repeated. Prefer "
   173→            "`desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import` "
   174→            "or run a blind reviewer pass before import.",
   175→            "yellow",
   176→        )
   177→    )
   178→
   179→
   180→def show_score_delta(
   181→    state: StateModel,
   182→    prev_overall: float | None,
   183→    prev_objective: float | None,
   184→    prev_strict: float | None,
   185→    prev_verified: float | None = None,
   186→    non_comparable_reason: str | None = None,
   187→    *,
   188→    target_strict: float | None = None,
   189→) -> None:
   190→    """Print the canonical score quartet with deltas."""
   191→    stats = state["stats"]
   192→    new = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
   193→
   194→    if not _has_complete_scores(new):
   195→        print(
   196→            colorize(
   197→                "  Scores unavailable — run a full scan with language detectors enabled.",
   198→                "yellow",
   199→            )
   200→        )
   201→        return
   202→
   203→    # Detect score-reveal scan: plan_start_scores existed and queue was clear
   204→    _show_score_reveal(state, new, target_strict=target_strict)
   205→
   206→    overall_delta_str, overall_color = format_delta(new.overall, prev_overall)
   207→    objective_delta_str, objective_color = format_delta(new.objective, prev_objective)
   208→    strict_delta_str, strict_color = format_delta(new.strict, prev_strict)
   209→    verified_delta_str, verified_color = format_delta(new.verified, prev_verified)
   210→    print(
   211→        "  Scores: "
   212→        + colorize(f"overall {new.overall:.1f}/100{overall_delta_str}", overall_color)
   213→        + colorize(
   214→            f"  objective {new.objective:.1f}/100{objective_delta_str}",
   215→            objective_color,
   216→        )
   217→        + colorize(f"  strict {new.strict:.1f}/100{strict_delta_str}", strict_color)
   218→        + colorize(
   219→            f"  verified {new.verified:.1f}/100{verified_delta_str}",
   220→            verified_color,
   221→        )
   222→    )
   223→    if isinstance(non_comparable_reason, str) and non_comparable_reason.strip():
   224→        print(colorize(f"  Δ non-comparable: {non_comparable_reason.strip()}", "yellow"))
   225→    # Surface wontfix debt gap prominently when significant
   226→    wontfix = stats.get("wontfix", 0)
   227→    gap = (new.overall or 0) - (new.strict or 0)
   228→    if gap >= 5 and wontfix >= 10:
   229→        print(
   230→            colorize(
   231→                f"  ⚠ {gap:.1f}-point gap between overall and strict — "
   232→                f"{wontfix} wontfix items represent hidden debt",
   233→                "yellow",
   234→            )
   235→        )
   236→
   237→    # Score legend — shown on first scan or when strict gap is significant
   238→    scan_count = state.get("scan_count", 0)
   239→    if scan_count <= 1 or gap > 10 or is_agent_environment():
   240→        _print_score_guide()
   241→
   242→    # Show strict target progress
   243→    if target_strict is not None and new.strict is not None:
   244→        print_strict_target_nudge(new.strict, target_strict, show_next=False)
   245→
   246→    integrity = state.get("subjective_integrity", {})
   247→    if isinstance(integrity, dict):
   248→        _print_subjective_integrity_warning(state, integrity)
   249→

   251→def show_concern_count(state: StateModel, lang_name: str | None = None) -> None:
   252→    """Print concern count if any exist."""
   253→    try:
   254→        concerns = generate_concerns(state)
   255→        if concerns:
   256→            print(
   257→                colorize(
   258→                    f"  {len(concerns)} potential design concern{'s' if len(concerns) != 1 else ''}"
   259→                    " (run `show concerns` to view)",
   260→                    "cyan",
   261→                )
   262→            )
   263→    except (ImportError, AttributeError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
   264→        logger.debug("Concern generation failed (best-effort): %s", exc)
   265→
   266→
   267→def show_strict_target_progress(
   268→    strict_target: dict[str, Any] | None,
   269→) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
   270→    """Print strict target progress lines and return (target, gap)."""
   271→    lines, target, gap = format_strict_target_progress(strict_target)
   272→    for message, style in lines:
   273→        print(colorize(message, style))
   274→    return target, gap
   275→

   203→def _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   204→    state: state_mod.StateModel,

   206→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   207→) -> int:
   208→    """Reset known subjective dimensions to 0 so the next scan starts fresh."""

   211→    reset_keys = {

   215→    }
   216→    reset_keys.update(_subjective_reset_dimensions(lang_name=lang_name))
   217→
   218→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   219→    for key in sorted(reset_keys):
   220→        payload = assessments.get(key)
   221→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
   222→            payload["score"] = 0.0
   223→            payload["source"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   224→            payload["assessed_at"] = now
   225→            payload["reset_by"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   226→            payload["placeholder"] = True
   227→            payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   228→            payload.pop("components", None)
   229→            payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   230→            continue
   231→        assessments[key] = {
   232→            "score": 0.0,
   233→            "source": "scan_reset_subjective",
   234→            "assessed_at": now,
   235→            "reset_by": "scan_reset_subjective",
   236→            "placeholder": True,

   245→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   246→
   247→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   248→    expired = 0
   249→    for payload in assessments.values():

   252→        if payload.get("provisional_override") is not True:

   254→        payload["score"] = 0.0

   261→        payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   262→        payload.pop("components", None)
   263→        payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   264→        expired += 1

   313→def _augment_with_stale_exclusion_issues(
   314→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   315→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   316→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   317→    """Append stale exclude issues when excluded dirs are unreferenced."""
   318→    extra_exclusions = get_exclusions()
   319→    if not (extra_exclusions and runtime.lang and runtime.lang.file_finder):
   320→        return issues
   321→
   322→    scanned_files = runtime.lang.file_finder(runtime.path)
   323→    stale = _audit_excluded_dirs(
   324→        extra_exclusions, scanned_files, get_project_root()
   325→    )
   326→    if not stale:
   327→        return issues
   328→
   329→    augmented = list(issues)
   330→    augmented.extend(stale)
   331→    for stale_issue in stale:
   332→        print(colorize(f"  ℹ {stale_issue['summary']}", "dim"))
   333→    return augmented

   352→def run_scan_generation(
   353→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   354→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, object], dict[str, object] | None]:
   355→    """Run detector pipeline and return issues, potentials, and codebase metrics."""
   356→    enable_file_cache()
   357→    enable_parse_cache()
   358→    try:
   359→        issues, potentials = plan_mod.generate_issues(
   360→            runtime.path,
   361→            lang=runtime.lang,
   362→            options=PlanScanOptions(
   363→                include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   364→                zone_overrides=runtime.zone_overrides,
   365→                profile=runtime.profile,
   366→            ),
   367→        )
   368→    finally:
   369→        disable_parse_cache()
   370→        disable_file_cache()
   371→
   372→    codebase_metrics = _collect_codebase_metrics(runtime.lang, runtime.path)
   373→    _warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files(
   374→        runtime.args, runtime.lang, runtime.path, codebase_metrics
   375→    )
   376→    issues = _augment_with_stale_exclusion_issues(issues, runtime)
   377→    decay_scans = _coerce_int(
   378→        runtime.config.get("wontfix_decay_scans"),
   379→        default=_WONTFIX_DECAY_SCANS_DEFAULT,
   380→    )
   381→    issues, monitored_wontfix = _augment_with_stale_wontfix_issues(
   382→        issues,
   383→        runtime,
   384→        decay_scans=max(decay_scans, 0),
   385→    )
   386→    potentials["stale_wontfix"] = monitored_wontfix
   387→    return issues, potentials, codebase_metrics

   390→def merge_scan_results(
   391→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   392→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   393→    potentials: dict[str, object],
   394→    codebase_metrics: dict[str, object] | None,
   395→) -> ScanMergeResult:
   396→    """Merge issues into persistent state and return diff + previous score snapshot."""
   397→    scan_path_rel = rel(str(runtime.path))
   398→    prev_scan_path = runtime.state.get("scan_path")
   399→    path_changed = prev_scan_path is not None and prev_scan_path != scan_path_rel
   400→
   401→    if not path_changed:
   402→        prev = state_mod.score_snapshot(runtime.state)
   403→    else:
   404→        prev = state_mod.ScoreSnapshot(None, None, None, None)
   405→    prev_dim_scores = (
   406→        runtime.state.get("dimension_scores", {}) if not path_changed else {}
   407→    )
   408→
   409→    if runtime.lang and runtime.lang.zone_map is not None:
   410→        runtime.state["zone_distribution"] = runtime.lang.zone_map.counts()
   411→    _persist_scan_coverage(runtime.state, runtime.lang)
   412→
   413→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   414→
   415→    diff = state_mod.merge_scan(
   416→        runtime.state,
   417→        issues,
   418→        options=state_mod.MergeScanOptions(
   419→            lang=runtime.lang.name if runtime.lang else None,
   420→            scan_path=scan_path_rel,
   421→            force_resolve=getattr(runtime.args, "force_resolve", False),
   422→            exclude=get_exclusions(),
   423→            potentials=potentials,
   424→            codebase_metrics=codebase_metrics,
   425→            include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   426→            ignore=runtime.config.get("ignore", []),

   440→    _clear_needs_rescan_flag(runtime.config)

   443→    return ScanMergeResult(

   453→def resolve_noise_snapshot(

   458→    noise_budget, global_noise_budget, budget_warning = (

   362→    try:

   373→    state_data = _load_state_file_payload(path)
   374→    if state_data is None:
   375→        return False
   376→    old_config = state_data.get("config")
   377→    if not isinstance(old_config, dict) or not old_config:
   378→        return False
   379→
   380→    _merge_legacy_state_config(config, old_config)
   381→    _strip_config_from_state_file(path, state_data)

   385→def _migrate_from_state_files(config_path: Path) -> dict:
   386→    """Migrate config keys from state-*.json files into config.json.
   387→
   388→    Reads state["config"] from all state files, merges them (union for
   389→    lists, merge for dicts), writes config.json, and strips "config" from
   390→    the state files.
   391→    """
   392→    config: dict = {}
   393→    state_dir = config_path.parent
   394→    if not state_dir.exists():
   395→        return config
   396→
   397→    state_files = list(state_dir.glob("state-*.json")) + list(
   398→        state_dir.glob("state.json")
   399→    )
   400→    migrated_any = False
   401→    for sf in state_files:
   402→        migrated_any = _migrate_single_state_file(config, sf) or migrated_any
   403→
   404→    if migrated_any and config:
   405→        try:
   406→            save_config(config, config_path)
   407→        except OSError as exc:
   408→            log_best_effort_failure(
   409→                logger, f"save migrated config to {config_path}", exc
   410→            )
   411→
   412→    return config

   415→# ── Target score helpers ─────────────────────────────────────
   416→
   417→
   418→def coerce_target_score(value: object, *, fallback: float = 95.0) -> float:
   419→    """Normalize target score-like values to a safe [0, 100] float."""
   420→    if is_numeric(fallback):
   421→        fallback_value = float(fallback)
   422→    else:
   423→        fallback_value = 95.0
   424→
   425→    if is_numeric(value):
   426→        parsed = float(value)
   427→    elif isinstance(value, str):
   428→        text = value.strip()
   429→        if not text:
   430→            parsed = fallback_value
   431→        else:
   432→            try:
   433→                parsed = float(text)
   434→            except ValueError:
   435→                parsed = fallback_value
   436→    else:
   437→        parsed = fallback_value
   438→    return max(0.0, min(100.0, parsed))
   439→
   440→
   441→def target_strict_score_from_config(
   442→    config: dict | None, *, fallback: float = 95.0
   443→) -> float:
   444→    """Read and normalize target strict score from config."""
   445→    if isinstance(config, dict):
   446→        raw = config.get("target_strict_score", fallback)
   447→    else:
   448→        raw = fallback
   449→    return coerce_target_score(raw, fallback=fallback)
