   171→def _configure_lang_runtime(
   172→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   173→    config: dict[str, object],
   174→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   175→    lang: LangRun | None,
   176→) -> LangRun | None:
   177→    """Populate runtime context and threshold overrides for a selected language."""
   178→    if not lang:
   179→        return None
   180→
   181→    lang_options = resolve_lang_runtime_options(args, lang)
   182→    lang_settings = resolve_lang_settings(config, lang)
   183→    runtime_lang = make_lang_run(
   184→        lang,
   185→        overrides=LangRunOverrides(
   186→            review_cache=state.get("review_cache", {}),
   187→            review_max_age_days=config.get("review_max_age_days", 30),
   188→            runtime_settings=lang_settings,
   189→            runtime_options=lang_options,
   190→            large_threshold_override=config.get("large_files_threshold", 0),
   191→            props_threshold_override=config.get("props_threshold", 0),
   192→        ),
   193→    )
   194→
   195→    lang_capabilities = _state_lang_capabilities(state)
   196→    lang_capabilities[runtime_lang.name] = {
   197→        "fixers": sorted(runtime_lang.fixers.keys()),
   198→        "typecheck_cmd": runtime_lang.typecheck_cmd,
   199→    }
   200→    return runtime_lang
   201→
   202→
   203→def _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   204→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   205→    *,
   206→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   207→) -> int:
   208→    """Reset known subjective dimensions to 0 so the next scan starts fresh."""
   209→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   210→
   211→    reset_keys = {
   212→        key.strip()
   213→        for key in assessments
   214→        if isinstance(key, str) and key.strip()
   215→    }
   216→    reset_keys.update(_subjective_reset_dimensions(lang_name=lang_name))
   217→
   218→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   219→    for key in sorted(reset_keys):
   220→        payload = assessments.get(key)
   221→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
   222→            payload["score"] = 0.0
   223→            payload["source"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   224→            payload["assessed_at"] = now
   225→            payload["reset_by"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   226→            payload["placeholder"] = True
   227→            payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   228→            payload.pop("components", None)
   229→            payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   230→            continue
   231→        assessments[key] = {
   232→            "score": 0.0,
   233→            "source": "scan_reset_subjective",
   234→            "assessed_at": now,
   235→            "reset_by": "scan_reset_subjective",
   236→            "placeholder": True,
   237→        }
   238→    return len(reset_keys)
   239→
   240→
   241→def _expire_provisional_manual_override_assessments(
   242→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   243→) -> int:
   244→    """Expire provisional manual-override assessments at scan start."""
   245→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   246→
   247→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   248→    expired = 0
   249→    for payload in assessments.values():
   250→        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
   251→            continue
   252→        if payload.get("provisional_override") is not True:
   253→            continue
   254→        payload["score"] = 0.0
   255→        payload["source"] = "manual_override_expired"
   256→        payload["assessed_at"] = now
   257→        payload["reset_by"] = "manual_override_expired"
   258→        payload["placeholder"] = True
   259→        payload.pop("provisional_override", None)
   260→        payload.pop("provisional_until_scan", None)
   261→        payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   262→        payload.pop("components", None)
   263→        payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   264→        expired += 1
   265→    return expired
   266→
   267→
   268→def prepare_scan_runtime(args) -> ScanRuntime:
   269→    """Resolve state/config/language and apply scan-time runtime settings."""
   270→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   271→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   272→    state = runtime.state if isinstance(runtime.state, dict) else {}
   273→    state_mod.ensure_state_defaults(state)
   274→    path = Path(args.path)
   275→    config = runtime.config if isinstance(runtime.config, dict) else {}
   276→    lang_config = resolve_lang(args)
   277→    reset_subjective_count = 0
   278→    expired_manual_override_count = _expire_provisional_manual_override_assessments(
   279→        state
   280→    )
   281→    if getattr(args, "reset_subjective", False):
   282→        reset_subjective_count = _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   283→            state,
   284→            lang_name=getattr(lang_config, "name", None),
   285→        )
   286→
   287→    include_slow = not getattr(args, "skip_slow", False)
   288→    profile = _resolve_scan_profile(getattr(args, "profile", None), lang_config)
   289→    effective_include_slow = _effective_include_slow(include_slow, profile)
   290→
   291→    lang = _configure_lang_runtime(args, config, state, lang_config)
   292→    coverage_warnings = _seed_runtime_coverage_warnings(lang)
   293→    zone_overrides_raw = config.get("zone_overrides")
   294→    zone_overrides = zone_overrides_raw if isinstance(zone_overrides_raw, dict) else None
   295→
   296→    return ScanRuntime(
   297→        args=args,
   298→        state_path=state_file,
   299→        state=state,
   300→        path=path,
   301→        config=config,
   302→        lang=lang,
   303→        lang_label=f" ({lang.name})" if lang else "",
   304→        profile=profile,
   305→        effective_include_slow=effective_include_slow,
   306→        zone_overrides=zone_overrides,
   307→        reset_subjective_count=reset_subjective_count,
   308→        expired_manual_override_count=expired_manual_override_count,
   309→        coverage_warnings=coverage_warnings,
   310→    )
   311→
   312→
   313→def _augment_with_stale_exclusion_issues(
   314→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   315→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   316→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   317→    """Append stale exclude issues when excluded dirs are unreferenced."""
   318→    extra_exclusions = get_exclusions()
   319→    if not (extra_exclusions and runtime.lang and runtime.lang.file_finder):
   320→        return issues
   321→
   322→    scanned_files = runtime.lang.file_finder(runtime.path)
   323→    stale = _audit_excluded_dirs(
   324→        extra_exclusions, scanned_files, get_project_root()
   325→    )
   326→    if not stale:
   327→        return issues
   328→
   329→    augmented = list(issues)
   330→    augmented.extend(stale)
   331→    for stale_issue in stale:
   332→        print(colorize(f"  ℹ {stale_issue['summary']}", "dim"))
   333→    return augmented
   334→
   335→
   336→def _augment_with_stale_wontfix_issues(
   337→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   338→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   339→    *,
   340→    decay_scans: int,
   341→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]:
   342→    """Append re-triage issues for stale/worsening wontfix debt."""
   343→    return _augment_stale_wontfix_impl(
   344→        issues,
   345→        state=runtime.state,
   346→        scan_path=runtime.path,
   347→        project_root=get_project_root(),
   348→        decay_scans=decay_scans,
   349→    )
   350→
   351→
   352→def run_scan_generation(
   353→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   354→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, object], dict[str, object] | None]:
   355→    """Run detector pipeline and return issues, potentials, and codebase metrics."""
   356→    enable_file_cache()
   357→    enable_parse_cache()
   358→    try:
   359→        issues, potentials = plan_mod.generate_issues(
   360→            runtime.path,
   361→            lang=runtime.lang,
   362→            options=PlanScanOptions(
   363→                include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   364→                zone_overrides=runtime.zone_overrides,
   365→                profile=runtime.profile,
   366→            ),
   367→        )
   368→    finally:
   369→        disable_parse_cache()
   370→        disable_file_cache()
   371→
   372→    codebase_metrics = _collect_codebase_metrics(runtime.lang, runtime.path)
   373→    _warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files(
   374→        runtime.args, runtime.lang, runtime.path, codebase_metrics
   375→    )
   376→    issues = _augment_with_stale_exclusion_issues(issues, runtime)
   377→    decay_scans = _coerce_int(
   378→        runtime.config.get("wontfix_decay_scans"),
   379→        default=_WONTFIX_DECAY_SCANS_DEFAULT,
   380→    )
   381→    issues, monitored_wontfix = _augment_with_stale_wontfix_issues(
   382→        issues,
   383→        runtime,
   384→        decay_scans=max(decay_scans, 0),
   385→    )
   386→    potentials["stale_wontfix"] = monitored_wontfix
   387→    return issues, potentials, codebase_metrics
   388→
   389→
   390→def merge_scan_results(
   391→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   392→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   393→    potentials: dict[str, object],
   394→    codebase_metrics: dict[str, object] | None,
   395→) -> ScanMergeResult:
   396→    """Merge issues into persistent state and return diff + previous score snapshot."""
   397→    scan_path_rel = rel(str(runtime.path))
   398→    prev_scan_path = runtime.state.get("scan_path")
   399→    path_changed = prev_scan_path is not None and prev_scan_path != scan_path_rel
   400→
   401→    if not path_changed:
   402→        prev = state_mod.score_snapshot(runtime.state)
   403→    else:
   404→        prev = state_mod.ScoreSnapshot(None, None, None, None)
   405→    prev_dim_scores = (
   406→        runtime.state.get("dimension_scores", {}) if not path_changed else {}
   407→    )
   408→
   409→    if runtime.lang and runtime.lang.zone_map is not None:
   410→        runtime.state["zone_distribution"] = runtime.lang.zone_map.counts()
   411→    _persist_scan_coverage(runtime.state, runtime.lang)
   412→
   413→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   414→
   415→    diff = state_mod.merge_scan(
   416→        runtime.state,
   417→        issues,
   418→        options=state_mod.MergeScanOptions(
   419→            lang=runtime.lang.name if runtime.lang else None,
   420→            scan_path=scan_path_rel,
   421→            force_resolve=getattr(runtime.args, "force_resolve", False),
   422→            exclude=get_exclusions(),
   423→            potentials=potentials,
   424→            codebase_metrics=codebase_metrics,
   425→            include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   426→            ignore=runtime.config.get("ignore", []),
   427→            subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   428→        ),
   429→    )
   430→
   431→    expire_stale_holistic(
   432→        runtime.state, runtime.config.get("holistic_max_age_days", 30)
   433→    )
   434→    state_mod.save_state(
   435→        runtime.state,
   436→        runtime.state_path,
   437→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   438→    )
   439→
   440→    _clear_needs_rescan_flag(runtime.config)
   441→    _reconcile_plan_post_scan(runtime)
   442→
   443→    return ScanMergeResult(
   444→        diff=diff,
   445→        prev_overall=prev.overall,
   446→        prev_objective=prev.objective,
   447→        prev_strict=prev.strict,
   448→        prev_verified=prev.verified,
   449→        prev_dim_scores=prev_dim_scores,
   450→    )
   451→
   452→
   453→def resolve_noise_snapshot(
   454→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   455→    config: dict[str, object],
   456→) -> ScanNoiseSnapshot:
   457→    """Resolve noise budget settings and hidden issue counters."""
   458→    noise_budget, global_noise_budget, budget_warning = (
   459→        state_mod.resolve_issue_noise_settings(config)
   460→    )
   461→    issues_by_id = _state_issues(state)
   462→    open_issues = [
   463→        issue
   464→        for issue in state_mod.path_scoped_issues(
   465→            issues_by_id, state.get("scan_path")
   466→        ).values()
   467→        if issue.get("status") == "open"
   468→    ]
   469→    _, hidden_by_detector = state_mod.apply_issue_noise_budget(
   470→        open_issues,
   471→        budget=noise_budget,
   472→        global_budget=global_noise_budget,
   473→    )
   474→
   475→    return ScanNoiseSnapshot(
   476→        noise_budget=noise_budget,
   477→        global_noise_budget=global_noise_budget,
   478→        budget_warning=budget_warning,
   479→        hidden_by_detector=hidden_by_detector,
   480→        hidden_total=sum(hidden_by_detector.values()),
   481→    )
   482→
   483→
   484→def persist_reminder_history(
   485→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   486→    narrative: dict[str, object],
   487→) -> None:
   488→    """Persist reminder history emitted by narrative computation."""
   489→    if not (narrative and "reminder_history" in narrative):
   490→        return
   491→
   492→    runtime.state["reminder_history"] = narrative["reminder_history"]
   493→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   494→    state_mod.save_state(
   495→        runtime.state,
   496→        runtime.state_path,
   497→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   498→    )
   499→
   500→
   501→__all__ = [
   502→    "ScanStateContractError",
   503→    "ScanMergeResult",
   504→    "ScanNoiseSnapshot",
   505→    "ScanRuntime",
   506→    "merge_scan_results",
   507→    "persist_reminder_history",
   508→    "prepare_scan_runtime",
   509→    "resolve_noise_snapshot",
   510→    "run_scan_generation",
   511→]

1→"""Empty if-chain fixer: deletes if/else chains where all branches are empty."""
     2→
     3→from typing import Any
     4→
     5→from desloppify.languages.typescript.detectors._smell_helpers import scan_code
     6→from desloppify.languages.typescript.fixers.fixer_io import apply_fixer
     7→from desloppify.languages.typescript.fixers.syntax_scan import collapse_blank_lines
     8→
     9→
    10→def fix_empty_if_chain(
    11→    entries: list[dict[str, Any]],
    12→    *,
    13→    dry_run: bool = False,
    14→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    15→    """Delete if/else chains where all branches are empty."""
    16→
    17→    def transform(
    18→        lines: list[str],
    19→        file_entries: list[dict[str, Any]],
    20→    ) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    21→        lines_to_remove: set[int] = set()
    22→
    23→        for e in file_entries:
    24→            line_idx = e["line"] - 1
    25→            if line_idx < 0 or line_idx >= len(lines):
    26→                continue
    27→
    28→            end = _find_if_chain_end(lines, line_idx)
    29→            for idx in range(line_idx, end + 1):
    30→                lines_to_remove.add(idx)
    31→
    32→        new_lines = collapse_blank_lines(lines, lines_to_remove)
    33→        return new_lines, ["empty_if_chain"]
    34→
    35→    return apply_fixer(entries, transform, dry_run=dry_run)
    36→
    37→
    38→def _find_if_chain_end(lines: list[str], start: int) -> int:
    39→    """Find the last line of an if/else chain starting at `start`.
    40→
    41→    Tracks brace depth. Chain ends when braces balance and no else follows.
    42→    """
    43→    brace_depth = 0
    44→    found_brace = False
    45→
    46→    for i in range(start, min(start + 100, len(lines))):
    47→        line = lines[i]
    48→        for ci, ch, in_s in scan_code(line):
    49→            if in_s:
    50→                continue
    51→            if ch == "{":
    52→                brace_depth += 1
    53→                found_brace = True
    54→            elif ch == "}":
    55→                brace_depth -= 1
    56→                if found_brace and brace_depth == 0:
    57→                    rest = line[ci + 1 :].strip()
    58→                    if rest.startswith("else"):

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations

    10→
    11→def fix_unused_imports(entries: list[dict], *, dry_run: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    12→    """Remove unused imports from source files."""
    13→    import_entries = [entry for entry in entries if entry.get("category") == "imports"]
    14→
    15→    def transform(lines: list[str], file_entries: list[dict[str, object]]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    16→        unused_symbols = {str(entry["name"]) for entry in file_entries if "name" in entry}
    17→        unused_by_line: dict[int, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    18→        for entry in file_entries:
    19→            line = entry.get("line")
    20→            name = entry.get("name")
    21→            if isinstance(line, int) and name is not None:
    22→                unused_by_line[line].append(str(name))
    23→
    24→        new_lines, removed_symbols = process_unused_import_lines(lines, unused_symbols, unused_by_line)
    25→        removed: list[str] = []
    26→        for entry in file_entries:
    27→            name = str(entry.get("name", ""))
    28→            if name in removed_symbols and name not in removed:
    29→                removed.append(name)
    30→        return new_lines, removed
    31→
    32→    return apply_fixer(import_entries, transform, dry_run=dry_run)
    33→
    34→
    35→__all__ = ["fix_unused_imports"]

   107→def fix_debug_logs(entries: list[dict], *, dry_run: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
   108→    """Remove tagged console.log lines and clean up aftermath (dead vars, empty blocks)."""
   109→    entries_by_file: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
   110→    for e in entries:
   111→        entries_by_file.setdefault(e["file"], []).append(e)
   112→
   113→    def _transform(lines: list[str], file_entries: list[dict]):
   114→        lines_to_remove: set[int] = set()
   115→        for e in file_entries:
   116→            start = e["line"] - 1
   117→            if start >= len(lines):
   118→                continue
   119→            if _is_logger_wrapper_context(lines, start):
   120→                continue
   121→            end = find_balanced_end(lines, start, track="parens")
   122→            if end is None:
   123→                print(
   124→                    colorize(
   125→                        f"  Warn: skipping {rel(e['file'])}:{e['line']} — could not find statement end",
   126→                        "yellow",
   127→                    ),
   128→                    file=sys.stderr,
   129→                )
   130→                continue
   131→            for idx in range(start, end + 1):
   132→                lines_to_remove.add(idx)
   133→            _mark_orphaned_comments(lines, start, lines_to_remove)
   134→
   135→        dead_vars = _find_dead_log_variables(lines, lines_to_remove)
   136→        lines_to_remove |= dead_vars
   137→        new_lines = collapse_blank_lines(lines, lines_to_remove)
   138→        new_lines = _remove_empty_blocks(new_lines)
   139→        tags = sorted(set(e.get("tag", "") for e in file_entries))
   140→        return new_lines, tags
   141→
   142→    raw_results = apply_fixer(entries, _transform, dry_run=dry_run)
   143→    return [
   144→        {
   145→            "file": r["file"],
   146→            "removed": r["removed"],
   147→            "tags": r["removed"],
   148→            "lines_removed": r["lines_removed"],
   149→            "log_count": len(entries_by_file.get(r["file"], [])),
   150→        }
   151→        for r in raw_results

   155→def _normalize_wrapper_name(raw: str | None) -> str:
   156→    if not raw:
   157→        return ""
   158→    return raw.strip().strip("'\"").lower()
   159→
   160→
   161→def _is_logger_wrapper_name(raw: str | None) -> bool:
   162→    return _normalize_wrapper_name(raw) in _LOGGER_WRAPPER_NAMES
   163→
   164→
   165→def _line_logger_wrapper_name(line: str, patterns: tuple[re.Pattern[str], ...]) -> str | None:
   166→    for pattern in patterns:
   167→        match = pattern.match(line)
   168→        if match:
   169→            name = _normalize_wrapper_name(match.group("name"))
   170→            if name and name not in _CONTROL_FLOW_NAMES:
   171→                return name
   172→    return None
   173→
   174→
   175→def _previous_non_empty_line(lines: list[str], idx: int) -> str | None:
   176→    j = idx - 1
   177→    while j >= 0:
   178→        stripped = lines[j].strip()
   179→        if stripped:
   180→            return stripped
   181→        j -= 1
   182→    return None
   183→
   184→
   185→def _is_logger_wrapper_context(lines: list[str], start: int) -> bool:
   186→    """Return True when console logging is part of a named logger wrapper."""
   187→    current = lines[start].strip()
   188→    inline_name = _line_logger_wrapper_name(current, _INLINE_WRAPPER_PATTERNS)
   189→    if _is_logger_wrapper_name(inline_name):

   198→    prev_name = _line_logger_wrapper_name(prev, _PREV_LINE_HEADER_PATTERNS)

   209→def _mark_orphaned_comments(

   213→    for offset in range(1, 4):

   233→        "console",
   234→        "log",
   235→        "warn",
   236→        "info",
   237→        "debug",
   238→        "error",
   239→        "const",
   240→        "let",
   241→        "var",
   242→        "true",
   243→        "false",
   244→        "null",
   245→        "undefined",
   246→        "if",
   247→        "else",
   248→        "return",
   249→        "function",
   250→        "new",
   251→        "this",
   252→        "typeof",
   253→        "length",
   254→        "toString",
   255→        "JSON",
   256→        "stringify",
   257→        "Date",
   258→        "now",
   259→        "Math",
   260→        "Object",
   261→        "Array",
   262→        "String",
   263→        "Number",
   264→        "Boolean",
   265→        "Map",
   266→        "Set",
   267→        "Promise",
   268→        "Error",
   269→    ]
   270→)

   272→
   273→def _find_dead_log_variables(lines: list[str], removed_indices: set[int]) -> set[int]:
   274→    """Find variable declarations that were only used in removed log lines."""
   275→    referenced_in_logs: set[str] = set()
   276→    for idx in removed_indices:
   277→        if idx < len(lines):
   278→            for m in _IDENT_RE.finditer(lines[idx]):
   279→                ident = m.group(1)
   280→                if ident not in _IGNORE_IDENTS:
   281→                    referenced_in_logs.add(ident)
   282→
   283→    if not referenced_in_logs:
   284→        return set()
   285→
   286→    decl_lines: dict[str, int] = {}
   287→    for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
   288→        if idx in removed_indices:
   289→            continue
   290→        m = _VAR_DECL_RE.match(line)
   291→        if m and m.group(1) in referenced_in_logs:
   292→            decl_lines[m.group(1)] = idx
   293→
   294→    if not decl_lines:
   295→        return set()
   296→
   297→    dead: set[int] = set()
   298→    for ident, decl_idx in decl_lines.items():
   299→        used_elsewhere = False
   300→        pattern = re.compile(r"\b" + re.escape(ident) + r"\b")
   301→        for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
   302→            if idx == decl_idx or idx in removed_indices:
   303→                continue
   304→            if pattern.search(line):
   305→                used_elsewhere = True
   306→                break
   307→        if not used_elsewhere:
   308→            dead.add(decl_idx)
   309→
   310→    return dead

   313→# ── Empty block cleaner ────────────────────────────────────
   314→
   315→_EMPTY_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
   316→    r"""
   317→    ^(\s*)
   318→    (?:
   319→        (?:if|else\s+if)\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{\s*\}
   320→        | else\s*\{\s*\}
   321→        | \}\s*else\s*\{\s*\}
   322→    )
   323→    \s*$
   324→    """,
   325→    re.VERBOSE,
   326→)
   327→
   328→_EMPTY_CALLBACK_RE = re.compile(
   329→    r"""
   330→    ^\s*
   331→    (?:
   332→        \.then\s*\(\s*\(?[^)]*\)?\s*=>\s*\{\s*\}\s*\)
   333→        | \.catch\s*\(\s*\(?[^)]*\)?\s*=>\s*\{\s*\}\s*\)
   334→    )
   335→    \s*[;,]?\s*$
   336→    """,
   337→    re.VERBOSE,
   338→)

   340→
   341→def _try_remove_empty_use_effect(
   342→    lines: list[str], i: int, new_lines: list[str]
   343→) -> int | None:
   344→    """Remove empty useEffect(() => { }). Returns new index or None."""
   345→    stripped = lines[i].strip()
   346→    if not re.match(r"(?:React\.)?useEffect\s*\(\s*\(\s*\)\s*=>\s*\{", stripped):
   347→        return None
   348→    end = find_balanced_end(lines, i, track="all")
   349→    if end is None:
   350→        return None
   351→    body = "".join(lines[i : end + 1])
   352→    inner = extract_body_between_braces(body, search_after="=>")
   353→    if inner is None or inner.strip() != "":
   354→        return None
   355→    if new_lines and new_lines[-1].strip().startswith("//"):
   356→        new_lines.pop()
   357→    return end + 1
   358→
   359→
   360→def _try_remove_empty_callback(lines: list[str], i: int) -> int | None:
   361→    """Remove single-line .then(() => { }) / .catch((e) => { })."""
   362→    if _EMPTY_CALLBACK_RE.match(lines[i].strip()):
   363→        return i + 1
   364→    return None
   365→
   366→
   367→def _try_remove_multiline_callback(lines: list[str], i: int) -> int | None:
   368→    """Remove multi-line empty callback: someFunc(() => {\\n})."""
   369→    stripped = lines[i].strip()
   370→    if not re.search(r"=>\s*\{\s*$", stripped):
   371→        return None
   372→    if not re.search(r"\(\s*(?:\([^)]*\))?\s*=>\s*\{\s*$", stripped):
   373→        return None
   374→    j = i + 1
   375→    while j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip() == "":
   376→        j += 1
   377→    if j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip() in ("});", "},"):
   378→        return j + 1
   379→    return None
   380→
   381→
   382→def _try_remove_multiline_block(
   383→    lines: list[str], i: int, new_lines: list[str]
   384→) -> int | None:
   385→    """Remove multi-line empty if/else/else-if blocks."""
   386→    line = lines[i]
   387→    stripped = line.strip()
   388→    if not stripped.endswith("{"):
   389→        return None
   390→    j = i + 1
   391→    while j < len(lines) and lines[j].strip() == "":
   392→        j += 1
   393→    if j >= len(lines) or lines[j].strip() not in ("}", "});"):
   394→        return None
   395→
   396→    if re.match(r"\s*else\s*\{", stripped):
   397→        return j + 1
   398→    if re.match(r"\s*\}\s*else\s*\{", stripped):
   399→        indent = line[: len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
   400→        new_lines.append(f"{indent}}}\n")
   401→        return j + 1
   402→    if re.match(r"\s*(?:if|else\s+if)\s*\(", stripped):
   403→        return j + 1
   404→    return None
   405→
   406→
   407→def _try_remove_single_empty_block(lines: list[str], i: int) -> int | None:
   408→    """Remove single-line empty block (if/else/else-if with empty {})."""
   409→    if _EMPTY_BLOCK_RE.match(lines[i].strip()):
   410→        return i + 1
   411→    return None
   412→
   413→
   414→def _remove_empty_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
   415→    """Remove empty blocks left behind after log removal.
   416→
   417→    Handles: empty if/else, empty useEffect, empty catch, empty callbacks.
   418→    Makes multiple passes until stable.
   419→    """
   420→    _handlers = [
   421→        lambda lines, i, out: _try_remove_empty_use_effect(lines, i, out),
   422→        lambda lines, i, out: _try_remove_empty_callback(lines, i),
   423→        lambda lines, i, out: _try_remove_multiline_callback(lines, i),
   424→        lambda lines, i, out: _try_remove_multiline_block(lines, i, out),
   425→        lambda lines, i, out: _try_remove_single_empty_block(lines, i),
   426→    ]
   427→    changed = True
   428→    while changed:
   429→        changed = False
   430→        new_lines: list[str] = []
   431→        i = 0
   432→        while i < len(lines):
   433→            new_i = None
   434→            for handler in _handlers:
   435→                new_i = handler(lines, i, new_lines)
   436→                if new_i is not None:
   437→                    break
   438→            if new_i is not None:
   439→                changed = True
   440→                i = new_i
   441→            else:
   442→                new_lines.append(lines[i])
   443→                i += 1
   444→        lines = new_lines
   445→
   446→    # Final pass: collapse double blank lines
   447→    result = []
   448→    prev_blank = False
   449→    for line in lines:
   450→        is_blank = line.strip() == ""
   451→        if is_blank and prev_blank:
   452→            continue
   453→        result.append(line)
   454→        prev_blank = is_blank
   455→    return result
   456→

1→"""TypeScript fixer loader utilities."""

     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import importlib
     6→
     7→__all__ = [
     8→    "fix_debug_logs",
     9→    "fix_unused_imports",
    10→    "fix_unused_vars",
    11→    "fix_unused_params",
    12→    "fix_dead_useeffect",
    13→    "fix_empty_if_chain",
    14→]
    15→
    16→_EXPORT_MODULES = {
    17→    "fix_debug_logs": ".logs",
    18→    "fix_unused_imports": ".imports",
    19→    "fix_unused_vars": ".vars",
    20→    "fix_unused_params": ".params",
    21→    "fix_dead_useeffect": ".useeffect",
    22→    "fix_empty_if_chain": ".if_chain",
    23→}
    24→
    25→
    26→def __getattr__(name: str):
    27→    module_path = _EXPORT_MODULES.get(name)
    28→    if module_path is None:
    29→        raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")
    30→    module = importlib.import_module(module_path, __name__)
    31→    value = getattr(module, name)
    32→    globals()[name] = value
    33→    return value
    34→
    35→
    36→def __dir__() -> list[str]:
    37→    return sorted(set(globals()) | set(__all__))
    38→

    15→
    16→
    17→def find_balanced_end(
    18→    lines: list[str], start: int, *, track: str = "parens", max_lines: int = 80
    19→) -> int | None:
    20→    """Find the line where brackets opened at *start* balance to zero."""
    21→    depths = {"parens": 0, "braces": 0, "brackets": 0}
    22→    for idx in range(start, min(start + max_lines, len(lines))):
    23→        for _, ch, in_s in scan_code(lines[idx]):
    24→            if in_s:
    25→                continue
    26→            delta_spec = _CHAR_DEPTH_DELTA.get(ch)
    27→            if delta_spec is None:
    28→                continue
    29→            key, delta = delta_spec
    30→            depths[key] += delta
    31→            if delta > 0:
    32→                continue
    33→            if track == "parens" and key == "parens" and depths["parens"] <= 0:
    34→                return idx
    35→            if track == "braces" and key == "braces" and depths["braces"] <= 0:
    36→                return idx
    37→            if track == "all" and key == "parens" and depths["parens"] <= 0:
    38→                return idx
    39→    return None
    40→
    41→
    42→def extract_body_between_braces(text: str, search_after: str = "") -> str | None:
    43→    """Extract content between the first ``{`` and its matching ``}``."""
    44→    start_pos = 0
    45→    if search_after:
    46→        pos = text.find(search_after)
    47→        if pos == -1:
    48→            return None
    49→        start_pos = pos + len(search_after)
    50→
    51→    brace_pos = text.find("{", start_pos)
    52→    if brace_pos == -1:
    53→        return None
    54→
    55→    depth = 0
    56→    for i, ch, in_s in scan_code(text, brace_pos):
    57→        if in_s:
    58→            continue
    59→        if ch == "{":
    60→            depth += 1
    61→        elif ch == "}":
    62→            depth -= 1
    63→            if depth == 0:
    64→                return text[brace_pos + 1 : i]
    65→    return None
    66→
    67→
    68→def collapse_blank_lines(
    69→    lines: list[str], removed_indices: set[int] | None = None
    70→) -> list[str]:
    71→    """Filter removed lines and collapse repeated blank lines."""
    72→    result = []
    73→    prev_blank = False
    74→    for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
    75→        if removed_indices and idx in removed_indices:
    76→            continue
    77→        is_blank = line.strip() == ""
    78→        if is_blank and prev_blank:
    79→            continue
    80→        result.append(line)
    81→        prev_blank = is_blank
    82→    return result
    83→
    84→
    85→__all__ = [
    86→    "collapse_blank_lines",
    87→    "extract_body_between_braces",
    88→    "find_balanced_end",
    89→]

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging
     6→import sys
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→
     9→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    10→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import rel, safe_write_text
    11→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
    12→from desloppify.base.text.text_api import get_project_root
    13→
    14→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    15→
    16→
    17→def _group_entries(entries: list[dict], file_key: str) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
    18→    grouped: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    19→    for entry in entries:
    20→        filepath = entry.get(file_key)
    21→        if not isinstance(filepath, str) or not filepath:
    22→            continue
    23→        grouped.setdefault(filepath, []).append(entry)
    24→    return grouped
    25→
    26→
    27→def apply_fixer(
    28→    entries: list[dict], transform_fn, *, dry_run: bool = False, file_key: str = "file"
    29→) -> list[dict]:
    30→    """Shared file-loop template for fixers."""
    31→    by_file = _group_entries(entries, file_key)
    32→    results = []
    33→    skipped_files: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    34→    for filepath, file_entries in sorted(by_file.items()):
    35→        try:
    36→            changed = _process_fixer_file(
    37→                filepath,
    38→                file_entries,
    39→                transform_fn=transform_fn,
    40→                dry_run=dry_run,
    41→            )
    42→            if changed is not None:
    43→                results.append(changed)
    44→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as ex:
    45→            skipped_files.append((filepath, str(ex)))
    46→            print(colorize(f"  Skip {rel(filepath)}: {ex}", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
    47→
    48→    if skipped_files:
    49→        log_best_effort_failure(
    50→            logger,
    51→            f"apply TypeScript fixer across {len(skipped_files)} skipped file(s)",
    52→            OSError(
    53→                "; ".join(f"{path}: {reason}" for path, reason in skipped_files[:5])
    54→            ),
    55→        )
    56→
    57→    return results
    58→
    59→
    60→def _process_fixer_file(
    61→    filepath: str,
    62→    file_entries: list[dict],
    63→    *,
    64→    transform_fn,
    65→    dry_run: bool,
    66→) -> dict[str, object] | None:
    67→    path = Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else get_project_root() / filepath
    68→    original = path.read_text()
    69→    lines = original.splitlines(keepends=True)
    70→
    71→    new_lines, removed_names = transform_fn(lines, file_entries)
    72→    new_content = "".join(new_lines)
    73→    if new_content == original:
    74→        return None
    75→
    76→    if not dry_run:
    77→        _write_fixer_content(path, new_content)
    78→
    79→    lines_removed = len(original.splitlines()) - len(new_content.splitlines())
    80→    return {
    81→        "file": filepath,
    82→        "removed": removed_names,
    83→        "lines_removed": lines_removed,
    84→    }
    85→
    86→
    87→def _write_fixer_content(path: Path, content: str) -> None:
    88→    try:
    89→        safe_write_text(path, content)
    90→    except OSError as exc:
    91→        log_best_effort_failure(logger, f"write TypeScript fixer output {path}", exc)
    92→        raise
    93→
    94→
    95→__all__ = ["apply_fixer"]

    10→# Bump this integer whenever docs/SKILL.md changes in a way that agents

    14→SKILL_VERSION_RE = re.compile(r"<!--\s*desloppify-skill-version:\s*(\d+)\s*-->")
    15→SKILL_OVERLAY_RE = re.compile(r"<!--\s*desloppify-overlay:\s*(\w+)\s*-->")

    21→SKILL_SEARCH_PATHS = (

    23→    ".opencode/skills/desloppify/SKILL.md",
    24→    "AGENTS.md",

    34→    # OpenCode support added with thanks to @H3xKatana.
    35→    "opencode": (".opencode/skills/desloppify/SKILL.md", "OPENCODE", True),
    36→    "codex": ("AGENTS.md", "CODEX", False),
    37→    "cursor": (".cursor/rules/desloppify.md", "CURSOR", True),
    38→    "copilot": (".github/copilot-instructions.md", "COPILOT", False),
    39→    "windsurf": ("AGENTS.md", "WINDSURF", False),
    40→    "gemini": ("AGENTS.md", "GEMINI", False),

    42→
    43→
    44→@dataclass
    45→class SkillInstall:
    46→    """Detected skill document installation."""
    47→
    48→    rel_path: str
    49→    version: int
    50→    overlay: str | None
    51→    stale: bool
    52→
    53→
    54→def find_installed_skill() -> SkillInstall | None:
    55→    """Find installed skill document metadata, or None."""
    56→    project_root = get_project_root()
    57→    for rel_path in SKILL_SEARCH_PATHS:
    58→        full = project_root / rel_path
    59→        if not full.is_file():
    60→            continue
    61→        try:
    62→            content = full.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    63→        except OSError as exc:
    64→            _ = exc
    65→            continue
    66→        version_match = SKILL_VERSION_RE.search(content)
    67→        if not version_match:
    68→            continue
    69→        installed_version = int(version_match.group(1))
    70→        overlay_match = SKILL_OVERLAY_RE.search(content)
    71→        overlay = overlay_match.group(1) if overlay_match else None
    72→        return SkillInstall(
    73→            rel_path=rel_path,
    74→            version=installed_version,
    75→            overlay=overlay,
    76→            stale=installed_version < SKILL_VERSION,
    77→        )
    78→    return None
    79→
    80→
    81→def check_skill_version() -> str | None:
    82→    """Return a warning if installed skill doc is outdated."""
    83→    install = find_installed_skill()
    84→    if not install or not install.stale:
    85→        return None
    86→    return (
    87→        f"Your desloppify skill document is outdated "
    88→        f"(v{install.version}, current v{SKILL_VERSION}). "
    89→        "Run: desloppify update-skill"
    90→    )

   254→            f"for {key}, got: {raw}"
   255→        )
   256→    config[key] = target_strict_score
   257→
   258→
   259→def _set_bool_config_value(config: dict, key: str, raw: str) -> None:
   260→    normalized = raw.lower()
   261→    if normalized in ("true", "1", "yes"):
   262→        config[key] = True
   263→        return
   264→    if normalized in ("false", "0", "no"):
   265→        config[key] = False
   266→        return
   267→    raise ValueError(f"Expected true/false for {key}, got: {raw}")
   268→
   269→
   270→def _set_str_config_value(config: dict, key: str, raw: str) -> None:
   271→    if key == "badge_path":
   272→        config[key] = _validate_badge_path(raw)
   273→        return
   274→    config[key] = raw
   275→
   276→
   277→def _set_list_config_value(config: dict, key: str, raw: str) -> None:
   278→    config.setdefault(key, [])
   279→    if raw not in config[key]:
   280→        config[key].append(raw)
   281→
   282→
   283→_SCHEMA_SETTERS = {
   284→    int: _set_int_config_value,
   285→    bool: _set_bool_config_value,
   286→    str: _set_str_config_value,
   287→    list: _set_list_config_value,
   288→}
   289→
   290→
   291→def set_config_value(config: dict, key: str, raw: str) -> None:
   292→    """Parse and set a config value from a raw string.
   293→
   294→    Handles special cases:
   295→    - "never" → 0 for age keys
   296→    - "true"/"false" for bools
   297→    """
   298→    if key not in CONFIG_SCHEMA:
   299→        raise KeyError(f"Unknown config key: {key}")
   300→
   301→    schema = CONFIG_SCHEMA[key]
   302→    setter = _SCHEMA_SETTERS.get(schema.type)
   303→    if setter is not None:
   304→        setter(config, key, raw)
   305→        return
   306→    if schema.type is dict:
   307→        raise ValueError(f"Cannot set dict key '{key}' via CLI — use subcommands")
   308→    config[key] = raw
   309→
   310→
   311→def unset_config_value(config: dict, key: str) -> None:
   312→    """Reset a config key to its default value."""
   313→    if key not in CONFIG_SCHEMA:
   314→        raise KeyError(f"Unknown config key: {key}")
   315→    config[key] = copy.deepcopy(CONFIG_SCHEMA[key].default)
   316→
   317→
   318→def config_for_query(config: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   319→    """Return a sanitized config dict suitable for query.json."""
   320→    return {k: config.get(k, schema.default) for k, schema in CONFIG_SCHEMA.items()}
   321→
   322→
   323→def _merge_config_value(config: dict, key: str, value: object) -> None:
   324→    """Merge a config value into the target dict."""
   325→    if key not in config:
   326→        config[key] = copy.deepcopy(value)
   327→        return
   328→    if isinstance(value, list) and isinstance(config[key], list):
   329→        for item in value:
   330→            if item not in config[key]:
   331→                config[key].append(item)
   332→        return
   333→    if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(config[key], dict):
   334→        for dk, dv in value.items():
   335→            if dk not in config[key]:
   336→                config[key][dk] = copy.deepcopy(dv)
   337→        return
   338→
   339→
   340→def _load_state_file_payload(path: Path) -> dict | None:
   341→    try:
   342→        payload = json.loads(path.read_text())
   343→    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) as exc:
   344→        logger.debug("Skipping unreadable state file %s: %s", path, exc)
   345→        return None
   346→    if isinstance(payload, dict):
   347→        return payload
   348→    return None
   349→
   350→
   351→def _merge_legacy_state_config(config: dict, old_config: dict) -> None:
   352→    for key, value in old_config.items():
   353→        if key not in CONFIG_SCHEMA:
   354→            continue
   355→        _merge_config_value(config, key, value)
   356→
   357→
   358→def _strip_config_from_state_file(path: Path, state_data: dict) -> None:
   359→    if "config" not in state_data:
   360→        return
   361→    del state_data["config"]
   362→    try:
   363→        safe_write_text(path, json.dumps(state_data, indent=2) + "\n")
   364→    except OSError as exc:
   365→        log_best_effort_failure(
   366→            logger,
   367→            f"rewrite state file {path} after config migration",
   368→            exc,
   369→        )
   370→
   371→
   372→def _migrate_single_state_file(config: dict, path: Path) -> bool:
   373→    state_data = _load_state_file_payload(path)
   374→    if state_data is None:
   375→        return False
   376→    old_config = state_data.get("config")
   377→    if not isinstance(old_config, dict) or not old_config:
   378→        return False
   379→
   380→    _merge_legacy_state_config(config, old_config)
   381→    _strip_config_from_state_file(path, state_data)
   382→    return True
   383→
   384→
   385→def _migrate_from_state_files(config_path: Path) -> dict:
   386→    """Migrate config keys from state-*.json files into config.json.
   387→
   388→    Reads state["config"] from all state files, merges them (union for
   389→    lists, merge for dicts), writes config.json, and strips "config" from
   390→    the state files.
   391→    """
   392→    config: dict = {}
   393→    state_dir = config_path.parent
   394→    if not state_dir.exists():
   395→        return config
   396→
   397→    state_files = list(state_dir.glob("state-*.json")) + list(
   398→        state_dir.glob("state.json")
   399→    )
   400→    migrated_any = False
   401→    for sf in state_files:
   402→        migrated_any = _migrate_single_state_file(config, sf) or migrated_any
   403→
   404→    if migrated_any and config:
   405→        try:
   406→            save_config(config, config_path)
   407→        except OSError as exc:
   408→            log_best_effort_failure(
   409→                logger, f"save migrated config to {config_path}", exc
   410→            )
   411→
   412→    return config
   413→
   414→
   415→# ── Target score helpers ─────────────────────────────────────
   416→
   417→
   418→def coerce_target_score(value: object, *, fallback: float = 95.0) -> float:
   419→    """Normalize target score-like values to a safe [0, 100] float."""
   420→    if is_numeric(fallback):
   421→        fallback_value = float(fallback)
   422→    else:
   423→        fallback_value = 95.0
   424→
   425→    if is_numeric(value):
   426→        parsed = float(value)
   427→    elif isinstance(value, str):
   428→        text = value.strip()
   429→        if not text:
   430→            parsed = fallback_value
   431→        else:
   432→            try:
   433→                parsed = float(text)
   434→            except ValueError:
   435→                parsed = fallback_value
   436→    else:
   437→        parsed = fallback_value
   438→    return max(0.0, min(100.0, parsed))
   439→
   440→
   441→def target_strict_score_from_config(
   442→    config: dict | None, *, fallback: float = 95.0
   443→) -> float:
   444→    """Read and normalize target strict score from config."""
   445→    if isinstance(config, dict):
   446→        raw = config.get("target_strict_score", fallback)
   447→    else:
   448→        raw = fallback
   449→    return coerce_target_score(raw, fallback=fallback)
   450→

   142→    if not path.is_absolute() and not is_root_anchored:
   143→        return raw_path, project_root / path
   144→
   145→    try:
   146→        rel_path = str(path.relative_to(project_root))
   147→    except ValueError:
   148→        rel_path = str(path)
   149→    return rel_path, path
   150→
   151→
   152→def compute_badge_status() -> BadgeStatus:
   153→    """Check configured scorecard path and whether README references it."""
   154→    project_root = get_project_root()
   155→    scorecard_rel, scorecard_path = resolve_badge_path(project_root)
   156→    generated = scorecard_path.exists()
   157→
   158→    in_readme = False
   159→    if generated:
   160→        for readme_name in ("README.md", "readme.md", "README.MD"):
   161→            readme_path = project_root / readme_name
   162→            if readme_path.exists():
   163→                try:
   164→                    in_readme = scorecard_rel in readme_path.read_text(
   165→                        encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"
   166→                    )
   167→                except OSError:
   168→                    in_readme = False
   169→                break
   170→
   171→    recommendation = None
   172→    if generated and not in_readme:
   173→        recommendation = f'Add to README: <img src="{scorecard_rel}" width="100%">'
   174→
   175→    return {
   176→        "generated": generated,
   177→        "in_readme": in_readme,
   178→        "path": scorecard_rel,
   179→        "recommendation": recommendation,
   180→    }
   181→
   182→
   183→def compute_primary_action(actions: list[dict]) -> PrimaryAction | None:
   184→    """Pick the highest-priority action for user-facing guidance."""
   185→    if not actions:
   186→        return None
   187→    top = actions[0]
   188→    command = str(top.get("command", "")).strip()
   189→    if not command:
   190→        return None
   191→    description = str(top.get("description", "")).strip() or "run highest-impact action"
   192→    return {
   193→        "command": command,
   194→        "description": description,
   195→    }
   196→
   197→
   198→def compute_why_now(
   199→    phase: str,
   200→    strategy: dict[str, object],
   201→    primary_action: dict | None,
   202→) -> str:
   203→    """Explain why the recommended action should happen now."""
   204→    hint = str(strategy.get("hint", "")).strip() if isinstance(strategy, dict) else ""
   205→    if hint:
   206→        return hint
   207→    if primary_action and primary_action.get("description"):
   208→        return str(primary_action["description"])
   209→    phase_default = {
   210→        "first_scan": "Start with highest-impact issues to establish a clean baseline.",
   211→        "regression": "Recent regressions should be contained before new work.",
   212→        "stagnation": "Current approach is stalling; tackle a different high-impact lane.",
   213→        "maintenance": "Keep the codebase stable by resolving new risk quickly.",
   214→    }
   215→    return phase_default.get(phase, "Address the highest-impact open issues first.")
   216→
   217→
   218→def compute_verification_step(_command: str | None) -> VerificationStep:
   219→    """Verification step returned with every narrative plan."""
   220→    return {
   221→        "command": "desloppify scan",
   222→        "reason": "revalidate after changes",
   223→    }
   224→
   225→
   226→def compute_risk_flags(state: StateModel, debt: dict) -> list[RiskFlag]:
   227→    """Build ordered risk flags from suppression and wontfix debt signals."""
   228→    flags: list[RiskFlag] = []
   229→
   230→    ignore_integrity = state.get("ignore_integrity", {})
   231→    suppressed_pct = float(ignore_integrity.get("suppressed_pct", 0.0) or 0.0)
   232→    ignored_count = int(ignore_integrity.get("ignored", 0) or 0)
   233→    if suppressed_pct >= _HIGH_IGNORE_SUPPRESSION_THRESHOLD or ignored_count >= 100:
   234→        severity = "high" if suppressed_pct >= 40.0 or ignored_count >= 200 else "medium"
   235→        message = (
   236→            f"{suppressed_pct:.1f}% issues hidden by ignore patterns"
   237→            if suppressed_pct > 0
   238→            else f"{ignored_count} issues hidden by ignore patterns"
   239→        )
   240→        flags.append(
   241→            {
   242→                "type": "high_ignore_suppression",
   243→                "severity": severity,
   244→                "message": message,
   245→            }
   246→        )
   247→
   248→    wontfix_count = int(debt.get("wontfix_count", 0) or 0)
   249→    overall_gap = float(debt.get("overall_gap", 0.0) or 0.0)
   250→    if overall_gap >= _WONTFIX_GAP_THRESHOLD or wontfix_count > 0:
   251→        severity = "high" if overall_gap >= 5.0 or wontfix_count >= 50 else "medium"
   252→        flags.append(
   253→            {
   254→                "type": "wontfix_gap",
   255→                "severity": severity,
   256→                "message": (
   257→                    f"Strict/lenient gap is {overall_gap:.1f} pts with "
   258→                    f"{wontfix_count} wontfix issues"
   259→                ),
   260→            }
   261→        )
   262→
   263→    flags.sort(key=lambda flag: _RISK_SEVERITY_ORDER.get(flag.get("severity"), 99))
   264→    return flags
   265→
   266→
   267→def history_for_lang(raw_history: list[dict], lang: str | None) -> list[dict]:
   268→    if not lang:
   269→        return raw_history
   270→    return [entry for entry in raw_history if entry.get("lang") in (lang, None)]
   271→
   272→
   273→def scoped_issues(state: StateModel) -> dict[str, Issue]:
   274→    return path_scoped_issues(
   275→        state.get("issues", {}), state.get("scan_path")
   276→    )

   279→def score_snapshot(state: StateModel) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
   280→    scores = state_score_snapshot(state)
   281→    return scores.strict, scores.overall

    35→    plan: dict | None
    36→    target_strict: float
    37→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility
    38→

    40→def queue_context(
    41→    state: StateModel,
    42→    *,
    43→    config: dict | None = None,
    44→    plan: dict | None | object = _PLAN_AUTO_LOAD,
    45→    target_strict: float | None = None,
    46→) -> QueueContext:
    47→    """Build a :class:`QueueContext` with all parameters resolved.
    48→
    49→    Resolution order:
    50→
    51→    1. **plan** — explicit value wins; sentinel ``_PLAN_AUTO_LOAD`` triggers
    52→       ``load_plan()`` (guarded by ``PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS``).
    53→    2. **target_strict** — explicit float wins; ``None`` reads from *config*
    54→       via ``target_strict_score_from_config``; final fallback is ``95.0``.
    55→    3. **policy** — ``compute_subjective_visibility(state, ...)`` with the
    56→       resolved plan and target_strict so every downstream consumer sees
    57→       the same objective-vs-subjective balance.
    58→    """
    59→    # --- resolve plan ---
    60→    if plan is _PLAN_AUTO_LOAD:
    61→        try:
    62→            resolved_plan: dict | None = plan_mod.load_plan()
    63→        except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    64→            resolved_plan = None
    65→    else:
    66→        resolved_plan = plan  # type: ignore[assignment]
    67→
    68→    # --- resolve target_strict ---
    69→    if target_strict is not None:
    70→        resolved_target = target_strict
    71→    elif config is not None:
    72→        resolved_target = target_strict_score_from_config(config, fallback=95.0)
    73→    else:
    74→        resolved_target = 95.0
    75→
    76→    # --- resolve policy ---
    77→    resolved_policy = compute_subjective_visibility(
    78→        state,
    79→        target_strict=resolved_target,
    80→        plan=resolved_plan,
    81→    )
    82→
    83→    return QueueContext(
    84→        plan=resolved_plan,
    85→        target_strict=resolved_target,
    86→        policy=resolved_policy,
    87→    )
    88→
    89→

    91→    "QueueContext",
    92→    "queue_context",
    93→]

   712→class TestFindIfChainEnd:
   713→    """Tests for _find_if_chain_end()."""
   714→
   715→    def test_simple_if_block(self):
   716→        """Single if block end is found correctly."""
   717→        lines = ["if (x) {\n", "  doStuff();\n", "}\n"]
   718→        assert _find_if_chain_end(lines, 0) == 2
   719→
   720→    def test_if_else_chain_same_line(self):
   721→        """if/else chain where else is on the closing-brace line continues tracking."""
   722→        # When "} else {" is on one line, the brace tracker sees } (depth=0),
   723→        # recognizes "else" follows, breaks out of the char loop, but does NOT
   724→        # re-enter the second { on that line.  So brace_depth stays 0 and the
   725→        # function never finds the closing } of the else branch.  It falls
   726→        # through and returns `start`.
   727→        lines = [
   728→            "if (x) {\n",
   729→            "  a();\n",
   730→            "} else {\n",
   731→            "  b();\n",
   732→            "}\n",
   733→        ]
   734→        result = _find_if_chain_end(lines, 0)
   735→        # The current implementation returns start (0) for this pattern;
   736→        # fix_empty_if_chain uses apply_fixer/collapse which handles it
   737→        assert isinstance(result, int)
   738→
   739→    def test_fallback_to_start(self):
   740→        """If no braces found, returns start index."""
   741→        lines = ["if (x) doSomething();\n"]
   742→        assert _find_if_chain_end(lines, 0) == 0
   743→

## TASK A: Enforce FixResult contract

**Problem:** All 6 TypeScript fixers returned raw `list[dict]` (or `tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]` in the case of `vars.py`) instead of `FixResult`. The `isinstance` fallback in `fix/cmd.py` handled this but was a half-finished migration.

**Changes made:**

1. **`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/fixers/vars.py`** -- Changed return type from `tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]` to `FixResult`. Added `FixResult` import. Now returns `FixResult(entries=results, skip_reasons=dict(skip_reasons))`.

2. **`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/fixers/params.py`** -- Changed return type from `list[dict]` to `FixResult`. Added `FixResult` import. Wraps return in `FixResult(entries=...)`.

3. **`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/fixers/useeffect.py`** -- Changed return type from `list[dict[str, Any]]` to `FixResult`. Added `FixResult` import. Wraps return in `FixResult(entries=...)`.

4. **`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/fixers/if_chain.py`** -- Changed return type from `list[dict[str, Any]]` to `FixResult`. Added `FixResult` import. Wraps return in `FixResult(entries=...)`.

5. **`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/fixers/imports.py`** -- Changed return type from `list[dict]` to `FixResult`. Added `FixResult` import. Wraps return in `FixResult(entries=...)`.

6. **`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/fixers/logs.py`** -- Changed return type from `list[dict]` to `FixResult`. Added `FixResult` import. Wraps the list comprehension result in `FixResult(entries=[...])`.

7. **`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/__init__.py`** -- Simplified `_fix_vars` wrapper (now just passes through since `fix_unused_vars` returns `FixResult` directly). Updated `_fix_logs` to access `.entries` when iterating over results.

8. **`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/_framework/base/types.py`** -- Updated `FixerConfig.fix` type annotation from `Callable[..., FixResult | list[dict]]` to `Callable[..., FixResult]`.

9. **`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/fix/cmd.py`** -- Removed the `isinstance(raw, FixResult)` fallback branch. Now directly accesses `raw.entries` and `raw.skip_reasons`. Removed unused `FixResult` import.

10. **`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/tests/test_ts_fixers.py`** -- Updated all test assertions to use `.entries` and `.skip_reasons` attributes instead of treating return values as raw lists or tuples.

---

## TASK B: Split show_score_delta into focused functions

**Problem:** `show_score_delta` was a ~70-line function handling four independent display concerns.

**Changes made in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/scan/reporting/summary.py`:**

Extracted four focused helper functions:

1. **`_print_score_quartet(new, prev_overall, prev_objective, prev_strict, prev_verified, non_comparable_reason)`** -- Prints the four-score comparison line with deltas and the non-comparable reason if present.

2. **`_print_wontfix_gap(wontfix, gap)`** -- Prints the yellow warning about the gap between overall and strict scores when significant (gap >= 5 and wontfix >= 10).

3. **`_print_score_legend(state, gap)`** -- Conditionally shows the score guide text (on first scan, large gap, or agent environments). Delegates to the existing `_print_score_guide()`.

4. **`_print_integrity_warnings(state)`** -- Extracts subjective integrity data from state and delegates to the existing `_print_subjective_integrity_warning()`.

`show_score_delta` is now a short orchestrator that calls these four functions in sequence, with the early-exit for incomplete scores and the score-reveal check retained inline.

    63→def _update_max_signal(signals: ConcernSignals, key: SignalKey, value: object) -> None:

    65→    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int | float) or value <= 0:

   204→    if "coupling" in detectors:
   205→        return "coupling_design"
   206→    if signals.get("max_params", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_PARAMS:
   207→        return "interface_design"
   208→    if signals.get("max_nesting", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_NESTING:
   209→        return "structural_complexity"
   210→    if "responsibility_cohesion" in detectors:
   211→        return "mixed_responsibilities"
   212→    return "design_concern"
   213→
   214→
   215→def _build_summary(
   216→    concern_type: str,
   217→    detectors: set[str],
   218→    signals: ConcernSignals,
   219→) -> str:
   220→    """Human-readable one-liner."""
   221→    if concern_type == "mixed_responsibilities":
   222→        return (
   223→            f"Issues from {len(detectors)} detectors — "
   224→            "may have too many responsibilities"
   225→        )
   226→    if concern_type == "structural_complexity":
   227→        parts: list[str] = []
   228→        monster_loc = signals.get("monster_loc", 0)
   229→        if monster_loc:
   230→            funcs = signals.get("monster_funcs", [])
   231→            label = f" ({', '.join(funcs[:3])})" if funcs else ""
   232→            parts.append(f"monster function{label}: {int(monster_loc)} lines")
   233→        nesting = signals.get("max_nesting", 0)
   234→        if nesting >= ELEVATED_MAX_NESTING:
   235→            parts.append(f"nesting depth {int(nesting)}")
   236→        params = signals.get("max_params", 0)
   237→        if params >= ELEVATED_MAX_PARAMS:
   238→            parts.append(f"{int(params)} parameters")
   239→        return f"Structural complexity: {', '.join(parts) or 'elevated signals'}"
   240→    if concern_type == "duplication_design":
   241→        return "Duplication pattern — assess if extraction is warranted"
   242→    if concern_type == "coupling_design":
   243→        return "Coupling pattern — assess if boundaries need adjustment"
   244→    if concern_type == "interface_design":
   245→        return f"Interface complexity: {int(signals.get('max_params', 0))} parameters"
   246→    return f"Design signals from {', '.join(sorted(detectors))}"
   247→
   248→
   249→def _build_evidence(
   250→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   251→    signals: ConcernSignals,
   252→) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   253→    """Build evidence tuple from all issues and extracted signals."""
   254→    evidence: list[str] = []
   255→
   256→    detectors = sorted({f.get("detector", "") for f in issues})
   257→    evidence.append(f"Flagged by: {', '.join(detectors)}")
   258→
   259→    loc = signals.get("loc")
   260→    if loc:
   261→        evidence.append(f"File size: {int(loc)} lines")
   262→    params = signals.get("max_params")
   263→    if params and params >= ELEVATED_MAX_PARAMS:
   264→        evidence.append(f"Max parameters: {int(params)}")
   265→    nesting = signals.get("max_nesting")
   266→    if nesting and nesting >= ELEVATED_MAX_NESTING:
   267→        evidence.append(f"Max nesting depth: {int(nesting)}")
   268→    monster_loc = signals.get("monster_loc")
   269→    if monster_loc:
   270→        funcs = signals.get("monster_funcs", [])
   271→        label = f" ({', '.join(funcs[:3])})" if funcs else ""
   272→        evidence.append(f"Monster function{label}: {int(monster_loc)} lines")
   273→
   274→    # Individual issue summaries — give LLM the full picture, capped.
   275→    for f in issues[:10]:
   276→        summary = f.get("summary", "")
   277→        if summary:
   278→            evidence.append(f"[{f.get('detector', '')}] {summary}")
   279→
   280→    return tuple(evidence)
   281→
   282→
   283→def _build_question(
   284→    detectors: set[str], signals: ConcernSignals
   285→) -> str:
   286→    """Build targeted question from dominant signals."""
   287→    parts: list[str] = []
   288→
   289→    if len(detectors) >= MIN_DETECTORS_FOR_MIXED:
   290→        parts.append(
   291→            f"This file has issues across {len(detectors)} dimensions "
   292→            f"({', '.join(sorted(detectors))}). Is it trying to do too many "
   293→            "things, or is this complexity inherent to its domain?"
   294→        )
   295→
   296→    funcs = signals.get("monster_funcs", [])
   297→    if funcs:
   298→        parts.append(
   299→            f"What are the distinct responsibilities in {funcs[0]}()? "
   300→            "Should it be decomposed into focused functions?"
   301→        )
   302→
   303→    if signals.get("max_params", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_PARAMS:
   304→        parts.append(
   305→            "Should the parameters be grouped into a config/context object? "
   306→            "Which ones belong together?"
   307→        )
   308→
   309→    if signals.get("max_nesting", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_NESTING:
   310→        parts.append(
   311→            "Can the nesting be reduced with early returns, guard clauses, "
   312→            "or extraction into helper functions?"
   313→        )
   314→
   315→    if "dupes" in detectors or "boilerplate_duplication" in detectors:
   316→        parts.append(
   317→            "Is the duplication worth extracting into a shared utility, "
   318→            "or is it intentional variation?"
   319→        )
   320→
   321→    if "coupling" in detectors:
   322→        parts.append(
   323→            "Is the coupling intentional or does it indicate a missing "
   324→            "abstraction boundary?"
   325→        )
   326→
   327→    if "orphaned" in detectors:
   328→        parts.append(
   329→            "Is this file truly dead, or is it used via a non-import mechanism "
   330→            "(dynamic import, CLI entry point, plugin)?"
   331→        )
   332→
   333→    if "responsibility_cohesion" in detectors:
   334→        parts.append(
   335→            "What are the distinct responsibilities? Should this module be "
   336→            "split along those lines?"
   337→        )
   338→
   339→    if not parts:
   340→        parts.append(
   341→            "Review the flagged patterns — are they design problems that "
   342→            "need addressing, or acceptable given the file's role?"
   343→        )
   344→
   345→    return " ".join(parts)
   346→
   347→
   348→# ── Generators ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   349→
   350→
   351→def _file_concerns(state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   352→    """Per-file design concerns from aggregated mechanical signals.
   353→
   354→    Flags a file if it has 2+ judgment-needed detectors OR a single
   355→    detector with elevated signals (monster function, high params,
   356→    deep nesting, duplication, coupling, mixed responsibilities).
   357→    Bundles ALL issues for that file so the LLM sees the full picture.
   358→    """
   359→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   360→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   361→
   362→    for file, all_issues in by_file.items():
   363→        judgment = [
   364→            f for f in all_issues
   365→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   366→        ]
   367→        if not judgment:
   368→            continue
   369→
   370→        judgment_dets = {f.get("detector", "") for f in judgment}
   371→        elevated = _has_elevated_signals(judgment)
   372→
   373→        # Flag if 2+ judgment detectors OR 1 with elevated signals
   374→        # OR 1 judgment detector + 2 mechanical issues from any detector.
   375→        mechanical_count = len(all_issues)
   376→        if len(judgment_dets) < 2 and not elevated:
   377→            if not (len(judgment_dets) >= 1 and mechanical_count >= 3):
   378→                continue
   379→
   380→        signals = _extract_signals(judgment)
   381→        concern_type = _classify(judgment_dets, signals)
   382→        evidence = _build_evidence(judgment, signals)
   383→        question = _build_question(judgment_dets, signals)
   384→        summary = _build_summary(concern_type, judgment_dets, signals)
   385→
   386→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(f.get("id", "") for f in judgment))
   387→        fp_keys = tuple(sorted(judgment_dets))
   388→        fp = _fingerprint(concern_type, file, fp_keys)
   389→
   390→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   391→            continue
   392→
   393→        concerns.append(
   394→            Concern(
   395→                type=concern_type,
   396→                file=file,
   397→                summary=summary,
   398→                evidence=evidence,
   399→                question=question,
   400→                fingerprint=fp,
   401→                source_issues=all_ids,
   402→            )
   403→        )
   404→
   405→    return concerns
   406→
   407→
   408→def _cross_file_patterns(state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   409→    """Systemic patterns: same judgment detector combo across 3+ files.
   410→
   411→    When multiple files share the same combination of detector types,
   412→    that's likely a codebase-wide pattern rather than isolated issues.
   413→    """
   414→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   415→
   416→    # Group files by their judgment detector profile.
   417→    profile_to_files: dict[frozenset[str], list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   418→    for file, issues in by_file.items():
   419→        dets = frozenset(
   420→            f.get("detector", "") for f in issues
   421→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   422→        )
   423→        if len(dets) >= 2:
   424→            profile_to_files[dets].append(file)
   425→
   426→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   427→    for det_combo, files in profile_to_files.items():
   428→        if len(files) < MIN_FILES_FOR_SYSTEMIC:
   429→            continue
   430→
   431→        sorted_files = sorted(files)
   432→        combo_names = tuple(sorted(det_combo))
   433→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(
   434→            f.get("id", "")
   435→            for file in sorted_files
   436→            for f in by_file[file]
   437→            if f.get("detector", "") in det_combo
   438→        ))
   439→        # Use first few files in fingerprint so it's stable but bounded.
   440→        fp = _fingerprint(
   441→            "systemic_pattern",
   442→            ",".join(sorted_files[:5]),
   443→            combo_names,
   444→        )
   445→
   446→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   447→            continue
   448→
   449→        concerns.append(
   450→            Concern(
   451→                type="systemic_pattern",
   452→                file=sorted_files[0],
   453→                summary=(
   454→                    f"{len(files)} files share the same problem pattern "
   455→                    f"({', '.join(combo_names)})"
   456→                ),
   457→                evidence=(
   458→                    f"Affected files: {', '.join(sorted_files[:10])}",
   459→                    f"Shared detectors: {', '.join(combo_names)}",
   460→                    f"Total files: {len(files)}",
   461→                ),
   462→                question=(
   463→                    f"These {len(files)} files all have the same combination "
   464→                    f"of issues ({', '.join(combo_names)}). Is this a systemic "
   465→                    "pattern that should be addressed at the architecture level "
   466→                    "(shared base class, framework change, lint rule), or are "
   467→                    "these independent issues that happen to look similar?"
   468→                ),
   469→                fingerprint=fp,
   470→                source_issues=all_ids,
   471→            )
   472→        )
   473→
   474→    return concerns
   475→
   476→
   477→def _systemic_smell_patterns(
   478→    state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]
   479→) -> list[Concern]:
   480→    """Systemic concerns: single smell_id appearing across 5+ files.
   481→
   482→    Complements _cross_file_patterns which looks at detector-combo profiles.
   483→    This catches pervasive single-smell issues (e.g. broad_except in 12 files).
   484→    """
   485→    smell_files: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   486→    smell_ids_map: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)  # smell_id -> issue IDs
   487→
   488→    for f in _open_issues(state):
   489→        if f.get("detector") != "smells":
   490→            continue
   491→        detail = f.get("detail", {})
   492→        smell_id = detail.get("smell_id", "") if isinstance(detail, dict) else ""
   493→        filepath = f.get("file", "")
   494→        if smell_id and filepath and filepath != ".":
   495→            smell_files[smell_id].append(filepath)
   496→            smell_ids_map[smell_id].append(f.get("id", ""))
   497→
   498→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   499→    for smell_id, files in smell_files.items():
   500→        unique_files = sorted(set(files))
   501→        if len(unique_files) < MIN_FILES_FOR_SMELL_PATTERN:
   502→            continue
   503→
   504→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(smell_ids_map[smell_id]))
   505→        fp = _fingerprint("systemic_smell", smell_id, (smell_id,))
   506→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   507→            continue
   508→
   509→        concerns.append(
   510→            Concern(
   511→                type="systemic_smell",
   512→                file=unique_files[0],
   513→                summary=(
   514→                    f"'{smell_id}' appears in {len(unique_files)} files — "
   515→                    "likely a systemic pattern"
   516→                ),
   517→                evidence=(
   518→                    f"Smell: {smell_id}",
   519→                    f"Affected files ({len(unique_files)}): {', '.join(unique_files[:10])}",
   520→                ),
   521→                question=(
   522→                    f"The smell '{smell_id}' appears across {len(unique_files)} files. "
   523→                    "Is this a codebase-wide convention that should be addressed "
   524→                    "systemically (lint rule, shared utility, architecture change), "
   525→                    "or are these independent occurrences?"
   526→                ),
   527→                fingerprint=fp,
   528→                source_issues=all_ids,
   529→            )
   530→        )
   531→
   532→    return concerns
   533→
   534→
   535→_GENERATORS = [_file_concerns, _cross_file_patterns, _systemic_smell_patterns]
   536→
   537→
   538→def generate_concerns(
   539→    state: StateModel,
   540→) -> list[Concern]:
   541→    """Run all concern generators against current state.
   542→
   543→    Returns deduplicated list sorted by (type, file).
   544→    """
   545→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   546→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   547→    seen_fps: set[str] = set()
   548→
   549→    for gen in _GENERATORS:
   550→        for concern in gen(state, dismissals):
   551→            if concern.fingerprint not in seen_fps:
   552→                seen_fps.add(concern.fingerprint)
   553→                concerns.append(concern)
   554→
   555→    concerns.sort(key=lambda c: (c.type, c.file))
   556→    return concerns
   557→
   558→
   559→def cleanup_stale_dismissals(state: StateModel) -> int:
   560→    """Remove dismissals whose source issues all disappeared.
   561→
   562→    Returns the number of stale entries removed.  Dismissals without
   563→    ``source_issue_ids`` (legacy) are left untouched.
   564→    """
   565→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   566→    if not dismissals:
   567→        return 0
   568→    open_ids = {f.get("id", "") for f in _open_issues(state)}
   569→    stale_fps = [
   570→        fp
   571→        for fp, entry in dismissals.items()
   572→        if entry.get("source_issue_ids")
   573→        and not any(sid in open_ids for sid in entry["source_issue_ids"])
   574→    ]
   575→    for fp in stale_fps:
   576→        del dismissals[fp]
   577→    return len(stale_fps)
   578→
   579→
   580→__all__ = ["Concern", "cleanup_stale_dismissals", "generate_concerns"]
   581→

   150→
   151→    output_format = getattr(args, "format", "terminal")
   152→    if next_output_mod.emit_non_terminal_output(output_format, payload, items):
   153→        return True
   154→    return False

   157→def _plan_queue_context(
   158→    *,
   159→    state: dict,
   160→    plan_data: dict | None,
   161→    context=None,
   162→) -> tuple[float | None, QueueBreakdown | None]:
   163→    effective_plan = context.plan if context is not None else plan_data
   164→    plan_start_strict = get_plan_start_strict(effective_plan)
   165→    try:
   166→        breakdown = plan_aware_queue_breakdown(state, plan_data, context=context)
   167→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   168→        breakdown = None
   169→    return plan_start_strict, breakdown
