```
   171→
   172→def _merge_potentials_safe(raw_potentials: dict | None) -> dict | None:
   173→    try:
   174→        return merge_potentials(raw_potentials) or None
   175→    except (ImportError, TypeError, ValueError):
   176→        return raw_potentials or None
   177→
   178→
   179→def _get_items(args, state: dict, config: dict) -> None:
   180→    count = getattr(args, "count", 1) or 1
   181→    scope = getattr(args, "scope", None)
   182→    status = getattr(args, "status", "open")
   183→    group = getattr(args, "group", "item")
   184→    explain = bool(getattr(args, "explain", False))
   185→    cluster_arg = getattr(args, "cluster", None)
   186→    include_skipped = bool(getattr(args, "include_skipped", False))
   187→
   188→    target_strict = target_strict_score_from_config(config)
   189→
   190→    # Load the living plan
   191→    plan = load_plan()
   192→    plan_data: dict | None = None
   193→    if (
   194→        plan.get("queue_order")
   195→        or plan.get("overrides")
   196→        or plan.get("clusters")
   197→    ):
   198→        plan_data = plan
   199→
   200→    # Build unified context once — all downstream consumers agree on
   201→    # plan, target_strict, and subjective visibility policy.
   202→    ctx = queue_context(
   203→        state, config=config, plan=plan_data, target_strict=target_strict,
   204→    )
   205→
   206→    # Auto-scope to focus cluster if set and no explicit scope/cluster
   207→    effective_cluster = _resolve_cluster_focus(
   208→        plan_data,
   209→        cluster_arg=cluster_arg,
   210→        scope=scope,
   211→    )
   212→
   213→    queue = build_work_queue(
   214→        state,
   215→        options=QueueBuildOptions(
   216→            count=count,
   217→            scope=scope,
   218→            status=status,
   219→            include_subjective=True,
   220→            subjective_threshold=target_strict,
   221→            explain=explain,
   222→            include_skipped=include_skipped,
   223→            cluster=effective_cluster,
   224→            context=ctx,
   225→        ),
   226→    )
   227→    items = queue.get("items", [])
   228→
   229→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
   230→    lang_name = lang.name if lang else None
   231→    narrative = compute_narrative(
   232→        state,
   233→        context=NarrativeContext(lang=lang_name, command="next", plan=plan_data),
   234→    )
   235→
   236→    payload = _build_next_payload(
   237→        queue=queue,
   238→        items=items,
   239→        state=state,
   240→        narrative=narrative,
   241→        plan_data=plan_data,
   242→    )
   243→    write_query(payload)
   244→
   245→    if _emit_requested_output(args, payload, items):
   246→        return
   247→
   248→    dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {})
   249→    issues_scoped = state_mod.path_scoped_issues(
   250→        state.get("issues", {}),
   251→        state.get("scan_path"),
   252→    )
   253→
   254→    # Extract frozen plan-start score and queue breakdown for lifecycle display
   255→    plan_start_strict, breakdown = _plan_queue_context(
   256→        state=state,
   257→        plan_data=plan_data,
   258→        context=ctx,
   259→    )
   260→    queue_total = breakdown.queue_total if breakdown else 0
   261→
   262→    _render_queue_header(queue, explain)
   263→    strict_score = state_mod.score_snapshot(state).strict
   264→    if _show_empty_queue(
   265→        queue,
   266→        strict_score,
   267→        plan_start_strict=plan_start_strict,
   268→        target_strict=target_strict,
   269→    ):
   270→        return
   271→
   272→    raw_potentials = state.get("potentials", {})
   273→    potentials = _merge_potentials_safe(raw_potentials)
   274→    next_render_mod.render_terminal_items(
   275→        items, dim_scores, issues_scoped, group=group, explain=explain,
   276→        potentials=potentials, plan=plan_data,
   277→        cluster_filter=effective_cluster,
   278→    )
   279→    next_nudges_mod.render_single_item_resolution_hint(items)
   280→    next_nudges_mod.render_uncommitted_reminder(plan_data)
   281→    next_nudges_mod.render_followup_nudges(
   282→        state,
   283→        dim_scores,
   284→        issues_scoped,
   285→        strict_score=strict_score,
   286→        target_strict_score=target_strict,
   287→        queue_total=queue_total,
   288→        plan_start_strict=plan_start_strict,
   289→        breakdown=breakdown,
   290→    )
   291→    print()
   292→
   293→
   294→__all__ = ["_low_subjective_dimensions", "cmd_next"]
```

```
477→def _systemic_smell_patterns(
   478→    state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]
   479→) -> list[Concern]:
   480→    """Systemic concerns: single smell_id appearing across 5+ files.
   481→
   482→    Complements _cross_file_patterns which looks at detector-combo profiles.
   483→    This catches pervasive single-smell issues (e.g. broad_except in 12 files).
   484→    """
   485→    smell_files: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   486→    smell_ids_map: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)  # smell_id -> issue IDs
   487→
   488→    for f in _open_issues(state):
   489→        if f.get("detector") != "smells":
   490→            continue
   491→        detail = f.get("detail", {})
   492→        smell_id = detail.get("smell_id", "") if isinstance(detail, dict) else ""
   493→        filepath = f.get("file", "")
   494→        if smell_id and filepath and filepath != ".":
   495→            smell_files[smell_id].append(filepath)
   496→            smell_ids_map[smell_id].append(f.get("id", ""))
   497→
   498→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   499→    for smell_id, files in smell_files.items():
   500→        unique_files = sorted(set(files))
   501→        if len(unique_files) < MIN_FILES_FOR_SMELL_PATTERN:
   502→            continue
   503→
   504→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(smell_ids_map[smell_id]))
   505→        fp = _fingerprint("systemic_smell", smell_id, (smell_id,))
   506→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   507→            continue
   508→
   509→        concerns.append(
   510→            Concern(
   511→                type="systemic_smell",
   512→                file=unique_files[0],
   513→                summary=(
   514→                    f"'{smell_id}' appears in {len(unique_files)} files — "
   515→                    "likely a systemic pattern"
   516→                ),
   517→                evidence=(
   518→                    f"Smell: {smell_id}",
   519→                    f"Affected files ({len(unique_files)}): {', '.join(unique_files[:10])}",
   520→                ),
   521→                question=(
   522→                    f"The smell '{smell_id}' appears across {len(unique_files)} files. "
   523→                    "Is this a codebase-wide convention that should be addressed "
   524→                    "systemically (lint rule, shared utility, architecture change), "
   525→                    "or are these independent occurrences?"
   526→                ),
   527→                fingerprint=fp,
   528→                source_issues=all_ids,
   529→            )
   530→        )
   531→
   532→    return concerns
```

### **1. CONCERN CONSTRUCTION DEDUP (HIGH CONFIDENCE, 20-30 lines saved)**

**Location:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/concerns.py`

**Issue:** Functions `_cross_file_patterns()` (lines 408-474, 67 lines) and `_systemic_smell_patterns()` (lines 477-532, 56 lines) share identical Concern construction pattern:

```python
# Both functions duplicate this ~15-line block:
fingerprint_computed = _fingerprint(...)
if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
    continue

concerns.append(
    Concern(
        type="...",
        file=...,
        summary=(...),
        evidence=(...),
        question=(...),
        fingerprint=fp,
        source_issues=all_ids,
    )
)
```

**Quick Win:** Extract a `_make_concern()` factory function taking concern metadata:
```python
def _make_concern(
    type: str,
    file: str,
    summary: str,
    evidence: tuple[str, ...],
    question: str,
    fingerprint: str,
    source_issues: tuple[str, ...],
) -> Concern:
    return Concern(type=type, file=file, summary=summary, evidence=evidence, question=question, fingerprint=fingerprint, source_issues=source_issues)
```

**Impact:** Eliminates ~20 lines of near-identical boilerplate. Both functions already compute the same fields; the factory just eliminates the repeated Concern constructor call pattern.

**TASK A: Extract _make_concern() factory in concerns.py**

In `desloppify/engine/concerns.py`, functions `_cross_file_patterns()` and `_systemic_smell_patterns()` both duplicate ~15-20 lines of:

Extract a helper that encapsulates the fingerprint→dismiss→construct pattern. Something like:

```python
def _try_make_concern(
    *,
    concern_type: str,
    file: str,
    all_ids: tuple[str, ...],
    signals: dict,
    dismissals: ...,
) -> Concern | None:
    """Compute fingerprint, check dismissal, and construct Concern if not dismissed."""
    fp = _fingerprint(concern_type, file, all_ids)
    if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
        return None
    return Concern(
```

```
    63→def _update_max_signal(signals: ConcernSignals, key: SignalKey, value: object) -> None:

   110→def _parse_complexity_signals(detail: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, float]:
   111→    """Parse complexity_signals strings into numeric values.
   112→
   113→    Structural detail dicts store complexity signals as strings like
   114→    "12 params" and "nesting depth 8" in the ``complexity_signals``
   115→    list.  Extract max_params and max_nesting from those labels so
   116→    the concern generator can evaluate thresholds.
   117→    """
   118→    result: dict[str, float] = {}
   119→    raw_signals = detail.get("complexity_signals", [])
   120→    if not isinstance(raw_signals, list):
   121→        return result
   122→
   123→    for sig in raw_signals:
   124→        if not isinstance(sig, str):
   125→            continue
   126→        m = re.search(r"(\d+)\s*params", sig)
   127→        if m:
   128→            result["max_params"] = max(result.get("max_params", 0), float(m.group(1)))
   129→        m = re.search(r"nesting depth\s*(\d+)", sig)
   130→        if m:
   131→            result["max_nesting"] = max(result.get("max_nesting", 0), float(m.group(1)))
   132→    return result

   135→def _extract_signals(issues: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> ConcernSignals:
   136→    """Extract key quantitative signals from a file's issues."""
   137→    signals: ConcernSignals = {}
   138→    monster_funcs: list[str] = []
   139→
   140→    for f in issues:
   141→        det = f.get("detector", "")
   142→        detail_raw = f.get("detail", {})
   143→        detail = detail_raw if isinstance(detail_raw, dict) else {}
   144→
   145→        if det == "structural":
   146→            # Read loc directly from the flat detail dict.
   147→            _update_max_signal(signals, "loc", detail.get("loc", 0))
   148→            # Parse complexity_signals strings for params/nesting.
   149→            parsed = _parse_complexity_signals(detail)
   150→            for key in ("max_params", "max_nesting"):
   151→                if key in parsed:
   152→                    _update_max_signal(signals, key, parsed[key])
   153→
   154→        if det == "smells" and detail.get("smell_id") == "monster_function":
   155→            _update_max_signal(signals, "monster_loc", detail.get("loc", 0))
   156→            func = detail.get("function", "")
   157→            if isinstance(func, str) and func:
   158→                monster_funcs.append(func)
   159→
   160→    if monster_funcs:
   161→        signals["monster_funcs"] = monster_funcs
   162→    return signals

   165→def _has_elevated_signals(issues: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> bool:

   167→    for f in issues:

   169→        detail_raw = f.get("detail", {})
   170→        detail = detail_raw if isinstance(detail_raw, dict) else {}
   171→
   172→        if det == "structural":

   174→            if detail.get("loc", 0) >= ELEVATED_LOC:
   175→                return True
   176→            # Parse complexity_signals strings.

   179→                return True

   182→
   183→        if det == "smells" and detail.get("smell_id") == "monster_function":

   196→def _classify(detectors: set[str], signals: ConcernSignals) -> str:

   198→    if len(detectors) >= MIN_DETECTORS_FOR_MIXED:
   199→        return "mixed_responsibilities"
   200→    if "dupes" in detectors or "boilerplate_duplication" in detectors:
   201→        return "duplication_design"
   202→    if signals.get("monster_loc", 0) > 0:
   203→        return "structural_complexity"
   204→    if "coupling" in detectors:

   206→    if signals.get("max_params", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_PARAMS:
   207→        return "interface_design"
   208→    if signals.get("max_nesting", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_NESTING:
   209→        return "structural_complexity"
   210→    if "responsibility_cohesion" in detectors:
   211→        return "mixed_responsibilities"
   212→    return "design_concern"

   215→def _build_summary(

   231→            label = f" ({', '.join(funcs[:3])})" if funcs else ""
   232→            parts.append(f"monster function{label}: {int(monster_loc)} lines")
   233→        nesting = signals.get("max_nesting", 0)
   234→        if nesting >= ELEVATED_MAX_NESTING:
   235→            parts.append(f"nesting depth {int(nesting)}")
   236→        params = signals.get("max_params", 0)
   237→        if params >= ELEVATED_MAX_PARAMS:
   238→            parts.append(f"{int(params)} parameters")
   239→        return f"Structural complexity: {', '.join(parts) or 'elevated signals'}"
   240→    if concern_type == "duplication_design":
   241→        return "Duplication pattern — assess if extraction is warranted"
   242→    if concern_type == "coupling_design":
   243→        return "Coupling pattern — assess if boundaries need adjustment"
   244→    if concern_type == "interface_design":
   245→        return f"Interface complexity: {int(signals.get('max_params', 0))} parameters"
   246→    return f"Design signals from {', '.join(sorted(detectors))}"

   351→def _file_concerns(state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   352→    """Per-file design concerns from aggregated mechanical signals.
   353→
   354→    Flags a file if it has 2+ judgment-needed detectors OR a single
   355→    detector with elevated signals (monster function, high params,
   356→    deep nesting, duplication, coupling, mixed responsibilities).
   357→    Bundles ALL issues for that file so the LLM sees the full picture.
   358→    """
   359→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   360→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   361→
   362→    for file, all_issues in by_file.items():
   363→        judgment = [
   364→            f for f in all_issues
   365→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   366→        ]
   367→        if not judgment:
   368→            continue
   369→
   370→        judgment_dets = {f.get("detector", "") for f in judgment}
   371→        elevated = _has_elevated_signals(judgment)
   372→
   373→        # Flag if 2+ judgment detectors OR 1 with elevated signals
   374→        # OR 1 judgment detector + 2 mechanical issues from any detector.
   375→        mechanical_count = len(all_issues)
   376→        if len(judgment_dets) < 2 and not elevated:
   377→            if not (len(judgment_dets) >= 1 and mechanical_count >= 3):
   378→                continue
   379→
   380→        signals = _extract_signals(judgment)
   381→        concern_type = _classify(judgment_dets, signals)
   382→        evidence = _build_evidence(judgment, signals)
   383→        question = _build_question(judgment_dets, signals)
   384→        summary = _build_summary(concern_type, judgment_dets, signals)
   385→
   386→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(f.get("id", "") for f in judgment))
   387→        fp_keys = tuple(sorted(judgment_dets))
   388→        fp = _fingerprint(concern_type, file, fp_keys)
   389→
   390→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   391→            continue
   392→
   393→        concerns.append(
   394→            Concern(
   395→                type=concern_type,
   396→                file=file,
   397→                summary=summary,
   398→                evidence=evidence,
   399→                question=question,
   400→                fingerprint=fp,
   401→                source_issues=all_ids,
   402→            )
   403→        )
   404→
   405→    return concerns
   406→

   408→def _cross_file_patterns(state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   409→    """Systemic patterns: same judgment detector combo across 3+ files.
   410→
   411→    When multiple files share the same combination of detector types,
   412→    that's likely a codebase-wide pattern rather than isolated issues.
   413→    """
   414→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   415→
   416→    # Group files by their judgment detector profile.
   417→    profile_to_files: dict[frozenset[str], list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   418→    for file, issues in by_file.items():
   419→        dets = frozenset(
   420→            f.get("detector", "") for f in issues
   421→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   422→        )
   423→        if len(dets) >= 2:
   424→            profile_to_files[dets].append(file)
   425→
   426→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   427→    for det_combo, files in profile_to_files.items():
   428→        if len(files) < MIN_FILES_FOR_SYSTEMIC:
   429→            continue
   430→
   431→        sorted_files = sorted(files)
   432→        combo_names = tuple(sorted(det_combo))
   433→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(
   434→            f.get("id", "")
   435→            for file in sorted_files
   436→            for f in by_file[file]
   437→            if f.get("detector", "") in det_combo
   438→        ))
   439→        # Use first few files in fingerprint so it's stable but bounded.
   440→        fp = _fingerprint(
   441→            "systemic_pattern",
   442→            ",".join(sorted_files[:5]),
   443→            combo_names,
   444→        )
   445→
   446→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   447→            continue
   448→
   449→        concerns.append(
   450→            Concern(
   451→                type="systemic_pattern",
   452→                file=sorted_files[0],
   453→                summary=(
   454→                    f"{len(files)} files share the same problem pattern "
   455→                    f"({', '.join(combo_names)})"
   456→                ),
   457→                evidence=(
   458→                    f"Affected files: {', '.join(sorted_files[:10])}",
   459→                    f"Shared detectors: {', '.join(combo_names)}",
   460→                    f"Total files: {len(files)}",
   461→                ),
   462→                question=(
   463→                    f"These {len(files)} files all have the same combination "
   464→                    f"of issues ({', '.join(combo_names)}). Is this a systemic "
   465→                    "pattern that should be addressed at the architecture level "
   466→                    "(shared base class, framework change, lint rule), or are "
   467→                    "these independent issues that happen to look similar?"
   468→                ),
   469→                fingerprint=fp,
   470→                source_issues=all_ids,
   471→            )
   472→        )
   473→
   474→    return concerns

   535→_GENERATORS = [_file_concerns, _cross_file_patterns, _systemic_smell_patterns]
   536→
   537→
   538→def generate_concerns(
   539→    state: StateModel,
   540→) -> list[Concern]:
   541→    """Run all concern generators against current state.
   542→
   543→    Returns deduplicated list sorted by (type, file).
   544→    """
   545→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   546→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   547→    seen_fps: set[str] = set()
   548→
   549→    for gen in _GENERATORS:
   550→        for concern in gen(state, dismissals):
   551→            if concern.fingerprint not in seen_fps:
   552→                seen_fps.add(concern.fingerprint)
   553→                concerns.append(concern)
   554→
   555→    concerns.sort(key=lambda c: (c.type, c.file))
   556→    return concerns
   557→
   558→
   559→def cleanup_stale_dismissals(state: StateModel) -> int:
   560→    """Remove dismissals whose source issues all disappeared.
   561→
   562→    Returns the number of stale entries removed.  Dismissals without
   563→    ``source_issue_ids`` (legacy) are left untouched.
   564→    """
   565→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   566→    if not dismissals:
   567→        return 0
   568→    open_ids = {f.get("id", "") for f in _open_issues(state)}
   569→    stale_fps = [
   570→        fp
   571→        for fp, entry in dismissals.items()
   572→        if entry.get("source_issue_ids")
   573→        and not any(sid in open_ids for sid in entry["source_issue_ids"])
   574→    ]
   575→    for fp in stale_fps:
   576→        del dismissals[fp]
   577→    return len(stale_fps)
   578→
   579→
   580→__all__ = ["Concern", "cleanup_stale_dismissals", "generate_concerns"]
```

```
    44→def _scorecard_subjective(

    48→    """Return scorecard-aligned subjective entries for current dimension scores."""

    52→def _low_subjective_dimensions(
    53→    state: dict,
    54→    dim_scores: dict,
    55→    *,
    56→    threshold: float = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    57→) -> list[tuple[str, float, int]]:
    58→    """Return assessed scorecard-subjective entries below the threshold."""
    59→    low: list[tuple[str, float, int]] = []
    60→    for entry in _scorecard_subjective(state, dim_scores):
    61→        if entry.get("placeholder"):

    63→        strict_val = float(entry.get("strict", entry.get("score", 100.0)))

    65→            low.append(
    66→                (
    67→                    str(entry.get("name", "Subjective")),
    68→                    strict_val,
    69→                    int(entry.get("failing", 0)),
    70→                )
    71→            )
    72→    low.sort(key=lambda item: item[1])
    73→    return low
```

```
1→"""Predicates and small utilities for work queue items."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import re
     6→from fnmatch import fnmatch
     7→from typing import Any
     8→
     9→from desloppify.base.enums import issue_status_tokens
    10→from desloppify.base.registry import DETECTORS
    11→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel
    12→
    13→ALL_STATUSES = set(issue_status_tokens(include_all=True))
    14→ACTION_TYPE_PRIORITY = {"auto_fix": 0, "refactor": 1, "manual_fix": 2, "reorganize": 3}
    15→ATTEST_EXAMPLE = (
    16→    "I have actually [DESCRIBE THE CONCRETE CHANGE YOU MADE] "
    17→    "and I am not gaming the score by resolving without fixing."
    18→)
    19→
    20→
    21→def detail_dict(item: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    22→    """Return issue detail as a dict; tolerate legacy/non-dict payloads."""
    23→    detail = item.get("detail")
    24→    return detail if isinstance(detail, dict) else {}
    25→
    26→
    27→def status_matches(item_status: str, status_filter: str) -> bool:
    28→    return status_filter == "all" or item_status == status_filter
    29→
    30→
    31→def is_subjective_issue(item: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    32→    detector = item.get("detector")
    33→    if detector in {"subjective_assessment"}:
    34→        return True
    35→    if detector == "holistic_review":
    36→        return True
    37→    return False
    38→
    39→
    40→def is_review_issue(item: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    41→    return item.get("detector") == "review"
    42→
    43→
    44→def is_subjective_queue_item(item: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    45→    """True for subjective work items, including collapsed subjective clusters."""
    46→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
    47→        return True
    48→    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
    49→        members = item.get("members", [])
    50→        return bool(members) and all(
    51→            m.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension" for m in members
    52→        )
    53→    return False
    54→
    55→
    56→def review_issue_weight(item: dict[str, Any]) -> float:
    57→    """Return review issue weight aligned with issues list ordering."""
    58→    confidence = str(item.get("confidence", "low")).lower()
    59→    weight_by_confidence = {
    60→        "high": 1.0,
    61→        "medium": 0.7,
    62→        "low": 0.3,
    63→    }
    64→    weight = weight_by_confidence.get(confidence, 0.3)
    65→    if detail_dict(item).get("holistic"):
    66→        weight *= 10.0
    67→    return float(weight)
    68→
    69→
    70→def scope_matches(item: dict[str, Any], scope: str | None) -> bool:
    71→    """Apply show-style pattern matching against a queue item."""
    72→    if not scope:
    73→        return True
    74→
    75→    item_id = item.get("id", "")
    76→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
    77→    filepath = item.get("file", "")
    78→    summary = item.get("summary", "")
    79→    dimension = detail_dict(item).get("dimension_name", "")
    80→    kind = item.get("kind", "")
    81→
    82→    if "*" in scope:
    83→        return any(
    84→            fnmatch(candidate, scope)
    85→            for candidate in (item_id, filepath, detector, dimension, summary)
    86→        )
    87→
    88→    if "::" in scope:
    89→        return item_id.startswith(scope)
    90→
    91→    lowered = scope.lower()
    92→    if kind == "subjective_dimension":
    93→        return (
    94→            lowered in item_id.lower()
    95→            or lowered in dimension.lower()
    96→            or lowered in summary.lower()
    97→        )
    98→
    99→    # Hash suffix: 8+ hex chars matches the tail segment of a issue ID.
   100→    if len(lowered) >= 8 and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]+", lowered):
   101→        return item_id.lower().endswith("::" + lowered)
   102→
   103→    return (
   104→        detector == scope
   105→        or filepath == scope
   106→        or filepath.startswith(scope.rstrip("/") + "/")
   107→    )
   108→
   109→
   110→def slugify(text: str) -> str:
   111→    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]+", "_", text.lower()).strip("_")
   112→
   113→
   114→def supported_fixers_for_item(
   115→    state: StateModel, item: dict[str, Any]
   116→) -> set[str] | None:
   117→    """Return supported fixers for an item's language when known."""
   118→    lang = str(item.get("lang", "") or "").strip()
   119→    if not lang:
   120→        return None
   121→
   122→    caps = state.get("lang_capabilities", {})
   123→    if not isinstance(caps, dict):
   124→        return None
   125→
   126→    lang_caps = caps.get(lang, {})
   127→    if not isinstance(lang_caps, dict):
   128→        return None
   129→
   130→    fixers = lang_caps.get("fixers")
   131→    if not isinstance(fixers, list):
   132→        return None
   133→    return {fixer for fixer in fixers if isinstance(fixer, str)}
   134→
   135→
   136→def primary_command_for_issue(
   137→    item: dict[str, Any], *, supported_fixers: set[str] | None = None
   138→) -> str:
   139→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
   140→    meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   141→    if meta and meta.action_type == "auto_fix" and meta.fixers:
   142→        available_fixers = [
   143→            fixer
   144→            for fixer in meta.fixers
   145→            if supported_fixers is not None and fixer in supported_fixers
   146→        ]
   147→        if available_fixers:
   148→            return f"desloppify autofix {available_fixers[0]} --dry-run"
   149→    if detector == "subjective_review":
   150→        from desloppify.intelligence.integrity import (
   151→            is_holistic_subjective_issue,  # cycle-break: helpers.py ↔ integrity.py
   152→        )
   153→
   154→        if is_holistic_subjective_issue(item):
   155→            return "desloppify review --prepare"
   156→        return "desloppify show subjective"
   157→    return f'desloppify plan resolve "{item.get("id", "")}" --note "<what you did>" --confirm'
   158→
   159→
   160→__all__ = [
   161→    "ALL_STATUSES",
   162→    "ATTEST_EXAMPLE",
   163→    "detail_dict",
   164→    "is_review_issue",
   165→    "is_subjective_issue",
   166→    "is_subjective_queue_item",
   167→    "primary_command_for_issue",
   168→    "review_issue_weight",
   169→    "scope_matches",
   170→    "slugify",
   171→    "status_matches",
   172→    "supported_fixers_for_item",
   173→]
   174→
```

```
    13→def add_structural_signal(structural: dict, file: str, signal: str, detail: dict):
    14→    """Add a complexity signal to the per-file structural dict.
    15→
    16→    Accumulates signals per file so they can be merged into tiered issues.
    17→    """
    18→    f = resolve_path(file)
    19→    structural.setdefault(f, {"signals": [], "detail": {}})
    20→    structural[f]["signals"].append(signal)
    21→    structural[f]["detail"].update(detail)
    22→
    23→
    24→def merge_structural_signals(
    25→    structural: dict,
    26→    stderr_fn,
    27→    *,
    28→    complexity_only_min: int = 35,
    29→) -> list[Issue]:
    30→    """Convert per-file structural signals into tiered issues.
    31→
    32→    3+ signals -> T4/high (needs decomposition).
    33→    1-2 signals -> T3/medium.
    34→    Complexity-only files (no large/god signals) need score >= complexity_only_min
    35→    to be flagged — lower complexity in small files is normal, not decomposition-worthy.
    36→    """
    37→    results = []
    38→    suppressed = 0
    39→    for filepath, data in structural.items():
    40→        if "loc" not in data["detail"]:
    41→            try:
    42→                p = (
    43→                    Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else get_project_root() / filepath
    44→                )
    45→                data["detail"]["loc"] = count_lines(p)
    46→            except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
    47→                data["detail"]["loc"] = 0
    48→
    49→        # Suppress complexity-only issues below the elevated threshold.
    50→        signals = data["signals"]
    51→        is_complexity_only = all(s.startswith("complexity") for s in signals)
    52→        if is_complexity_only:
    53→            score = data["detail"].get("complexity_score", 0)
    54→            if score < complexity_only_min:
    55→                suppressed += 1
    56→                continue
    57→
    58→        signal_count = len(signals)
    59→        tier = 4 if signal_count >= 3 else 3
    60→        confidence = "high" if signal_count >= 3 else "medium"
    61→        summary = "Needs decomposition: " + " / ".join(signals)
    62→        results.append(
    63→            make_issue(
    64→                "structural",
    65→                filepath,
    66→                "",
    67→                tier=tier,
    68→                confidence=confidence,
    69→                summary=summary,
    70→                detail=data["detail"],
    71→            )
    72→        )
    73→    if suppressed:
    74→        stderr_fn(
    75→            "         "
    76→            f"{suppressed} complexity-only files below threshold (< {complexity_only_min})"
    77→        )
    78→    stderr_fn(f"         -> {len(results)} structural issues")
    79→    return results
    80→
    81→
    82→__all__ = ["add_structural_signal", "merge_structural_signals"]
    83→
```

```
   192→def make_smell_issues(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[Issue]:
   193→    """Group smell entries by file and assign tiers from severity.
   194→
   195→    Input: list of smell dicts from detect_smells, each with id/label/severity/matches.
   196→    Output: issues grouped per (file, smell_id).
   197→    """
   198→    results = []
   199→    for e in entries:
   200→        by_file: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
   201→        for m in e["matches"]:
   202→            by_file[m["file"]].append(m)
   203→        for file, matches in by_file.items():
   204→            conf = "medium" if e["severity"] != "low" else "low"
   205→            tier = SMELL_TIER_MAP.get(e["severity"], 3)
   206→            results.append(
   207→                make_issue(
   208→                    "smells",
   209→                    file,
   210→                    e["id"],

   212→                    confidence=conf,
```

```
1→"""Coupling analysis: boundary violations and boundary candidates.
     2→
     3→These detect architectural violations in codebases with shared/tools structure.
     4→The algorithms work on any dep graph — the boundary definitions (what prefixes
     5→constitute "shared" vs "tools") are provided by the caller.

    19→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    20→class CouplingEdgeCounts:
    21→    """Explicit coupling-edge counters.
    22→
    23→    `eligible_edges` tracks the denominator universe for a detector.
    24→    `violating_edges` tracks only edges that violate the rule.
    25→    """
    26→
    27→    violating_edges: int = 0
    28→    eligible_edges: int = 0
    29→
    30→
    31→def _norm_path(path: str) -> str:
    32→    """Normalize path separators for cross-platform prefix matching."""
    33→    return path.replace("\\", "/")
    34→
    35→
    36→def _norm_prefix(prefix: str, *, name: str) -> str:
    37→    """Normalize a directory prefix and ensure trailing slash."""
    38→    p = _norm_path(str(prefix).strip())
    39→    if not p:
    40→        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-empty directory prefix")
    41→    return p if p.endswith("/") else p + "/"
    42→
    43→
    44→def _norm_root(path: Path) -> str:
    45→    """Normalize project root path for absolute/relative prefix matching."""
    46→    try:
    47→        root = _norm_path(str(path.resolve()))
    48→    except OSError:
    49→        root = _norm_path(str(path))
    50→    return root if root.endswith("/") else root + "/"
    51→
    52→
    53→def _rel_to_root(value: str, root_norm: str) -> str:
    54→    """Return root-relative variant (best effort) for path/prefix matching."""
    55→    if value.startswith(root_norm):
    56→        return value[len(root_norm) :]
    57→    return value.lstrip("/")
    58→
    59→
    60→def _matches_prefix(value: str, prefix: str, *, root_norm: str) -> bool:
    61→    """Match value against prefix regardless of abs/rel shape."""
    62→    if value.startswith(prefix):
    63→        return True
    64→    return _rel_to_root(value, root_norm).startswith(_rel_to_root(prefix, root_norm))
    65→
    66→
    67→def _strip_prefix(value: str, prefix: str, *, root_norm: str) -> str:
    68→    """Strip prefix from value while tolerating abs/rel shape differences."""
    69→    if value.startswith(prefix):
    70→        return value[len(prefix) :]
    71→    value_rel = _rel_to_root(value, root_norm)
    72→    prefix_rel = _rel_to_root(prefix, root_norm)
    73→    if value_rel.startswith(prefix_rel):
    74→        return value_rel[len(prefix_rel) :]
    75→    return value
    76→
    77→
    78→def detect_coupling_violations(
    79→    path: Path, graph: dict, shared_prefix: str, tools_prefix: str
    80→) -> tuple[list[dict], CouplingEdgeCounts]:
    81→    """Find files in shared/ that import from tools/ (backwards coupling)."""
    82→    shared_prefix_norm = _norm_prefix(shared_prefix, name="shared_prefix")
    83→    tools_prefix_norm = _norm_prefix(tools_prefix, name="tools_prefix")
    84→    root_norm = _norm_root(path)

    86→    violating_edges = 0

    95→            if _matches_prefix(target_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
    96→                violating_edges += 1
    97→                eligible_edges += 1
    98→                remainder = _strip_prefix(
    99→                    target_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm
   100→                )
   101→                tool = remainder.split("/")[0] if "/" in remainder else remainder
   102→                entries.append(

   111→                eligible_edges += 1
   112→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: (e["file"], e["target"])), CouplingEdgeCounts(
   113→        violating_edges=violating_edges,

   115→    )
   116→
   117→
   118→def detect_boundary_candidates(
   119→    path: Path,
   120→    graph: dict,
   121→    shared_prefix: str,
   122→    tools_prefix: str,
   123→    skip_basenames: set[str] | None = None,
   124→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   125→    """Find shared/ files whose importers ALL come from a single tool."""
   126→    shared_prefix_norm = _norm_prefix(shared_prefix, name="shared_prefix")
   127→    tools_prefix_norm = _norm_prefix(tools_prefix, name="tools_prefix")
   128→    root_norm = _norm_root(path)
   129→    ui_prefix_norm = shared_prefix_norm + "components/ui/"
   130→
   131→    total_shared = 0
   132→    entries = []
   133→    skip_basenames = skip_basenames or set()
   134→    for filepath, entry in graph.items():
   135→        filepath_norm = _norm_path(filepath)
   136→        if not _matches_prefix(filepath_norm, shared_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
   137→            continue
   138→        total_shared += 1
   139→        basename = Path(filepath).name
   140→        if basename in skip_basenames:
   141→            continue
   142→        if _matches_prefix(filepath_norm, ui_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
   143→            continue
   144→        if entry["importer_count"] == 0:
   145→            continue
   146→
   147→        tool_areas = set()
   148→        has_non_tool_importer = False
   149→        for imp in entry["importers"]:
   150→            imp_norm = _norm_path(imp)
   151→            if _matches_prefix(imp_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
   152→                remainder = _strip_prefix(
   153→                    imp_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm
   154→                )
   155→                tool = remainder.split("/")[0]
   156→                tool_areas.add(tool)
   157→            else:
   158→                has_non_tool_importer = True
   159→
   160→        if len(tool_areas) == 1 and not has_non_tool_importer:
   161→            try:
   162→                resolved = resolve_scan_file(filepath, scan_root=path)
   163→                if not resolved.exists():
   164→                    raise FileNotFoundError(resolved)
   165→                loc = count_lines(resolved)
   166→            except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
   167→                log_best_effort_failure(

   171→                )
   172→                continue
   173→            entries.append(
   174→                {

   176→                    "sole_tool": f"src/tools/{list(tool_areas)[0]}",
   177→                    "importer_count": entry["importer_count"],
   178→                    "loc": loc,
   179→                }
   180→            )
   181→
   182→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["loc"]), total_shared

   185→def detect_cross_tool_imports(
   186→    path: Path, graph: dict, tools_prefix: str
   187→) -> tuple[list[dict], CouplingEdgeCounts]:

   192→    violating_edges = 0

   196→        filepath_norm = _norm_path(filepath)
   197→        if not _matches_prefix(filepath_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
   198→            continue
   199→        remainder = _strip_prefix(filepath_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm)
   200→        if "/" not in remainder:

   203→        for target in entry["imports"]:

   207→            target_tool = _strip_prefix(

   218→                        "target_tool": target_tool,
   219→                        "direction": "tools→tools",
   220→                    }

   222→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: (e["source_tool"], e["file"])), CouplingEdgeCounts(
```

```
    46→class NextOptions:

    59→    @classmethod

    75→def _scorecard_subjective(
    76→    state: dict,
    77→    dim_scores: dict,
    78→) -> list[dict]:
    79→    """Return scorecard-aligned subjective entries for current dimension scores."""
    80→    return _scorecard_subjective_impl(state, dim_scores)

    82→
    83→def _low_subjective_dimensions(
    84→    state: dict,
    85→    dim_scores: dict,
    86→    *,
    87→    threshold: float = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    88→) -> list[tuple[str, float, int]]:
    89→    """Return assessed scorecard-subjective entries below the threshold."""
    90→    low: list[tuple[str, float, int]] = []
    91→    for entry in _scorecard_subjective(state, dim_scores):
    92→        if entry.get("placeholder"):
    93→            continue
    94→        strict_val = float(entry.get("strict", entry.get("score", 100.0)))
    95→        if strict_val < threshold:
    96→            low.append(
    97→                (
    98→                    str(entry.get("name", "Subjective")),
    99→                    strict_val,
   100→                    int(entry.get("failing", 0)),
   101→                )
   102→            )
   103→    low.sort(key=lambda item: item[1])
   104→    return low

   107→def cmd_next(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   108→    """Show next highest-priority queue items."""
   109→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   110→    state = runtime.state
   111→    config = runtime.config
   112→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   113→        return
   114→
   115→    skill_warning = check_skill_version()
   116→    if skill_warning:
   117→        print(colorize(f"  {skill_warning}", "yellow"))
   118→    config_warning = check_config_staleness(config)
   119→    if config_warning:
   120→        print(colorize(f"  {config_warning}", "yellow"))
   121→
   122→    print_triage_guardrail_info(state=state)
   123→    _get_items(args, state, config)
   124→
   125→
   126→def _resolve_cluster_focus(
   127→    plan_data: dict | None,
   128→    *,
   129→    cluster_arg: str | None,
   130→    scope: str | None,
   131→) -> str | None:
   132→    effective_cluster = cluster_arg
   133→    if plan_data and not cluster_arg and not scope:
   134→        active_cluster = plan_data.get("active_cluster")
   135→        if active_cluster:
   136→            effective_cluster = active_cluster
   137→    return effective_cluster
   138→
   139→
   140→def _build_next_payload(
   141→    *,
   142→    queue: dict,
   143→    items: list[dict],
   144→    state: dict,
   145→    narrative: dict,
   146→    plan_data: dict | None,
   147→) -> dict:
   148→    payload = next_output_mod.build_query_payload(
   149→        queue, items, command="next", narrative=narrative, plan=plan_data
   150→    )
   151→    scores = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
   152→    payload["overall_score"] = scores.overall
   153→    payload["objective_score"] = scores.objective
   154→    payload["strict_score"] = scores.strict
   155→    payload["scorecard_dimensions"] = scorecard_dimensions_payload(
   156→        state,
   157→        dim_scores=state.get("dimension_scores", {}),
   158→    )
   159→    payload["subjective_measures"] = [
   160→        row for row in payload["scorecard_dimensions"] if row.get("subjective")
   161→    ]
   162→    return payload
   163→
   164→
   165→def _emit_requested_output(
   166→    opts: NextOptions,
   167→    payload: dict,
   168→    items: list[dict],
   169→) -> bool:
   170→    if opts.output_file:
   171→        if next_output_mod.write_output_file(
   172→            opts.output_file,
   173→            payload,
   174→            len(items),
   175→            safe_write_text_fn=safe_write_text,
   176→            colorize_fn=colorize,
   177→        ):
   178→            return True
   179→        raise SystemExit(1)
   180→
   181→    if next_output_mod.emit_non_terminal_output(opts.output_format, payload, items):
   182→        return True
   183→    return False
   184→
   185→
   186→def _plan_queue_context(
   187→    *,
   188→    state: dict,
   189→    plan_data: dict | None,
   190→    context=None,
   191→) -> tuple[float | None, QueueBreakdown | None]:
   192→    effective_plan = context.plan if context is not None else plan_data
   193→    plan_start_strict = get_plan_start_strict(effective_plan)
   194→    try:
   195→        breakdown = plan_aware_queue_breakdown(state, plan_data, context=context)
   196→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   197→        breakdown = None
   198→    return plan_start_strict, breakdown
   199→
   200→
   201→def _merge_potentials_safe(raw_potentials: dict | None) -> dict | None:
   202→    try:
   203→        return merge_potentials(raw_potentials) or None
   204→    except (ImportError, TypeError, ValueError):
   205→        return raw_potentials or None
   206→
   207→
   208→def _get_items(args: argparse.Namespace, state: dict, config: dict) -> None:
   209→    opts = NextOptions.from_args(args)
   210→
   211→    target_strict = target_strict_score_from_config(config)
   212→
   213→    # Load the living plan
   214→    plan = load_plan()
   215→    plan_data: dict | None = None
   216→    if (
   217→        plan.get("queue_order")
   218→        or plan.get("overrides")
   219→        or plan.get("clusters")
   220→    ):
   221→        plan_data = plan
   222→
   223→    # Build unified context once — all downstream consumers agree on
   224→    # plan, target_strict, and subjective visibility policy.
   225→    ctx = queue_context(
   226→        state, config=config, plan=plan_data, target_strict=target_strict,
   227→    )
   228→
   229→    # Auto-scope to focus cluster if set and no explicit scope/cluster
   230→    effective_cluster = _resolve_cluster_focus(
   231→        plan_data,
   232→        cluster_arg=opts.cluster,
   233→        scope=opts.scope,
   234→    )
   235→
   236→    queue = build_work_queue(
   237→        state,
   238→        options=QueueBuildOptions(
   239→            count=opts.count,
   240→            scope=opts.scope,
   241→            status=opts.status,
   242→            include_subjective=True,
   243→            subjective_threshold=target_strict,
   244→            explain=opts.explain,
   245→            include_skipped=opts.include_skipped,
   246→            cluster=effective_cluster,
   247→            context=ctx,
   248→        ),
   249→    )
   250→    items = queue.get("items", [])
   251→
   252→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
   253→    lang_name = lang.name if lang else None
   254→    narrative = compute_narrative(
   255→        state,
   256→        context=NarrativeContext(lang=lang_name, command="next", plan=plan_data),
   257→    )
   258→
   259→    payload = _build_next_payload(
   260→        queue=queue,
   261→        items=items,
   262→        state=state,
   263→        narrative=narrative,
   264→        plan_data=plan_data,
   265→    )
   266→    write_query(payload)
   267→
   268→    if _emit_requested_output(opts, payload, items):
   269→        return
   270→
   271→    dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {})
   272→    issues_scoped = state_mod.path_scoped_issues(
   273→        state.get("issues", {}),
   274→        state.get("scan_path"),
   275→    )
   276→
   277→    # Extract frozen plan-start score and queue breakdown for lifecycle display
   278→    plan_start_strict, breakdown = _plan_queue_context(
   279→        state=state,
   280→        plan_data=plan_data,
   281→        context=ctx,
   282→    )
   283→    queue_total = breakdown.queue_total if breakdown else 0
   284→
   285→    _render_queue_header(queue, opts.explain)
   286→    strict_score = state_mod.score_snapshot(state).strict
   287→    if _show_empty_queue(
   288→        queue,
   289→        strict_score,
   290→        plan_start_strict=plan_start_strict,
   291→        target_strict=target_strict,
   292→    ):
   293→        return
   294→
   295→    raw_potentials = state.get("potentials", {})
   296→    potentials = _merge_potentials_safe(raw_potentials)
   297→    next_render_mod.render_terminal_items(
   298→        items, dim_scores, issues_scoped, group=opts.group, explain=opts.explain,
   299→        potentials=potentials, plan=plan_data,
   300→        cluster_filter=effective_cluster,
   301→    )
   302→    next_nudges_mod.render_single_item_resolution_hint(items)
   303→    next_nudges_mod.render_uncommitted_reminder(plan_data)
   304→    next_nudges_mod.render_followup_nudges(

   308→        strict_score=strict_score,

   310→        queue_total=queue_total,
   311→        plan_start_strict=plan_start_strict,
   312→        breakdown=breakdown,
   313→    )
```

Here is a summary of what was done in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/next/cmd.py`:

**Added `from dataclasses import dataclass`** to the imports (line 6).

**Defined `NextOptions` frozen dataclass** (lines 45-72) with all 9 fields that were previously scattered as `getattr` calls:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NextOptions:
    """All user-facing options for the ``next`` command, extracted once."""

    count: int = 1
    scope: str | None = None
    status: str = "open"
    group: str = "item"
    explain: bool = False
    cluster: str | None = None
    include_skipped: bool = False
    output_file: str | None = None
    output_format: str = "terminal"

    @classmethod
    def from_args(cls, args: argparse.Namespace) -> NextOptions:
        """Build from an argparse Namespace, applying defaults for missing attrs."""
        return cls(
            count=getattr(args, "count", 1) or 1,
            scope=getattr(args, "scope", None),
            status=getattr(args, "status", "open"),
            group=getattr(args, "group", "item"),
            explain=bool(getattr(args, "explain", False)),
            cluster=getattr(args, "cluster", None),
            include_skipped=bool(getattr(args, "include_skipped", False)),
            output_file=getattr(args, "output", None),
            output_format=getattr(args, "format", "terminal"),
        )
```

**Refactored `_get_items`** to create `opts = NextOptions.from_args(args)` once at the top, then use `opts.count`, `opts.scope`, `opts.status`, `opts.group`, `opts.explain`, `opts.cluster`, `opts.include_skipped` throughout.

**Refactored `_emit_requested_output`** to accept `opts: NextOptions` instead of raw `args`, using `opts.output_file` and `opts.output_format` directly instead of doing its own `getattr` calls.

**Updated `__all__`** to include `"NextOptions"`.

All `getattr` calls now live exclusively inside `NextOptions.from_args()`. The rest of the module references typed, documented fields on the frozen dataclass. Test result: **4056 passed, 3 skipped**.

Now let me carefully analyze the duplication patterns in `_cross_file_patterns()` and `_systemic_smell_patterns()`. Also re-read the `_file_concerns()` to see if it can benefit too.

Looking at the three functions:

**`_file_concerns()`** (lines 351-405): Builds all_ids from judgment issues, computes fp_keys from sorted detector names, then calls `_fingerprint`, `_is_dismissed`, and constructs `Concern`. However, it builds `evidence`, `question`, and `summary` BEFORE the fingerprint check. This means we'd either have to compute those eagerly (wasted work if dismissed) or restructure. The user's request says "the two generator functions" referring to `_cross_file_patterns` and `_systemic_smell_patterns`, so we focus there.

**`_cross_file_patterns()`** (lines 408-474): The pattern is:
1. Compute `all_ids`
2. `fp = _fingerprint("systemic_pattern", file_key, combo_names)`
3. `if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids): continue`
4. Construct `Concern(type=..., file=..., summary=..., evidence=..., question=..., fingerprint=fp, source_issues=all_ids)`

**`_systemic_smell_patterns()`** (lines 477-532): Same pattern:
1. Compute `all_ids`
2. `fp = _fingerprint("systemic_smell", smell_id, (smell_id,))`
3. `if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids): continue`
4. Construct `Concern(type=..., file=..., summary=..., evidence=..., question=..., fingerprint=fp, source_issues=all_ids)`

And `_file_concerns()` (lines 351-405):
1. Compute `all_ids`, `fp_keys`
2. `fp = _fingerprint(concern_type, file, fp_keys)`
3. `if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids): continue`
4. Construct `Concern(...)`

All three share the exact same fingerprint -> dismiss -> construct pattern! The only difference is that `_file_concerns` computes summary/evidence/question before the check (which is actually fine -- we can still pass them in).

```
    63→def _update_max_signal(signals: ConcernSignals, key: SignalKey, value: object) -> None:
    64→    """Update numeric signal key with max(existing, value) when value is valid."""
    65→    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int | float) or value <= 0:
    66→        return
    67→    current = float(signals.get(key, 0.0))
    68→    signals[key] = max(current, float(value))

    71→def _fingerprint(concern_type: str, file: str, key_signals: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:

    73→    raw = f"{concern_type}::{file}::{','.join(sorted(key_signals))}"
    74→    return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

   110→def _parse_complexity_signals(detail: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, float]:
   111→    """Parse complexity_signals strings into numeric values.
   112→
   113→    Structural detail dicts store complexity signals as strings like
   114→    "12 params" and "nesting depth 8" in the ``complexity_signals``
   115→    list.  Extract max_params and max_nesting from those labels so
   116→    the concern generator can evaluate thresholds.
   117→    """
   118→    result: dict[str, float] = {}
   119→    raw_signals = detail.get("complexity_signals", [])
   120→    if not isinstance(raw_signals, list):
   121→        return result
   122→
   123→    for sig in raw_signals:
   124→        if not isinstance(sig, str):
   125→            continue
   126→        m = re.search(r"(\d+)\s*params", sig)
   127→        if m:
   128→            result["max_params"] = max(result.get("max_params", 0), float(m.group(1)))
   129→        m = re.search(r"nesting depth\s*(\d+)", sig)
   130→        if m:
   131→            result["max_nesting"] = max(result.get("max_nesting", 0), float(m.group(1)))
   132→    return result

   135→def _extract_signals(issues: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> ConcernSignals:
   136→    """Extract key quantitative signals from a file's issues."""
   137→    signals: ConcernSignals = {}
   138→    monster_funcs: list[str] = []
   139→
   140→    for f in issues:

   142→        detail_raw = f.get("detail", {})
   143→        detail = detail_raw if isinstance(detail_raw, dict) else {}
   144→
   145→        if det == "structural":

   147→            _update_max_signal(signals, "loc", detail.get("loc", 0))
   148→            # Parse complexity_signals strings for params/nesting.
   149→            parsed = _parse_complexity_signals(detail)
   150→            for key in ("max_params", "max_nesting"):
   151→                if key in parsed:
   152→                    _update_max_signal(signals, key, parsed[key])
   153→
   154→        if det == "smells" and detail.get("smell_id") == "monster_function":
   155→            _update_max_signal(signals, "monster_loc", detail.get("loc", 0))
   156→            func = detail.get("function", "")
   157→            if isinstance(func, str) and func:
   158→                monster_funcs.append(func)

   283→def _try_make_concern(
   284→    *,
   285→    concern_type: str,
   286→    file: str,
   287→    fp_keys: tuple[str, ...],
   288→    all_ids: tuple[str, ...],
   289→    dismissals: dict,
   290→    summary: str,
   291→    evidence: tuple[str, ...],
   292→    question: str,
   293→    fp_file: str | None = None,
   294→) -> Concern | None:
   295→    """Compute fingerprint, check dismissal, and construct Concern if not dismissed.
   296→
   297→    Encapsulates the shared fingerprint -> dismiss -> construct pattern used by
   298→    all three concern generators.
   299→
   300→    ``fp_file`` overrides the file string used in the fingerprint hash when it

   302→    joined file list for fingerprint stability but report the first file).

   305→    if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   306→        return None
   307→    return Concern(
   308→        type=concern_type,
   309→        file=file,
   310→        summary=summary,

   312→        question=question,
   313→        fingerprint=fp,

   318→def _build_question(
   319→    detectors: set[str], signals: ConcernSignals
   320→) -> str:
   321→    """Build targeted question from dominant signals."""
   322→    parts: list[str] = []
   323→
   324→    if len(detectors) >= MIN_DETECTORS_FOR_MIXED:
   325→        parts.append(
   326→            f"This file has issues across {len(detectors)} dimensions "
   327→            f"({', '.join(sorted(detectors))}). Is it trying to do too many "
   328→            "things, or is this complexity inherent to its domain?"
   329→        )
   330→
   331→    funcs = signals.get("monster_funcs", [])
   332→    if funcs:
   333→        parts.append(
   334→            f"What are the distinct responsibilities in {funcs[0]}()? "
   335→            "Should it be decomposed into focused functions?"
   336→        )
   337→
   338→    if signals.get("max_params", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_PARAMS:
   339→        parts.append(
   340→            "Should the parameters be grouped into a config/context object? "
   341→            "Which ones belong together?"
   342→        )
   343→
   344→    if signals.get("max_nesting", 0) >= ELEVATED_MAX_NESTING:
   345→        parts.append(
   346→            "Can the nesting be reduced with early returns, guard clauses, "
   347→            "or extraction into helper functions?"
   348→        )
   349→
   350→    if "dupes" in detectors or "boilerplate_duplication" in detectors:
   351→        parts.append(
   352→            "Is the duplication worth extracting into a shared utility, "
   353→            "or is it intentional variation?"
   354→        )
   355→
   356→    if "coupling" in detectors:
   357→        parts.append(
   358→            "Is the coupling intentional or does it indicate a missing "
   359→            "abstraction boundary?"
   360→        )
   361→
   362→    if "orphaned" in detectors:
   363→        parts.append(
   364→            "Is this file truly dead, or is it used via a non-import mechanism "
   365→            "(dynamic import, CLI entry point, plugin)?"
   366→        )
   367→
   368→    if "responsibility_cohesion" in detectors:

   370→            "What are the distinct responsibilities? Should this module be "
   371→            "split along those lines?"
   372→        )

   374→    if not parts:

   376→            "Review the flagged patterns — are they design problems that "

   384→
   385→
   386→def _file_concerns(state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   387→    """Per-file design concerns from aggregated mechanical signals.
   388→
   389→    Flags a file if it has 2+ judgment-needed detectors OR a single
   390→    detector with elevated signals (monster function, high params,
   391→    deep nesting, duplication, coupling, mixed responsibilities).
   392→    Bundles ALL issues for that file so the LLM sees the full picture.
   393→    """
   394→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   395→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   396→
   397→    for file, all_issues in by_file.items():
   398→        judgment = [
   399→            f for f in all_issues
   400→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   401→        ]
   402→        if not judgment:
   403→            continue
   404→
   405→        judgment_dets = {f.get("detector", "") for f in judgment}
   406→        elevated = _has_elevated_signals(judgment)
   407→
   408→        # Flag if 2+ judgment detectors OR 1 with elevated signals
   409→        # OR 1 judgment detector + 2 mechanical issues from any detector.
   410→        mechanical_count = len(all_issues)
   411→        if len(judgment_dets) < 2 and not elevated:
   412→            if not (len(judgment_dets) >= 1 and mechanical_count >= 3):
   413→                continue
   414→
   415→        signals = _extract_signals(judgment)
   416→        concern_type = _classify(judgment_dets, signals)
   417→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(f.get("id", "") for f in judgment))
   418→        fp_keys = tuple(sorted(judgment_dets))
   419→
   420→        concern = _try_make_concern(
   421→            concern_type=concern_type,
   422→            file=file,
   423→            fp_keys=fp_keys,
   424→            all_ids=all_ids,
   425→            dismissals=dismissals,
   426→            summary=_build_summary(concern_type, judgment_dets, signals),
   427→            evidence=_build_evidence(judgment, signals),
   428→            question=_build_question(judgment_dets, signals),
   429→        )
   430→        if concern is not None:
   431→            concerns.append(concern)
   432→
   433→    return concerns
   434→
   435→
   436→def _cross_file_patterns(state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   437→    """Systemic patterns: same judgment detector combo across 3+ files.
   438→
   439→    When multiple files share the same combination of detector types,
   440→    that's likely a codebase-wide pattern rather than isolated issues.
   441→    """
   442→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   443→
   444→    # Group files by their judgment detector profile.
   445→    profile_to_files: dict[frozenset[str], list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   446→    for file, issues in by_file.items():
   447→        dets = frozenset(
   448→            f.get("detector", "") for f in issues
   449→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   450→        )
   451→        if len(dets) >= 2:
   452→            profile_to_files[dets].append(file)
   453→
   454→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   455→    for det_combo, files in profile_to_files.items():
   456→        if len(files) < MIN_FILES_FOR_SYSTEMIC:
   457→            continue
   458→
   459→        sorted_files = sorted(files)
   460→        combo_names = tuple(sorted(det_combo))
   461→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(
   462→            f.get("id", "")
   463→            for file in sorted_files
   464→            for f in by_file[file]
   465→            if f.get("detector", "") in det_combo
   466→        ))
   467→        # Use first few files in fingerprint so it's stable but bounded.
   468→        concern = _try_make_concern(
   469→            concern_type="systemic_pattern",
   470→            file=sorted_files[0],
   471→            fp_file=",".join(sorted_files[:5]),
   472→            fp_keys=combo_names,
   473→            all_ids=all_ids,
   474→            dismissals=dismissals,
   475→            summary=(
   476→                f"{len(files)} files share the same problem pattern "
   477→                f"({', '.join(combo_names)})"
   478→            ),
   479→            evidence=(
   480→                f"Affected files: {', '.join(sorted_files[:10])}",
   481→                f"Shared detectors: {', '.join(combo_names)}",
   482→                f"Total files: {len(files)}",
   483→            ),
   484→            question=(
   485→                f"These {len(files)} files all have the same combination "
   486→                f"of issues ({', '.join(combo_names)}). Is this a systemic "
   487→                "pattern that should be addressed at the architecture level "
   488→                "(shared base class, framework change, lint rule), or are "
   489→                "these independent issues that happen to look similar?"
   490→            ),
   491→        )
   492→        if concern is not None:
   493→            concerns.append(concern)
   494→
   495→    return concerns
   496→
   497→
   498→def _systemic_smell_patterns(
   499→    state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]
   500→) -> list[Concern]:
   501→    """Systemic concerns: single smell_id appearing across 5+ files.
   502→
   503→    Complements _cross_file_patterns which looks at detector-combo profiles.
   504→    This catches pervasive single-smell issues (e.g. broad_except in 12 files).
   505→    """
   506→    smell_files: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   507→    smell_ids_map: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)  # smell_id -> issue IDs
   508→
   509→    for f in _open_issues(state):
   510→        if f.get("detector") != "smells":
   511→            continue
   512→        detail = f.get("detail", {})
   513→        smell_id = detail.get("smell_id", "") if isinstance(detail, dict) else ""
   514→        filepath = f.get("file", "")
   515→        if smell_id and filepath and filepath != ".":
   516→            smell_files[smell_id].append(filepath)
   517→            smell_ids_map[smell_id].append(f.get("id", ""))
   518→
   519→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   520→    for smell_id, files in smell_files.items():
   521→        unique_files = sorted(set(files))
   522→        if len(unique_files) < MIN_FILES_FOR_SMELL_PATTERN:
   523→            continue
   524→
   525→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(smell_ids_map[smell_id]))
   526→        concern = _try_make_concern(
   527→            concern_type="systemic_smell",
   528→            file=unique_files[0],
   529→            fp_file=smell_id,
   530→            fp_keys=(smell_id,),
   531→            all_ids=all_ids,
   532→            dismissals=dismissals,
   533→            summary=(
   534→                f"'{smell_id}' appears in {len(unique_files)} files — "
   535→                "likely a systemic pattern"
   536→            ),
   537→            evidence=(
   538→                f"Smell: {smell_id}",
   539→                f"Affected files ({len(unique_files)}): {', '.join(unique_files[:10])}",
   540→            ),
   541→            question=(
   542→                f"The smell '{smell_id}' appears across {len(unique_files)} files. "
   543→                "Is this a codebase-wide convention that should be addressed "
   544→                "systemically (lint rule, shared utility, architecture change), "
   545→                "or are these independent occurrences?"
   546→            ),
   547→        )
   548→        if concern is not None:
   549→            concerns.append(concern)
   550→
   551→    return concerns
   552→
   553→
   554→_GENERATORS = [_file_concerns, _cross_file_patterns, _systemic_smell_patterns]
   555→
   556→
   557→def generate_concerns(
   558→    state: StateModel,
   559→) -> list[Concern]:
   560→    """Run all concern generators against current state.
   561→
   562→    Returns deduplicated list sorted by (type, file).
   563→    """
   564→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   565→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   566→    seen_fps: set[str] = set()
   567→
   568→    for gen in _GENERATORS:
   569→        for concern in gen(state, dismissals):
   570→            if concern.fingerprint not in seen_fps:
   571→                seen_fps.add(concern.fingerprint)
   572→                concerns.append(concern)
   573→
   574→    concerns.sort(key=lambda c: (c.type, c.file))
   575→    return concerns
   576→
   577→
   578→def cleanup_stale_dismissals(state: StateModel) -> int:
   579→    """Remove dismissals whose source issues all disappeared.
   580→
   581→    Returns the number of stale entries removed.  Dismissals without
   582→    ``source_issue_ids`` (legacy) are left untouched.
   583→    """
   584→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   585→    if not dismissals:
   586→        return 0
   587→    open_ids = {f.get("id", "") for f in _open_issues(state)}
   588→    stale_fps = [
   589→        fp
   590→        for fp, entry in dismissals.items()
   591→        if entry.get("source_issue_ids")
   592→        and not any(sid in open_ids for sid in entry["source_issue_ids"])
   593→    ]
   594→    for fp in stale_fps:
   595→        del dismissals[fp]
   596→    return len(stale_fps)
   597→
   598→
   599→__all__ = ["Concern", "cleanup_stale_dismissals", "generate_concerns"]
   600→
```

## Task A: Extract `_try_make_concern()` factory in concerns.py

**File modified:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/concerns.py`

I extracted a `_try_make_concern()` helper (lines 283-315) that encapsulates the shared fingerprint -> dismiss -> construct pattern that was duplicated across all three concern generators:

```python
def _try_make_concern(
    *,
    concern_type: str,
    file: str,
    fp_keys: tuple[str, ...],
    all_ids: tuple[str, ...],
    dismissals: dict,
    summary: str,
    evidence: tuple[str, ...],
    question: str,
    fp_file: str | None = None,
) -> Concern | None:
```

The `fp_file` parameter handles the case where the fingerprint file key differs from the Concern's display file (used by `_cross_file_patterns` which hashes a joined file list but displays the first file, and `_systemic_smell_patterns` which uses the smell_id as the fingerprint key).

All three generators now use this helper:

- **`_systemic_smell_patterns()`** -- replaced 17 lines with a `_try_make_concern()` call using `fp_file=smell_id`

No behavioral changes -- the fingerprints and concern objects produced are identical to the original code.

```
   125→def cmd_plan_triage(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
```

```
1→"""Helper utilities for plan triage workflow."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→from collections import defaultdict
     7→
     8→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.runtime import command_runtime
     9→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
    10→from desloppify.engine.plan import (
    11→    TRIAGE_IDS,
    12→    TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS,
    13→    purge_ids,
    14→    review_issue_snapshot_hash,
    15→    save_plan,
    16→)
    17→from desloppify.state import utc_now
    18→
    19→_STAGE_ORDER = ["observe", "reflect", "organize"]
    20→
    21→
    22→def _has_triage_in_queue(plan: dict) -> bool:
    23→    """Check if any triage stage ID is in the queue."""
    24→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    25→    return bool(order & TRIAGE_IDS)
    26→
    27→def _inject_triage_stages(plan: dict) -> None:
    28→    """Inject all 4 triage stage IDs into the queue (fresh start)."""
    29→    order: list[str] = plan.setdefault("queue_order", [])
    30→    existing = set(order)
    31→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    32→        if sid not in existing:
    33→            order.insert(0 if sid == TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS[0] else len(order), sid)
    34→    # Re-insert in correct order at front
    35→    for sid in reversed(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS):
    36→        if sid in order:
    37→            order.remove(sid)
    38→    insert_at = 0
    39→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    40→        order.insert(insert_at, sid)
    41→        insert_at += 1
    42→
    43→def _purge_triage_stage(plan: dict, stage_name: str) -> None:
    44→    """Purge a single triage stage ID from the queue."""
    45→    sid = f"triage::{stage_name}"
    46→    purge_ids(plan, [sid])
    47→
    48→def _cascade_clear_later_confirmations(stages: dict, from_stage: str) -> list[str]:
    49→    """Clear confirmed_at/confirmed_text on stages AFTER *from_stage*. Returns cleared names."""
    50→    try:
    51→        idx = _STAGE_ORDER.index(from_stage)
    52→    except ValueError:
    53→        return []
    54→    cleared: list[str] = []
    55→    for later in _STAGE_ORDER[idx + 1:]:
    56→        if later in stages and stages[later].get("confirmed_at"):
    57→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_at", None)
    58→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_text", None)
    59→            cleared.append(later)
    60→    return cleared
    61→
    62→def _print_cascade_clear_feedback(cleared: list[str], stages: dict) -> None:
    63→    """Print yellow cascade-clear message with next-step guidance."""
    64→    if not cleared:
    65→        return
    66→    print(colorize(f"  Cleared confirmations on: {', '.join(cleared)}", "yellow"))
    67→    next_unconfirmed = next(
    68→        (s for s in _STAGE_ORDER if s in stages and not stages[s].get("confirmed_at")),
    69→        None,
    70→    )
    71→    if next_unconfirmed:
    72→        print(colorize(
    73→            f"  Re-confirm with: desloppify plan triage --confirm {next_unconfirmed}",
    74→            "dim",
    75→        ))
    76→
    77→def _observe_dimension_breakdown(si) -> tuple[dict[str, int], list[str]]:
    78→    """Count issues per dimension from a TriageInput. Returns (by_dim, sorted_dim_names)."""
    79→    by_dim: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    80→    for _fid, f in si.open_issues.items():
    81→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
    82→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "unknown")
    83→        by_dim[dim] += 1
    84→    dim_names = sorted(by_dim, key=lambda d: (-by_dim[d], d))
    85→    return dict(by_dim), dim_names
    86→
    87→def _open_review_ids_from_state(state: dict) -> set[str]:
    88→    """Return IDs of all open review/concerns issues in state."""
    89→    return {
    90→        fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
    91→        if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
    92→    }
    93→
    94→def _triage_coverage(
    95→    plan: dict,
    96→    open_review_ids: set[str] | None = None,
    97→) -> tuple[int, int, dict]:
    98→    """Return (organized, total, clusters) for review issues in triage.
    99→
   100→    When *open_review_ids* is provided, use it as the full set of review
   101→    issues (from state) instead of falling back to queue_order.
   102→    """
   103→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   104→    all_cluster_ids: set[str] = set()
   105→    for c in clusters.values():
   106→        all_cluster_ids.update(c.get("issue_ids", []))
   107→    if open_review_ids is not None:
   108→        review_ids = list(open_review_ids)
   109→    else:
   110→        review_ids = [
   111→            fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   112→            if not fid.startswith("triage::") and not fid.startswith("workflow::") and (fid.startswith("review::") or fid.startswith("concerns::"))
   113→        ]
   114→    organized = sum(1 for fid in review_ids if fid in all_cluster_ids)
   115→    return organized, len(review_ids), clusters
   116→
   117→def _manual_clusters_with_issues(plan: dict) -> list[str]:
   118→    """Return names of non-auto clusters that have issues."""
   119→    return [
   120→        name for name, c in plan.get("clusters", {}).items()
   121→        if c.get("issue_ids") and not c.get("auto")
   122→    ]
   123→
   124→def _apply_completion(args: argparse.Namespace, plan: dict, strategy: str) -> None:
   125→    """Shared completion logic: update meta, remove triage::pending, save."""
   126→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   127→    state = runtime.state
   128→
   129→    organized, total, clusters = _triage_coverage(
   130→        plan, open_review_ids=_open_review_ids_from_state(state),
   131→    )
   132→
   133→    # Purge all triage stage IDs.
   134→    purge_ids(plan, list(TRIAGE_IDS))
   135→
   136→    current_hash = review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   137→
   138→    meta = plan.setdefault("epic_triage_meta", {})
   139→    meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   140→    open_review_ids = sorted(
   141→        fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   142→        if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   143→    )
   144→    meta["triaged_ids"] = open_review_ids
   145→    if strategy.strip().lower() != "same":
   146→        meta["strategy_summary"] = strategy
   147→    meta["trigger"] = "manual_triage"
   148→    meta["last_completed_at"] = utc_now()
   149→    # Archive stages before clearing so previous analysis is preserved
   150→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   151→    if stages:
   152→        meta["last_triage"] = {
   153→            "completed_at": utc_now(),
   154→            "stages": {k: dict(v) for k, v in stages.items()},
   155→            "strategy": strategy if strategy.strip().lower() != "same" else meta.get("strategy_summary", ""),
   156→        }
   157→    meta["triage_stages"] = {}  # clear stages on completion
   158→    meta.pop("stage_refresh_required", None)
   159→    meta.pop("stage_snapshot_hash", None)
   160→
   161→    save_plan(plan)
   162→
   163→    cluster_count = len([c for c in clusters.values() if c.get("issue_ids")])
   164→    print(colorize(f"  Triage complete: {organized}/{total} issues in {cluster_count} cluster(s).", "green"))
   165→    effective_strategy = strategy if strategy.strip().lower() != "same" else meta.get("strategy_summary", "")
   166→    if effective_strategy:
   167→        print(colorize(f"  Strategy: {effective_strategy}", "cyan"))
   168→    print(colorize("  Run `desloppify next` to start implementation.", "green"))
   169→
   170→def _find_cluster_for(fid: str, clusters: dict) -> str | None:
   171→    """Return the cluster name containing *fid*, or None."""
   172→    for name, c in clusters.items():
   173→        if fid in c.get("issue_ids", []):
   174→            return name
   175→    return None
   176→
   177→def _count_log_activity_since(plan: dict, since: str) -> dict[str, int]:
   178→    """Count execution log entries by action since *since* timestamp."""
   179→    counts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
   180→    for entry in plan.get("execution_log", []):
   181→        if entry.get("timestamp", "") >= since:
   182→            counts[entry.get("action", "unknown")] += 1
   183→    return dict(counts)
```

```
    58→def phase_dupes(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
    59→    """Shared phase runner: detect duplicate functions via lang.extract_functions.
    60→
    61→    When a zone map is available, filters out functions from zone-excluded files
    62→    before the O(n^2) comparison to avoid test/config/generated false positives.
    63→    """
    64→    functions = lang.extract_functions(path)
    65→
    66→    # Filter out functions from zone-excluded files.
    67→    if lang.zone_map is not None:
    68→        before = len(functions)
    69→        functions = [
    70→            f
    71→            for f in functions
    72→            if lang.zone_map.get(getattr(f, "file", "")) not in EXCLUDED_ZONES
    73→        ]
    74→        excluded = before - len(functions)
    75→        if excluded:
    76→            log(f"         zones: {excluded} functions excluded (non-production)")
    77→
    78→    entries, total_functions = detect_duplicates(functions)
    79→    issues = make_dupe_issues(entries, log)
    80→    return issues, {"dupes": total_functions}
    81→
```
