    83→def phase_boilerplate_duplication(
    84→    path: Path,
    85→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
    86→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
    87→    """Shared phase runner: detect repeated boilerplate code via jscpd."""
    88→    entries = detect_with_jscpd(path)
    89→    if entries is None:
    90→        return [], {}
    91→    entries = _filter_boilerplate_entries_by_zone(entries, lang.zone_map)
    92→
    93→    issues: list[Issue] = []
    94→    for entry in entries:
    95→        locations = entry["locations"]
    96→        first = locations[0]
    97→        loc_preview = ", ".join(
    98→            f"{rel(item['file'])}:{item['line']}" for item in locations[:4]
    99→        )
   100→        if len(locations) > 4:
   101→            loc_preview += f", +{len(locations) - 4} more"
   102→        issues.append(
   103→            make_issue(
   104→                "boilerplate_duplication",
   105→                first["file"],
   106→                entry["id"],
   107→                tier=3,
   108→                confidence="medium",
   109→                summary=(
   110→                    f"Boilerplate block repeated across {entry['distinct_files']} files "
   111→                    f"(window {entry['window_size']} lines): {loc_preview}"
   112→                ),
   113→                detail={
   114→                    "distinct_files": entry["distinct_files"],
   115→                    "window_size": entry["window_size"],
   116→                    "locations": locations,
   117→                    "sample": entry["sample"],
   118→                },
   119→            )
   120→        )
   121→
   122→    if issues:
   123→        log(f"         boilerplate duplication: {len(issues)} clusters")
   124→    distinct_files = len({loc["file"] for e in entries for loc in e["locations"]})
   125→    return issues, {"boilerplate_duplication": distinct_files}
   126→
   127→
   128→def _filter_boilerplate_entries_by_zone(
   129→    entries: list[dict[str, Any]], zone_map
   130→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   131→    """Keep only in-scope, zone-allowed boilerplate clusters.
   132→
   133→    jscpd can return files that are outside language discovery (artifacts/docs).
   134→    Restricting to known zone-map files prevents unknown paths from being treated
   135→    as production issues.
   136→    """
   137→    if zone_map is None:
   138→        return entries
   139→
   140→    known_files = set(zone_map.all_files())
   141→    filtered: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   142→    skipped = 0
   143→    for entry in entries:
   144→        locations = entry.get("locations", [])
   145→        kept_locations = [
   146→            loc
   147→            for loc in locations
   148→            if loc.get("file") in known_files
   149→            and not should_skip_issue(
   150→                zone_map,
   151→                loc.get("file", ""),
   152→                "boilerplate_duplication",
   153→            )
   154→        ]
   155→        distinct_files = {loc["file"] for loc in kept_locations}
   156→        if len(distinct_files) < 2:
   157→            skipped += 1
   158→            continue
   159→
   160→        normalized = dict(entry)
   161→        normalized["locations"] = sorted(
   162→            kept_locations,
   163→            key=lambda item: (item.get("file", ""), item.get("line", 0)),
   164→        )
   165→        normalized["distinct_files"] = len(distinct_files)
   166→        filtered.append(normalized)
   167→
   168→    if skipped:
   169→        log(f"         zones: {skipped} boilerplate clusters excluded")
   170→    return filtered
   171→

   173→def find_external_test_files(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> set[str]:
   174→    """Find test files in standard locations outside the scanned path."""
   175→    extra = set()
   176→    path_root = path.resolve()
   177→    project_root = get_project_root()
   178→    test_dirs = lang.external_test_dirs or ["tests", "test"]
   179→    exts = tuple(lang.test_file_extensions or lang.extensions)
   180→    for test_dir in test_dirs:
   181→        d = project_root / test_dir
   182→        if not d.is_dir():
   183→            continue
   184→        if d.resolve().is_relative_to(path_root):
   185→            continue  # test_dir is inside scanned path, zone_map already has it
   186→        for root, _, files in os.walk(d):
   187→            for filename in files:
   188→                if any(filename.endswith(ext) for ext in exts):
   189→                    extra.add(os.path.join(root, filename))
   190→    return extra
   191→

   193→def _entries_to_issues(
   194→    detector: str,

   201→    """Convert detector entries to normalized issues."""
   202→    results: list[Issue] = []
   203→    for entry in entries:
   204→        issue = make_issue(
   205→            detector,
   206→            entry["file"],
   207→            entry.get("name", default_name),
   208→            tier=entry["tier"],
   209→            confidence=entry["confidence"],
   210→            summary=entry["summary"],

   212→        )
   213→        if include_zone and zone_map is not None:
   214→            z = zone_map.get(entry["file"])
   215→            if z is not None:
   216→                issue["zone"] = z.value
   217→        results.append(issue)

   229→def _coverage_to_dict(coverage: DetectorCoverageStatus) -> dict[str, Any]:
   230→    return {
   231→        "detector": coverage.detector,
   232→        "status": coverage.status,
   233→        "confidence": round(coerce_confidence(coverage.confidence), 2),
   234→        "summary": coverage.summary,
   235→        "impact": coverage.impact,
   236→        "remediation": coverage.remediation,
   237→        "tool": coverage.tool,
   238→        "reason": coverage.reason,
   239→    }
   240→
   241→
   242→def _merge_detector_coverage(
   243→    existing: dict[str, Any],
   244→    incoming: dict[str, Any],
   245→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   246→    merged = dict(existing)
   247→    merged["status"] = (
   248→        "reduced"
   249→        if str(existing.get("status", "full")) == "reduced"
   250→        or str(incoming.get("status", "full")) == "reduced"
   251→        else "full"
   252→    )
   253→    merged["confidence"] = round(
   254→        min(
   255→            coerce_confidence(existing.get("confidence")),
   256→            coerce_confidence(incoming.get("confidence")),
   257→        ),
   258→        2,
   259→    )
   260→
   261→    for key in ("summary", "impact", "remediation", "tool", "reason"):
   262→        current = str(merged.get(key, "") or "").strip()
   263→        update = str(incoming.get(key, "") or "").strip()
   264→        if update and not current:
   265→            merged[key] = update
   266→        elif update and current and update not in current:
   267→            merged[key] = f"{current} | {update}"
   268→    return merged
   269→
   270→
   271→def _record_detector_coverage(lang: LangRuntimeContract, coverage: DetectorCoverageStatus | None) -> None:
   272→    if coverage is None:
   273→        return
   274→    normalized = _coverage_to_dict(coverage)
   275→    detector = str(normalized.get("detector", "")).strip()
   276→    if not detector:
   277→        return
   278→    existing = lang.detector_coverage.get(detector)
   279→    if isinstance(existing, dict):
   280→        lang.detector_coverage[detector] = _merge_detector_coverage(existing, normalized)
   281→    else:
   282→        lang.detector_coverage[detector] = normalized

   285→def phase_security(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   286→    """Shared phase: detect security issues (cross-language + lang-specific)."""
   287→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   288→    files = lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else []
   289→    entries, cross_lang_scanned = detect_security_issues(
   290→        files,
   291→        zone_map,
   292→        lang.name,
   293→        scan_root=path,
   294→    )
   295→    lang_scanned = 0
   296→
   297→    # Also call lang-specific security detectors.
   298→    lang_result = lang.detect_lang_security_detailed(files, zone_map)
   299→    lang_entries = lang_result.entries
   300→    lang_scanned = max(0, int(lang_result.files_scanned))
   301→    _record_detector_coverage(lang, lang_result.coverage)
   302→    entries.extend(lang_entries)
   303→
   304→    entries = filter_entries(zone_map, entries, "security")
   305→    potential = max(cross_lang_scanned, lang_scanned)
   306→
   307→    results = _entries_to_issues(
   308→        "security",
   309→        entries,
   310→        include_zone=True,
   311→        zone_map=zone_map,
   312→    )
   313→    _log_phase_summary("security", results, potential, "files scanned")
   314→
   315→    if "security" not in lang.detector_coverage:
   316→        lang.detector_coverage["security"] = {
   317→            "detector": "security",
   318→            "status": "full",
   319→            "confidence": 1.0,
   320→            "summary": "Security coverage complete for enabled detectors.",
   321→            "impact": "",
   322→            "remediation": "",
   323→            "tool": "",
   324→            "reason": "",
   325→        }
   326→
   327→    return results, {"security": potential}

   330→def phase_test_coverage(

   344→        lang.name,
   345→        extra_test_files=extra or None,
   346→        complexity_map=lang.complexity_map or None,
   347→    )
   348→    entries = filter_entries(zone_map, entries, "test_coverage")
   349→
   350→    results = _entries_to_issues("test_coverage", entries, default_name="")
   351→    _log_phase_summary("test coverage", results, potential, "production files")
   352→
   353→    return results, {"test_coverage": potential}

   356→def phase_private_imports(
   357→    path: Path,
   358→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   359→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   360→    """Shared phase: detect cross-module private imports."""
   361→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   362→    graph = lang.dep_graph or lang.build_dep_graph(path)
   363→
   364→    entries, potential = lang.detect_private_imports(graph, zone_map)
   365→    entries = filter_entries(zone_map, entries, "private_imports")
   366→
   367→    results = _entries_to_issues("private_imports", entries)

   373→def phase_subjective_review(
   374→    path: Path,
   375→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   376→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   377→    """Shared phase: detect files missing subjective design review."""
   378→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   379→    max_age = lang.review_max_age_days
   380→    files = lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else []
   381→    review_cache = lang.review_cache
   382→    if isinstance(review_cache, dict) and "files" in review_cache:
   383→        per_file_cache = review_cache.get("files", {})
   384→    else:
   385→        # Legacy format: flat dict of file entries with no "files" wrapper.
   386→        # Filter out known top-level structural keys so they aren't treated as
   387→        # file paths, then reconstruct the canonical shape preserving them.
   388→        _TOP_LEVEL_KEYS = frozenset({"holistic"})
   389→        raw = review_cache if isinstance(review_cache, dict) else {}
   390→        per_file_cache = {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if k not in _TOP_LEVEL_KEYS}
   391→        review_cache = {"files": per_file_cache}
   392→        if "holistic" in raw:
   393→            review_cache["holistic"] = raw["holistic"]
   394→
   395→    entries, potential = detect_review_coverage(
   396→        files,
   397→        zone_map,
   398→        per_file_cache,
   399→        lang.name,
   400→        low_value_pattern=lang.review_low_value_pattern,
   401→        max_age_days=max_age,
   402→        holistic_cache=review_cache.get("holistic")
   403→        if isinstance(review_cache, dict)
   404→        else None,
   405→        holistic_total_files=len(files),
   406→    )
   407→
   408→    # Also check holistic review staleness.
   409→    holistic_entries = detect_holistic_review_staleness(
   410→        review_cache,
   411→        total_files=len(files),
   412→        max_age_days=max_age,
   413→    )
   414→    entries.extend(holistic_entries)
   415→
   416→    results = _entries_to_issues("subjective_review", entries)
   417→    _log_phase_summary("subjective review", results, potential, "reviewable files")
   418→
   419→    return results, {"subjective_review": potential}
   420→
   421→
   422→def phase_signature(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   423→    """Shared phase runner: detect signature variance via lang.extract_functions.
   424→
   425→    Backend-agnostic — works with any extractor that returns FunctionInfo objects
   426→    (tree-sitter, regex, AST, etc.).  Returns empty results when the lang has no
   427→    function extractor.
   428→    """
   429→    from desloppify.engine.detectors.signature import detect_signature_variance
   430→
   431→    functions = lang.extract_functions(path)
   432→
   433→    issues: list[Issue] = []
   434→    potentials: dict[str, int] = {}
   435→
   436→    if not functions:
   437→        return issues, potentials
   438→
   439→    entries, _total = detect_signature_variance(functions, min_occurrences=3)
   440→    for e in entries:
   441→        issues.append(make_issue(
   442→            "signature", e["files"][0],
   443→            f"signature_variance::{e['name']}",
   444→            tier=3, confidence="medium",
   445→            summary=(
   446→                f"'{e['name']}' has {e['signature_count']} different signatures "
   447→                f"across {e['file_count']} files"
   448→            ),
   449→        ))
   450→    if entries:
   451→        potentials["signature"] = len(entries)
   452→        log(f"         signature variance: {len(entries)}")
   453→
   454→    return issues, potentials
   455→
   456→
   457→def run_structural_phase(
   458→    path: Path,
   459→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   460→    *,
   461→    complexity_signals: list[ComplexitySignal],
   462→    log_fn,
   463→    min_loc: int = 40,
   464→    god_rules=None,
   465→    god_extractor_fn=None,
   466→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   467→    """Run large/complexity/flat directory detectors for a language.
   468→
   469→    Optional ``god_rules`` + ``god_extractor_fn`` enable god-class detection:
   470→    when both are provided, ``god_extractor_fn(path)`` is called to extract
   471→    class info, then ``detect_gods()`` finds classes matching multiple rules.
   472→    """
   473→    structural: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
   474→
   475→    large_entries, file_count = detect_large_files(
   476→        path,
   477→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   478→        threshold=lang.large_threshold,
   479→    )
   480→    for entry in large_entries:
   481→        add_structural_signal(
   482→            structural,
   483→            entry["file"],
   484→            f"large ({entry['loc']} LOC)",
   485→            {"loc": entry["loc"]},
   486→        )
   487→
   488→    complexity_entries, _ = detect_complexity(
   489→        path,
   490→        signals=complexity_signals,
   491→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   492→        threshold=lang.complexity_threshold,
   493→        min_loc=min_loc,
   494→    )
   495→    for entry in complexity_entries:
   496→        add_structural_signal(
   497→            structural,
   498→            entry["file"],
   499→            f"complexity score {entry['score']}",
   500→            {"complexity_score": entry["score"], "complexity_signals": entry["signals"]},
   501→        )
   502→        lang.complexity_map[entry["file"]] = entry["score"]
   503→
   504→    if god_rules and god_extractor_fn:
   505→        from desloppify.engine.detectors.gods import detect_gods
   506→
   507→        god_entries, _ = detect_gods(god_extractor_fn(path), god_rules, min_reasons=2)
   508→        for entry in god_entries:
   509→            add_structural_signal(
   510→                structural, entry["file"], entry["signal_text"], entry["detail"],
   511→            )
   512→        if god_entries:
   513→            log_fn(f"         god classes: {len(god_entries)}")
   514→
   515→    results = merge_structural_signals(structural, log_fn)
   516→    flat_entries, analyzed_dir_count = detect_flat_dirs(
   517→        path,
   518→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   519→        config=FlatDirDetectionConfig(),
   520→    )
   521→    for entry in flat_entries:
   522→        child_dir_count = int(entry.get("child_dir_count", 0))
   523→        combined_score = int(entry.get("combined_score", entry.get("file_count", 0)))
   524→        results.append(
   525→            make_issue(
   526→                "flat_dirs",
   527→                entry["directory"],
   528→                "",
   529→                tier=3,
   530→                confidence="medium",
   531→                summary=format_flat_dir_summary(entry),
   532→                detail={
   533→                    "file_count": entry["file_count"],
   534→                    "child_dir_count": child_dir_count,
   535→                    "combined_score": combined_score,
   536→                    "kind": entry.get("kind", "overload"),
   537→                    "parent_sibling_count": int(entry.get("parent_sibling_count", 0)),
   538→                    "wrapper_item_count": int(entry.get("wrapper_item_count", 0)),
   539→                    "sparse_child_count": int(entry.get("sparse_child_count", 0)),
   540→                    "sparse_child_ratio": float(entry.get("sparse_child_ratio", 0.0)),
   541→                    "sparse_child_file_threshold": int(
   542→                        entry.get("sparse_child_file_threshold", 0)
   543→                    ),
   544→                },
   545→            )
   546→        )
   547→    if flat_entries:
   548→        log_fn(
   549→            f"         flat dirs: {len(flat_entries)} overloaded directories "
   550→            "(files/subdirs/combined)"
   551→        )
   552→
   553→    potentials = {
   554→        "structural": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, file_count),
   555→        "flat_dirs": analyzed_dir_count,
   556→    }
   557→    return results, potentials
   558→
   559→
   560→def run_coupling_phase(
   561→    path: Path,
   562→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   563→    *,
   564→    build_dep_graph_fn,
   565→    log_fn,
   566→    post_process_fn=None,
   567→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   568→    """Run single-use/cycles/orphaned detectors against a language dep graph.
   569→
   570→    Optional ``post_process_fn(issues, entries, lang)`` is called after
   571→    creating single-use and orphaned issues to allow per-language
   572→    adjustments (e.g. confidence gating based on corroboration signals).
   573→    """
   574→    graph = build_dep_graph_fn(path)
   575→    lang.dep_graph = graph
   576→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   577→    results: list[Issue] = []
   578→
   579→    single_entries, single_candidates = detect_single_use_abstractions(
   580→        path,
   581→        graph,
   582→        barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   583→    )
   584→    single_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, single_entries, "single_use")
   585→    single_issues = make_single_use_issues(
   586→        single_entries, lang.get_area, stderr_fn=log_fn,
   587→    )
   588→    if post_process_fn:
   589→        post_process_fn(single_issues, single_entries, lang)
   590→    results.extend(single_issues)
   591→
   592→    cycle_entries, _ = detect_cycles(graph)
   593→    cycle_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, cycle_entries, "cycles", file_key="files")
   594→    results.extend(make_cycle_issues(cycle_entries, log_fn))
   595→
   596→    orphan_entries, total_graph_files = detect_orphaned_files(
   597→        path,
   598→        graph,
   599→        extensions=lang.extensions,
   600→        options=OrphanedDetectionOptions(
   601→            extra_entry_patterns=lang.entry_patterns,
   602→            extra_barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   603→        ),
   604→    )
   605→    orphan_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, orphan_entries, "orphaned")
   606→    orphan_issues = make_orphaned_issues(orphan_entries, log_fn)
   607→    if post_process_fn:
   608→        post_process_fn(orphan_issues, orphan_entries, lang)
   609→    results.extend(orphan_issues)
   610→
   611→    log_fn(f"         -> {len(results)} coupling/structural issues total")
   612→    potentials = {
   613→        "single_use": adjust_potential(zone_map, single_candidates),
   614→        "cycles": adjust_potential(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   615→        "orphaned": adjust_potential(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   616→    }
   617→    return results, potentials
   618→
   619→
   620→def make_structural_coupling_phase_pair(
   621→    *,
   622→    complexity_signals: list[ComplexitySignal],
   623→    build_dep_graph_fn,
   624→    log_fn,
   625→) -> tuple:
   626→    """Create default structural/coupling phase callables for a language.
   627→
   628→    This keeps language phase modules declarative by letting them provide only
   629→    their complexity signals and dependency-graph builder.
   630→    """
   631→
   632→    def phase_structural(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   633→        return run_structural_phase(
   634→            path,
   635→            lang,
   636→            complexity_signals=complexity_signals,
   637→            log_fn=log_fn,
   638→        )
   639→
   640→    def phase_coupling(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   641→        return run_coupling_phase(
   642→            path,
   643→            lang,
   644→            build_dep_graph_fn=build_dep_graph_fn,
   645→            log_fn=log_fn,
   646→        )
   647→
   648→    return phase_structural, phase_coupling
   649→
   650→
   651→__all__ = [
   652→    "find_external_test_files",
   653→    "make_structural_coupling_phase_pair",
   654→    "phase_boilerplate_duplication",
   655→    "phase_dupes",
   656→    "phase_private_imports",
   657→    "phase_security",
   658→    "phase_signature",
   659→    "phase_subjective_review",
   660→    "phase_test_coverage",
   661→    "run_coupling_phase",
   662→    "run_structural_phase",
   663→]

    36→def _cmd_triage_complete(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    37→    """Complete triage — requires organize stage (or confirm-existing path)."""
    38→    strategy: str | None = getattr(args, "strategy", None)
    39→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
    40→    plan = load_plan()
    41→
    42→    if not _has_triage_in_queue(plan):
    43→        print(colorize("  No planning stages in the queue — nothing to complete.", "yellow"))
    44→        return
    45→
    46→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
    47→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
    48→
    49→    state = command_runtime(args).state
    50→    review_ids = _open_review_ids_from_state(state)
    51→
    52→    # Require organize stage confirmed
    53→    if not _require_organize_stage_for_complete(
    54→        plan=plan,
    55→        meta=meta,
    56→        stages=stages,
    57→    ):
    58→        return
    59→
    60→    # Fold-confirm: auto-confirm organize if attestation provided
    61→    if not _auto_confirm_organize_for_complete(
    62→        plan=plan,
    63→        stages=stages,
    64→        attestation=attestation,
    65→    ):
    66→        return
    67→
    68→    # Re-validate cluster enrichment at completion time (prevents bypassing
    69→    # organize gate by editing plan.json directly)
    70→    if not _completion_clusters_valid(plan):
    71→        return
    72→
    73→    # Verify cluster coverage
    74→    organized, total, _clusters = _triage_coverage(plan, open_review_ids=review_ids)
    75→
    76→    if total > 0 and organized == 0:
    77→        print(colorize("  Cannot complete: no issues have been organized into clusters.", "red"))
    78→        print(colorize(f"  {total} issues are waiting.", "dim"))
    79→        return

Author: POM <[REDACTED]>
Date:   Fri Feb 20 17:53:04 2026 +0100

    Add external tool adapters: Knip (TS), ruff smells (Python), bandit (Python)
    
    Phase 1 — Knip adapter for TypeScript:
    - New `detectors/knip_adapter.py` runs `npx knip --reporter json` and parses
      unused exports and orphaned files from its output.
    - `_phase_exports` tries Knip first, falls back to grep-based detection.
    - `_phase_coupling` reuses Knip's orphaned results when available to avoid a
      second subprocess invocation.
    
    Phase 2 — Ruff smells for Python:
    - New `detectors/ruff_smells.py` runs ruff with B/E/W rules not covered by
      the existing regex smells: B007 (unused loop var), B023 (func in loop),
      B026 (star after keyword), B904 (raise without from), E711/E712 (None/bool
      comparisons), W605 (invalid escape).
    - `phase_smells` in `phases_quality.py` appends ruff entries when available.
    
    Phase 3 — Bandit adapter for Python security:
    - New `detectors/bandit_adapter.py` runs `bandit -r -f json` and converts
      its results to security entries, skipping LOW/LOW findings and IDs that
      overlap with the cross-language secret scanner.
    - `PythonConfig.detect_lang_security` tries bandit first, falls back to the
      existing regex/AST security checks when bandit is not installed.
    
    All adapters degrade gracefully (return None) on FileNotFoundError /
    TimeoutExpired — existing behaviour is preserved when tools are absent.
    32 new tests cover: graceful degradation, JSON parsing, entry structure.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

register_lang_hooks("python", test_coverage=py_test_coverage_hooks)


def _get_py_area(filepath: str) -> str:
    """Derive an area name from a Python file path for grouping."""
    parts = [part for part in re.split(r"[\\/]+", filepath) if part]
    if len(parts) > 2:
        return "/".join(parts[:2])
    return parts[0] if parts else filepath


def _py_build_dep_graph(path: Path) -> dict:
    return build_dep_graph(path)


def _py_extract_functions(path: Path) -> list:
    """Extract all Python functions for duplicate detection."""
    functions = []
    for filepath in find_py_files(path):
        functions.extend(extract_py_functions(filepath))
    return functions


def _scan_root_from_files(files: list[str]) -> Path | None:
    """Derive the common ancestor directory from a list of file paths."""
    import os

    py_files = [f for f in files if f.endswith(".py")]
    if not py_files:
        return None
    try:
        common = Path(os.path.commonpath(py_files))
        return common if common.is_dir() else common.parent
    except ValueError:
        return None

"""Handler for ``plan triage`` subcommand."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.runtime import command_runtime
from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.state import require_completed_scan
from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage import confirmations as _confirmations_mod
from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage import display as _display_mod
from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage import helpers as _helpers_mod
from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage import stages as _stages_mod
from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage_playbook import TRIAGE_CMD_OBSERVE
from desloppify.core.output import colorize
from desloppify.engine.plan import (
    append_log_entry,
    build_triage_prompt,
    collect_triage_input,
    detect_recurring_patterns,
    extract_issue_citations,
    load_plan,
    save_plan,
)

_MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN = _confirmations_mod._MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN
_validate_attestation = _confirmations_mod._validate_attestation
_triage_coverage = _helpers_mod._triage_coverage


def _sync_triage_module_bindings() -> None:
    """Propagate monkeypatch-friendly bindings into split triage modules."""
    _helpers_mod.command_runtime = command_runtime
    _helpers_mod.save_plan = save_plan

    _display_mod.command_runtime = command_runtime
    _display_mod.collect_triage_input = collect_triage_input
    _display_mod.detect_recurring_patterns = detect_recurring_patterns
    _display_mod.load_plan = load_plan

    _confirmations_mod.append_log_entry = append_log_entry
    _confirmations_mod.collect_triage_input = collect_triage_input
    _confirmations_mod.command_runtime = command_runtime
    _confirmations_mod.detect_recurring_patterns = detect_recurring_patterns
    _confirmations_mod.load_plan = load_plan
    _confirmations_mod.save_plan = save_plan

    _stages_mod.append_log_entry = append_log_entry
    _stages_mod.collect_triage_input = collect_triage_input
    _stages_mod.command_runtime = command_runtime
    _stages_mod.detect_recurring_patterns = detect_recurring_patterns
    _stages_mod.extract_issue_citations = extract_issue_citations
    _stages_mod.load_plan = load_plan
    _stages_mod.save_plan = save_plan


def _cmd_triage_start(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Manually inject triage stage IDs into the queue and clear prior stages."""
    _sync_triage_module_bindings()
    plan = load_plan()

    if _helpers_mod._has_triage_in_queue(plan):
        print(colorize("  Planning mode stages are already in the queue.", "yellow"))
        meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
        stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
        if stages:
            print(
                colorize(
                    f"  {len(stages)} stage(s) in progress — clearing to restart.", "yellow"
                )
            )
            meta["triage_stages"] = {}
            _helpers_mod._inject_triage_stages(plan)
            save_plan(plan)
            append_log_entry(
                plan,
                "triage_start",
                actor="user",
                detail={"action": "restart", "cleared_stages": list(stages.keys())},
            )
            save_plan(plan)
            print(colorize("  Stages cleared. Begin with observe:", "green"))
        else:
            print(colorize("  Begin with observe:", "green"))
        print(colorize(f"    {TRIAGE_CMD_OBSERVE}", "dim"))
        return

    _helpers_mod._inject_triage_stages(plan)
    meta = plan.setdefault("epic_triage_meta", {})
    meta["triage_stages"] = {}
    save_plan(plan)

    append_log_entry(plan, "triage_start", actor="user", detail={"action": "start"})
    save_plan(plan)

    runtime = command_runtime(args)
    si = collect_triage_input(plan, runtime.state)
    print(colorize("  Planning mode started (4 stages queued).", "green"))
    print(f"  Open review issues: {len(si.open_issues)}")
    print(colorize("  Begin with observe:", "dim"))
    print(colorize(f"    {TRIAGE_CMD_OBSERVE}", "dim"))


def cmd_plan_triage(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Run epic triage: staged workflow OBSERVE → REFLECT → ORGANIZE → COMMIT."""
    _sync_triage_module_bindings()
    runtime = command_runtime(args)
    state = runtime.state
    if not require_completed_scan(state):
        return

    if getattr(args, "start", False):
        _cmd_triage_start(args)
        return
    if getattr(args, "confirm", None):
        _confirmations_mod._cmd_confirm_stage(args)
        return
    if getattr(args, "complete", False):
        _stages_mod._cmd_triage_complete(args)
        return
    if getattr(args, "confirm_existing", False):
        _stages_mod._cmd_confirm_existing(args)
        return

    stage = getattr(args, "stage", None)
    if stage == "observe":
        _stages_mod._cmd_stage_observe(args)
        return
    if stage == "reflect":
        _stages_mod._cmd_stage_reflect(args)
        return
    if stage == "organize":
        _stages_mod._cmd_stage_organize(args)
        return

    if getattr(args, "dry_run", False):
        plan = load_plan()
        si = collect_triage_input(plan, state)
        prompt = build_triage_prompt(si)
        print(colorize("  Epic triage — dry run", "bold"))
        print(colorize("  " + "─" * 60, "dim"))
        print(f"  Open review issues: {len(si.open_issues)}")
        print(f"  Existing epics: {len(si.existing_epics)}")
        print(f"  New since last: {len(si.new_since_last)}")
        print(f"  Resolved since last: {len(si.resolved_since_last)}")
        print(colorize("\n  Prompt that would be sent to LLM:", "dim"))
        print()
        print(prompt)
        return

    _display_mod._cmd_triage_dashboard(args)

"""Shared compatibility behavior for typed detector adapters."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Protocol

from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import DetectorCoverageStatus


class CoverageStatusLike(Protocol):
    """Minimal status contract used by compatibility wrappers."""

    def coverage(self) -> DetectorCoverageStatus | None: ...


def entries_or_none_on_degradation(
    *,
    entries: list[dict],
    status: CoverageStatusLike,
) -> list[dict] | None:
    """Return entries when coverage is intact, otherwise preserve legacy ``None``."""
    if status.coverage() is None:
        return entries
    return None


__all__ = ["entries_or_none_on_degradation"]

+"""Shared compatibility behavior for typed detector adapters."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Protocol
+
+from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import DetectorCoverageStatus
+
+
+class CoverageStatusLike(Protocol):
+    """Minimal status contract used by compatibility wrappers."""
+
+    def coverage(self) -> DetectorCoverageStatus | None: ...
+
+
+def entries_or_none_on_degradation(
+    *,
+    entries: list[dict],
+    status: CoverageStatusLike,
+) -> list[dict] | None:
+    """Return entries when coverage is intact, otherwise preserve legacy ``None``."""
+    if status.coverage() is None:
+        return entries
+    return None
+
+
+__all__ = ["entries_or_none_on_degradation"]

def detect_lang_security_detailed(self, files, zone_map) -> LangSecurityResult:
        scan_root = _scan_root_from_files(files)
        if scan_root is None:
            return LangSecurityResult(entries=[], files_scanned=0)

        exclude_dirs = collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root)

        result = detect_with_bandit(scan_root, zone_map, exclude_dirs=exclude_dirs)
        coverage = result.status.coverage()
        return LangSecurityResult(
            entries=result.entries,
            files_scanned=result.files_scanned,
            coverage=coverage,
        )

    def detect_private_imports(self, graph, zone_map):
        return detect_python_private_imports(graph, zone_map)

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(
            name="python",
            extensions=[".py"],
            exclusions=["__pycache__", ".venv", "node_modules", ".eggs", "*.egg-info"],
            default_src=".",
            build_dep_graph=build_dep_graph,
            entry_patterns=PY_ENTRY_PATTERNS,
            barrel_names={"__init__.py"},
            phases=[
                DetectorPhase("Unused (ruff)", phase_unused),
                DetectorPhase("Structural analysis", phase_structural),
                DetectorPhase("Responsibility cohesion", phase_responsibility_cohesion),
                DetectorPhase("Coupling + cycles + orphaned", phase_coupling),
                DetectorPhase("Uncalled functions", phase_uncalled_functions),
                detector_phase_test_coverage(),
                DetectorPhase("Code smells", phase_smells),
                DetectorPhase("Mutable state", phase_mutable_state),

PERFECT! Now I see the exact issue. Let me trace through what happens:

1. Test monkeypatches `triage_mod.load_plan`, `triage_mod.command_runtime`, etc at the triage_handlers module level
2. `cmd_plan_triage` is called which calls `_sync_triage_module_bindings()`
3. The sync function copies those monkeypatched functions into the submodule attributes (e.g., `_confirmations_mod.load_plan = load_plan`)

## Thorough Analysis of Duplicated Security Orchestration Logic

Based on my investigation, here's a comprehensive analysis of the duplication in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/python/__init__.py`:

### 1. **What's Duplicated**

There are **two implementations** of the same security orchestration logic:

**In `/desloppify/languages/python/__init__.py` (lines 86-102):**
```python
def detect_python_security(files, zone_map) -> LangSecurityResult:
    """Run Bandit-backed Python security scan with runtime exclusion dirs.

    Kept at module scope for patchability in tests and downstream integrations.
    """
    scan_root = _scan_root_from_files(files)
    if scan_root is None:
        return LangSecurityResult(entries=[], files_scanned=0)

    exclude_dirs = collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root)
    result = detect_with_bandit(scan_root, zone_map, exclude_dirs=exclude_dirs)
    coverage = result.status.coverage()
    return LangSecurityResult(
        entries=result.entries,
        files_scanned=result.files_scanned,
        coverage=coverage,
    )
```

**In `/desloppify/languages/python/_security.py` (lines 35-47):**
```python
def detect_python_security(files, zone_map) -> LangSecurityResult:
    scan_root = scan_root_from_files(files)
    if scan_root is None:
        return LangSecurityResult(entries=[], files_scanned=0)

    exclude_dirs = collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root)
    result = detect_with_bandit(scan_root, zone_map, exclude_dirs=exclude_dirs)
    coverage = result.status.coverage()
    return LangSecurityResult(
        entries=result.entries,
        files_scanned=result.files_scanned,
        coverage=coverage,
    )
```

**Code is 95% identical** with one minor difference: `__init__.py` uses `_scan_root_from_files` (wrapper), while `_security.py` uses `scan_root_from_files` (original).

---

### 2. **Where the Original/Shared Version Is**

The primary implementation lives in **`desloppify/languages/python/_security.py`**:
- This is the intentional "real" location
- It's part of the Python language plugin's internal security wiring module
- It's properly documented and belongs with other security prerequisite functions

The `__init__.py` version is a **wrapper/duplicate** that sits at the module level.

---

### 3. **Why It Was Duplicated — The Evolution**

By tracing the git history, I found the reason:

**Commit 4cb29f0** ("Add external tool adapters...") introduced the bandit adapter and established this pattern with a method directly in `PythonConfig`:
```python
def detect_lang_security(self, files, zone_map):
    scan_root = _scan_root_from_files(files)
    if scan_root is None:
        return [], 0
    return detect_with_bandit(scan_root, zone_map) or ([], 0)
```

**Commit 12f9581** ("Fix four elegance issues...") refactored this to extract the logic:
- Created `_security.py` with the complete implementation
- Added the module-level wrapper in `__init__.py` for "patchability in tests and downstream integrations"

The comment on line 89 in `__init__.py` explicitly states:
> "Kept at module scope for patchability in tests and downstream integrations."

This was a **deliberate design decision** to allow test mocking/patching at the module level rather than through dependency injection.

---

### 4. **Is It For Monkey-Patching? Test Isolation? Plugin Compatibility?**

**YES — it was explicitly for monkey-patching support:**

The rationale was:
- **Test Isolation**: Tests can `patch('desloppify.languages.python.detect_python_security')` without having to navigate through `__init__.py` import re-exports
- **Downstream Integration**: External code (or plugins) that imports this module directly can monkey-patch the detector to substitute custom behavior
- **LangConfig Interface**: The `detect_lang_security_detailed()` method (line 113) calls the module-level `detect_python_security()`, so tests could patch just the orchestration layer

**However**, I found **ZERO actual usage** of this monkey-patching in the codebase:
- No tests use `patch('...detect_python_security')`
- No code directly calls the module-level function
- All real usage goes through `PythonConfig.detect_lang_security_detailed()` method

---

### 5. **Is the Duplication Still Necessary?**

**NO.** The compatibility concern has been largely resolved:

1. **No active monkey-patching**: The codebase has no tests or integrations that rely on patching this function at module scope
2. **Recent architecture cleanup**: Commit `cfd8dd0` ("Remove functional compatibility shims...") deleted similar compatibility wrappers (`compat.py`) and deprecated old patterns
3. **Backward compatibility policy**: The project memory states *"No backward compat for import paths/APIs — this is an internal tool, not a library"*
4. **TypeScript doesn't do this**: The equivalent TypeScript security detector (`detect_ts_security_result`) is NOT duplicated at module scope in `typescript/__init__.py`; it's just called directly from the config class

---

### 6. **Cleaner Design Option**

**Option A: Consolidate to _security.py only** (Recommended)
```python

@register_lang("python")
class PythonConfig(LangConfig):

```

Benefits:
- Single source of truth
- Matches TypeScript plugin architecture
- Simpler test setup (no patching needed)
- Aligns with backward-compat policy

**Option B: Inline small wrapper and remove standalone version** (Alternative)
- Keep `detect_python_security` ONLY in `__init__.py` as a thin orchestration layer
- Move helper functions (`scan_root_from_files`, `collect_exclude_dirs`) to a utilities module
- Delete `_security.py` entirely

---

### 7. **Assessment: Worth Fixing?**

**YES, this is worth fixing:**

- **Low risk**: No actual patching usage to break
- **Alignment benefit**: Matches the project's recent cleanup trend (`cfd8dd0`)
- **Clarity gain**: Eliminates a confusing module-level duplicate
- **Architecture consistency**: Aligns with TypeScript plugin (no duplication there)
- **Minimal effort**: Simple import rewiring in 2-3 files
- **Backward compat policy**: Project explicitly discourages keeping import shims "for tests/plugins"

## Thorough Analysis of `_sync_triage_module_bindings` Pattern

---

### Overview

The `_sync_triage_module_bindings()` function in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage_handlers.py` is a **monkeypatch-friendly rebinding mechanism** that dynamically propagates imported functions into split triage submodules. It exists to enable **test monkeypatching at a single point** while ensuring those patches are visible throughout the modular triage subsystem.

---

### What It Does

Located in `triage_handlers.py` lines 33-76, the function manually assigns module-level references:

```python
def _sync_triage_module_bindings() -> None:
    """Propagate monkeypatch-friendly bindings into split triage modules."""
    _helpers_mod.command_runtime = command_runtime
    _helpers_mod.save_plan = save_plan

    _display_mod.command_runtime = command_runtime
    _display_mod.collect_triage_input = collect_triage_input
    _display_mod.detect_recurring_patterns = detect_recurring_patterns
    _display_mod.load_plan = load_plan

    _confirmations_mod.append_log_entry = append_log_entry
    _confirmations_mod.collect_triage_input = collect_triage_input
    _confirmations_mod.command_runtime = command_runtime
    # ... etc for all 6 triage submodules
```

**It is called at two entry points:**
1. Line 80: `_cmd_triage_start()` — before executing the start subcommand
2. Line 127: `cmd_plan_triage()` — at the top of the main triage command dispatcher

**Modules being synced (6 total):**
- `_helpers_mod` (helpers.py)
- `_display_mod` (display.py)
- `_confirmations_mod` (confirmations.py)
- `_stages_mod` (stages.py)
- `_flow_mod` (_stage_flow_commands.py)
- `_completion_mod` (_stage_completion_commands.py)
- `_validation_mod` (_stage_validation.py)

**Functions being bound:**
- `command_runtime`
- `save_plan`
- `load_plan`
- `collect_triage_input`
- `detect_recurring_patterns`
- `append_log_entry`
- `extract_issue_citations`

---

### The Problem It Solves: Test Monkeypatching

The reason this pattern exists is **to enable tests to mock these functions at a single point**.

**Evidence from tests** (`test_triage_attestation.py`, lines 206-244):

```python
def test_confirm_observe_rejects_generic_attestation(self, monkeypatch, capsys):
    """Attestation of 80+ chars that doesn't mention any dimension is rejected."""
    plan = _plan_with_stages("observe")
    state = _state_with_issues("r1", "r2", "r3", dimension="naming")

    # Monkeypatch at the HANDLER module level, not the submodule
    monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "load_plan", lambda *a, **kw: plan)
    monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "command_runtime", lambda args: _fake_runtime(state))
    monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "require_completed_scan", lambda s: True)

    # Call the command...
    args = _fake_args(confirm="observe", attestation=attestation)
    triage_mod.cmd_plan_triage(args)  # ← This calls _sync_triage_module_bindings()
    
    # Now confirmations.py, display.py, etc. see the mocked functions
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
```

**Why the sync is necessary:**

1. Each submodule **imports these functions directly at the top** (e.g., `from desloppify.engine.plan import load_plan`)
2. When the test monkeypatches `triage_mod.load_plan`, it only affects the `triage_handlers` module
3. The submodules still reference the **original imported binding** from `desloppify.engine.plan`
4. The sync function **updates the module-level namespace** of each submodule: `_helpers_mod.load_plan = load_plan` (where `load_plan` is now the monkeypatched version)
5. When submodule code executes, Python looks up `load_plan` in its own module namespace and finds the **synced reference**

---

### Architecture Diagram

```
triage_handlers.py (entry point)
    │
    ├─ imports: load_plan, command_runtime, etc. from desloppify.engine.plan
    │
    └─ cmd_plan_triage(args)
         │
         ├─ _sync_triage_module_bindings()  ← Propagates references
         │   │
         │   ├─→ _helpers_mod.load_plan = load_plan (now possibly monkeypatched)
         │   ├─→ _display_mod.load_plan = load_plan
         │   ├─→ _confirmations_mod.load_plan = load_plan
         │   └─→ ... (6 modules, 7 functions)
         │
         └─ Execute stage commands
              │
              ├─→ _confirmations_mod._cmd_confirm_stage(args)
              │    └─ Uses load_plan (found in _confirmations_mod namespace)
              │
              └─→ _display_mod._cmd_triage_dashboard(args)
                   └─ Uses load_plan (found in _display_mod namespace)


Test context (with monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(triage_mod, "load_plan", mock_fn)
           ↓
    cmd_plan_triage() runs
           ↓
    _sync_triage_module_bindings()  ← Copies the MOCKED load_plan to all submodules
           ↓
    Submodules see the mock
```

---

### Why This Pattern Exists: Circular Import Avoidance

**Historical context** (commits show): The triage subsystem was refactored from a monolithic 1660-line file into a split module architecture:
- Original: `triage_handlers.py` contained all logic inline
- Refactored: Logic split into `helpers.py`, `display.py`, `confirmations.py`, `_stage_flow_commands.py`, `_stage_completion_commands.py`, `_stage_validation.py`

Without the sync pattern, a **circular import** would arise:
```
triage_handlers.py
    ├─ imports _confirmations_mod (confirmations.py)
    └─ imports append_log_entry, load_plan, etc.

confirmations.py
    ├─ imports from triage_handlers to use those functions?  ✗ CIRCULAR
```

The solution: Keep functions in `triage_handlers`, import them from `desloppify.engine.plan`, and **dynamically sync references** to submodules at runtime.

---

### Design Issues & Assessment

#### **The Core Problem:**

1. **Fragile Test Mocking**: Tests MUST monkeypatch at `triage_handlers` level, not at the actual modules where functions are called
2. **Hidden Dependencies**: It's not obvious from reading `confirmations.py` that it relies on `_sync_triage_module_bindings()` being called
3. **Implicit Behavior**: The function is a side effect—no type hints reflect "this function modifies module state"
4. **Maintenance Burden**: Adding a new submodule or function requires updating the sync function manually
5. **Runtime Cost**: The function is called on every `plan triage` invocation (though cost is negligible)

#### **Why It's Tolerable (Currently):**

- **No circular imports** — the pattern avoids the design problem
- **Simple enough** — the code is straightforward, not cryptic
- **Backward compatible** — as noted in `CLAUDE.md`: "Remove re-export facades, wrapper shims, compat layers" — but this pattern predates that era
- **Tests work** — the pattern enables the test strategy

---

### Cleaner Design Alternatives

#### **Alternative 1: Dependency Injection (Recommended)**

Instead of importing functions directly and syncing them, pass them as parameters or via a context object:

```python
# triage_context.py
@dataclass
class TriageContext:
    """Encapsulates all triage dependencies."""
    command_runtime: Callable
    load_plan: Callable
    save_plan: Callable
    collect_triage_input: Callable
    detect_recurring_patterns: Callable
    append_log_entry: Callable
    extract_issue_citations: Callable

# triage_handlers.py
def cmd_plan_triage(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Run epic triage: staged workflow OBSERVE → REFLECT → ORGANIZE → COMMIT."""
    ctx = TriageContext(
        command_runtime=command_runtime,
        load_plan=load_plan,
        save_plan=save_plan,
        collect_triage_input=collect_triage_input,
        detect_recurring_patterns=detect_recurring_patterns,
        append_log_entry=append_log_entry,
        extract_issue_citations=extract_issue_citations,
    )
    runtime = ctx.command_runtime(args)
    state = runtime.state
    if not require_completed_scan(state):
        return
    # Pass context to all subcommands
    if getattr(args, "confirm", None):
        _confirmations_mod._cmd_confirm_stage(args, ctx)
    # ...

# confirmations.py
def _cmd_confirm_stage(args: argparse.Namespace, ctx: TriageContext) -> None:
    plan = ctx.load_plan()  # Use context, not module-level import
    # ...
```

**Pros:**
- No monkeypatch magic — tests inject a mock context
- Clear dependencies (visible in function signatures)
- Type-safe (TriageContext has type hints)
- Easy to add new dependencies without modifying multiple places
- Self-documenting

**Cons:**
- Requires threading the context through all function calls
- More verbose

---

#### **Alternative 2: Late-Binding with `__getattr__` (Clever but Risky)**

Define `__getattr__` at the module level to dynamically look up functions:

```python
# confirmations.py
_LATE_BINDINGS = {
    "command_runtime",
    "load_plan",
    "save_plan",
    "collect_triage_input",
    "detect_recurring_patterns",
    "append_log_entry",
}

def __getattr__(name: str):
    if name in _LATE_BINDINGS:
        import desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage_handlers as handlers
        return getattr(handlers, name)
    raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__} has no attribute {name}")
```

**Pros:**
- No explicit sync function
- Clean from the perspective of submodule code
- Automatically resolves to monkeypatched versions

**Cons:**
- Obscure (most Python developers don't expect `__getattr__` at module level)
- Harder to test and debug
- Breaks type checkers and IDEs
- Hidden performance cost (attribute lookup overhead)

---

#### **Alternative 3: Explicit Module-Level Placeholders**

Define `None` placeholders that sync populates:

```python
# confirmations.py
load_plan: Callable | None = None
save_plan: Callable | None = None

def _cmd_confirm_stage(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    # ... would use global variables
    plan = load_plan()  # This is now explicitly None until sync runs
```

**Pros:**
- Makes the dependency explicit in the module
- Type checker can see the type signature

**Cons:**
- Still requires the sync function (no improvement)
- Adds "None sentinel" pattern clutter
- More verbose

---

### Recommendation

**Worth fixing if:**
- You're already refactoring the triage subsystem
- Tests are becoming unwieldy
- You want type safety and IDE support

**Not worth fixing if:**
- The pattern is working fine and tests pass
- Refactoring would introduce risk

**Suggested path (if fixing):**

1. **Adopt Dependency Injection** — Create `TriageContext` dataclass
2. **Thread the context** through `_cmd_triage_start()` → `_cmd_stage_observe()` → `_record_observe_stage()`, etc.
3. **Update tests** to inject mocks directly into the context (no monkeypatching needed)
4. **Delete `_sync_triage_module_bindings()`** — no longer necessary

This would:
- Eliminate the implicit monkeypatch coupling
- Make dependencies explicit
- Enable better IDE/type-checker support
- Make the code self-documenting

---

### Conclusion

The `_sync_triage_module_bindings` pattern is a **pragmatic workaround** for enabling **test monkeypatching in a modular architecture** without creating circular imports. It's not elegant, but it works reliably.

**It's worth refactoring to dependency injection** if you're doing broader triage subsystem work, but it's not a critical fix on its own.

    14→def resolve_go_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
    15→    """Resolve Go imports to local files.
    16→
    17→    Go imports are module paths like "myproject/pkg/foo". We need the go.mod
    18→    module path to determine if an import is local, then map it to a file.
    19→    """
    20→    # Skip standard library and common external packages.
    21→    if not import_text or "/" not in import_text:
    22→        return None  # stdlib (e.g. "fmt", "os")
    23→
    24→    # Read go.mod to get module path.
    25→    go_mod = os.path.join(scan_path, "go.mod")
    26→    module_path = _read_go_module_path(go_mod, logger=logger)
    27→    if not module_path:
    28→        return None
    29→
    30→    if not import_text.startswith(module_path):
    31→        return None  # external package
    32→
    33→    # Map module-relative import to filesystem path.
    34→    rel_path = import_text[len(module_path) :].lstrip("/")
    35→    candidate_dir = os.path.join(scan_path, rel_path)
    36→
    37→    # Go imports point to packages (directories), not files.
    38→    # Return the directory — the coupling detector works with directories.
    39→    if os.path.isdir(candidate_dir):
    40→        # Find the first .go file in the package dir.
    41→        for f in sorted(os.listdir(candidate_dir)):
    42→            if f.endswith(".go") and not f.endswith("_test.go"):
    43→                return os.path.join(candidate_dir, f)
    44→    return None

    54→

    64→    path_parts = parts[:-1] if len(parts) > 1 else parts

    66→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):

    71→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
    72→        return candidate
    73→
    74→    # Try with all parts as path.
    75→    candidate = os.path.join(src_dir, *parts) + ".rs"
    76→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
    77→        return candidate

    79→    return None

   244→def resolve_swift_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   245→    """Best-effort local Swift import resolution.
   246→
   247→    Swift imports are usually module-level and often external. Resolve only when
   248→    the import path clearly matches a local ``.swift`` file.
   249→    """
   250→    text = import_text.strip()
   251→    if not text:
   252→        return None
   253→
   254→    module_path = text.replace(".", os.sep)
   255→    leaf = module_path.split(os.sep)[-1]
   256→    source_dir = os.path.dirname(source_file)
   257→
   258→    candidates = [
   259→        os.path.join(source_dir, module_path + ".swift"),
   260→        os.path.join(scan_path, module_path + ".swift"),
   261→        os.path.join(scan_path, "Sources", module_path + ".swift"),
   262→        os.path.join(scan_path, "Sources", module_path, f"{leaf}.swift"),
   263→        os.path.join(scan_path, module_path, f"{leaf}.swift"),
   264→    ]
   265→    seen: set[str] = set()
   266→    for candidate in candidates:
   267→        if candidate in seen:
   268→            continue
   269→        seen.add(candidate)
   270→        if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   271→            return candidate
   272→    return None

   565→    """Resolve F# `open MyApp.Module` to local files.
   566→
   567→    Converts dots to path separators, searches in src/ and root.
   568→    """
   569→    if not import_text:
   570→        return None
   571→
   572→    # Skip stdlib namespaces.
   573→    if any(import_text.startswith(p) for p in _FSHARP_STDLIB_PREFIXES):
   574→        return None
   575→
   576→    parts = import_text.split(".")
   577→    if not parts:
   578→        return None
   579→
   580→    # Try last part as filename.
   581→    filename = parts[-1] + ".fs"
   582→    for base_dir in ["src", ".", "lib"]:
   583→        # Try with namespace as directory structure.
   584→        if len(parts) > 1:
   585→            rel_path = os.path.join(*parts[:-1], filename)
   586→            candidate = os.path.join(scan_path, base_dir, rel_path)
   587→            if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   588→                return candidate
   589→        # Try flat (just filename).
   590→        candidate = os.path.join(scan_path, base_dir, filename)
   591→        if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   592→            return candidate
   593→
   594→    return None
   595→
   596→
   597→def _camel_to_snake(name: str) -> str:
   598→    """Convert CamelCase to snake_case."""
   599→    s1 = re.sub(r"(.)([A-Z][a-z]+)", r"\1_\2", name)
   600→    return re.sub(r"([a-z0-9])([A-Z])", r"\1_\2", s1).lower()
   601→
   602→
   603→def resolve_r_import(import_text: str, source_file: str, scan_path: str) -> str | None:
   604→    """Resolve R source() calls to local files.
   605→
   606→    library() and require() load external CRAN packages — return None.
   607→    source() loads local R scripts — resolve to path.
   608→    """
   609→    if not import_text:
   610→        return None
   611→
   612→    text = import_text.strip("\"'")
   613→
   614→    # Only source() calls reference local files.
   615→    # library("pkg") and require("pkg") are external packages.
   616→    if not text.endswith((".R", ".r")):
   617→        return None
   618→
   619→    # Resolve relative to source file directory.
   620→    base = os.path.dirname(source_file)
   621→    candidate = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, text))
   622→    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   623→        return candidate
   624→
   625→    # Try relative to scan path (R/ subdirectory is standard for packages).
   626→    for src_root in [".", "R"]:
   627→        candidate = os.path.join(scan_path, src_root, text)
   628→        if os.path.isfile(candidate):
   629→            return candidate
   630→
   631→    return None
   632→
   633→
   634→__all__ = [
   635→    "_GO_MODULE_CACHE",
   636→    "resolve_bash_source",
   637→    "resolve_csharp_import",
   638→    "resolve_cxx_include",

1→"""Shared import graph construction utilities for tree-sitter backends."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import os
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
     8→
     9→from ._cache import _PARSE_CACHE
    10→from ._extractors import _get_parser, _make_query, _run_query, _unwrap_node
    11→
    12→if TYPE_CHECKING:
    13→    from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter import TreeSitterLangSpec
    14→
    15→
    16→def ts_build_dep_graph(
    17→    path: Path,
    18→    spec: TreeSitterLangSpec,
    19→    file_list: list[str],
    20→) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    21→    """Build a dependency graph by parsing imports with tree-sitter.
    22→
    23→    Returns the same shape as Python/TS dep graphs:
    24→    {file: {"imports": set[str], "importers": set[str], "import_count": int, "importer_count": int}}
    25→    """
    26→    if not spec.import_query or not spec.resolve_import:
    27→        return {}
    28→
    29→    parser, language = _get_parser(spec.grammar)
    30→    query = _make_query(language, spec.import_query)
    31→
    32→    scan_path = str(path.resolve())
    33→    file_set = set(file_list)
    34→    graph: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    35→
    36→    # Initialize all files in the graph.
    37→    for f in file_list:
    38→        graph[f] = {"imports": set(), "importers": set()}
    39→
    40→    for filepath in file_list:
    41→        cached = _PARSE_CACHE.get_or_parse(filepath, parser, spec.grammar)
    42→        if cached is None:
    43→            continue
    44→        _source, tree = cached
    45→        matches = _run_query(query, tree.root_node)
    46→
    47→        for _pattern_idx, captures in matches:
    48→            path_node = _unwrap_node(captures.get("path"))
    49→            if not path_node:
    50→                continue
    51→
    52→            raw_text = path_node.text
    53→            import_text = (
    54→                raw_text.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    55→                if isinstance(raw_text, bytes)
    56→                else str(raw_text)
    57→            )
    58→
    59→            # Strip surrounding quotes if present.
    60→            import_text = import_text.strip("\"'`")
    61→
    62→            resolved = spec.resolve_import(import_text, filepath, scan_path)
    63→            if resolved is None:
    64→                continue
    65→
    66→            # Normalize to absolute path.
    67→            if not os.path.isabs(resolved):
    68→                resolved = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(scan_path, resolved))
    69→
    70→            # Only track edges within the scanned file set.
    71→            if resolved not in file_set:
    72→                continue
    73→
    74→            graph[filepath]["imports"].add(resolved)
    75→            if resolved in graph:
    76→                graph[resolved]["importers"].add(filepath)
    77→
    78→    # Finalize: add counts.
    79→    for data in graph.values():
    80→        data["import_count"] = len(data["imports"])
    81→        data["importer_count"] = len(data["importers"])
    82→
    83→    return graph
    84→
    85→
    86→def make_ts_dep_builder(spec: TreeSitterLangSpec, file_finder):
    87→    """Create a dep graph builder bound to a TreeSitterLangSpec + file finder.
    88→
    89→    Returns a callable with signature (path: Path) -> dict,
    90→    matching the contract expected by LangConfig.build_dep_graph.
    91→    """
    92→
    93→    def build(path: Path) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    94→        file_list = file_finder(path)
    95→        return ts_build_dep_graph(path, spec, file_list)
    96→
    97→    return build
    98→
    99→
   100→__all__ = ["make_ts_dep_builder", "ts_build_dep_graph"]
   101→

PATTERN ANALYSIS OF RESOLVERS
==============================

Looking at the 22 resolvers, they fall into clear architectural patterns:

1. RELATIVE-PATH RESOLVERS (simpler, 18-30 LOC):
   - resolve_ruby_import: relative + lib search (22 LOC)
   - resolve_cxx_include: relative-first + search dirs (23 LOC)
   - resolve_csharp_import: namespace mapping → filename (24 LOC)
   - resolve_perl_import: :: → / conversion + lib search (25 LOC)
   - resolve_dart_import: package: + relative (26 LOC)
   - resolve_haskell_import: dot-to-path conversion (26 LOC)
   - resolve_ocaml_import: module name → lowercase filename (26 LOC)
   - resolve_zig_import: relative + .zig extension (28 LOC)
   - resolve_erlang_include: relative + include/ dir (28 LOC)
   - resolve_bash_source: relative + .sh extension (29 LOC)
   - resolve_swift_import: multiple candidate paths (30 LOC)
   - resolve_r_import: source() calls only (30 LOC)

2. MODULE-PATH RESOLVERS (namespace to filesystem, 20-34 LOC):
   - resolve_kotlin_import: dot-split → path, .kt/.kts (20 LOC)
   - resolve_php_import: PSR-4-like mapping (20 LOC)
   - resolve_scala_import: dot-split → .scala (17 LOC)
   - resolve_lua_import: dot → path conversion (18 LOC)
   - resolve_js_import: relative-only ESM (18 LOC)
   - resolve_java_import: dot → path, .java (26 LOC)
   - resolve_elixir_import: CamelCase → snake_case (26 LOC)
   - resolve_fsharp_import: namespace + filename search (32 LOC)
   - resolve_rust_import: crate:: + multiple patterns (34 LOC)
   - resolve_go_import: module path + first .go file (32 LOC)

3. SHARED CONSTANTS/UTILITIES:
   - _PERL_SKIP_MODULES: frozenset, module exclusion list
   - _PERL_SKIP_PREFIXES: tuple, prefix filtering
   - _HASKELL_STDLIB_PREFIXES: tuple, stdlib filtering
   - _OCAML_STDLIB_MODULES: frozenset, stdlib filtering
   - _FSHARP_STDLIB_PREFIXES: tuple, stdlib filtering
   - _camel_to_snake: utility function (5 LOC) — used only by elixir_import

4. SHARED INFRASTRUCTURE (from _import_cache.py):
   - _GO_MODULE_CACHE: cache object
   - _read_go_module_path: function (used by resolve_go_import)

ARCHITECTURE OBSERVATIONS:
==========================

Shared Patterns (could factor):
1. "Search multiple source roots" pattern (Java, Kotlin, Scala, C#, Haskell, OCaml, F#, R, Ruby, Perl)
2. "Dot-to-path conversion" (Java, Kotlin, Scala, Lua, Elixir, PHP, Haskell, F#)
3. "Relative path + search dirs" (Ruby, C++, Bash, Erlang)
4. "Strip quotes, check extension" (Bash, Erlang, Zig, R, Perl)
5. "Skip stdlib/core modules" (Perl, Haskell, OCaml, F#)
6. "Try multiple extensions" (JS: .js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs/index.js)

BUT: Even though patterns exist, they're LANGUAGE-SPECIFIC because:
- Each language has its own source root conventions (src/, lib/, app/, src/main/java, etc.)
- Each has different namespace-to-path transformation rules
- Each has different extension handling
- Each has different stdlib modules to filter
- Trying to parameterize would create a confusing DSL that's harder to understand than 23 simple functions

=============================

## Thorough Analysis: `_import_resolvers.py` (658 LOC)

### 1. File Contents Summary

**22 language-specific import resolver functions:**

| Language | Function | LOC |
|----------|----------|-----|
| Go | `resolve_go_import` | 32 |
| Rust | `resolve_rust_import` | 34 |
| Ruby | `resolve_ruby_import` | 22 |
| Java | `resolve_java_import` | 26 |
| Kotlin | `resolve_kotlin_import` | 20 |
| C/C++ | `resolve_cxx_include` | 23 |
| PHP | `resolve_php_import` | 20 |
| Elixir | `resolve_elixir_import` | 26 |
| Lua | `resolve_lua_import` | 18 |
| Swift | `resolve_swift_import` | 30 |
| Scala | `resolve_scala_import` | 17 |
| C# | `resolve_csharp_import` | 24 |
| Dart | `resolve_dart_import` | 26 |
| JavaScript | `resolve_js_import` | 18 |
| Bash | `resolve_bash_source` | 29 |
| Perl | `resolve_perl_import` | 25 |
| Zig | `resolve_zig_import` | 28 |
| Haskell | `resolve_haskell_import` | 26 |
| Erlang | `resolve_erlang_include` | 28 |
| OCaml | `resolve_ocaml_import` | 26 |
| F# | `resolve_fsharp_import` | 32 |
| R | `resolve_r_import` | 30 |

**Utility/Constants:**
- `_camel_to_snake()` — 5 LOC (used only by Elixir resolver)
- `_PERL_SKIP_MODULES` — frozenset with ~8 core modules
- `_PERL_SKIP_PREFIXES` — tuple with ~6 prefixes
- `_HASKELL_STDLIB_PREFIXES` — tuple with ~8 stdlib prefixes
- `_OCAML_STDLIB_MODULES` — frozenset with ~20 stdlib modules
- `_FSHARP_STDLIB_PREFIXES` — tuple with 3 prefixes

**Module overhead:** ~93 LOC (docstring, imports, `__all__` list)

### 2. Resolver Architecture Patterns

The resolvers fall into **two clear families** (though with overlap):

**Family A: Relative-Path Resolvers** (resolve relative imports + search source dirs)
- Ruby, C++, Bash, Erlang, Zig, Dart, R, Swift
- Typical: start with file directory, add .extension, try fallback roots
- LOC range: 18–30

**Family B: Module-Path Resolvers** (namespace to filesystem mapping)
- Java, Kotlin, Scala, C#, PHP, Haskell, OCaml, F#, Lua, Elixir, JS
- Typical: split namespace by delimiter (`.`, `::`), map to directory structure
- Special cases: Go (module path + file), Rust (crate:: + multiple patterns)
- LOC range: 17–34

**Shared Patterns Across All:**
1. **"Search multiple source roots"** — Java, Kotlin, Scala, C#, Haskell, OCaml, F#, Ruby, Perl, R
2. **"Dot-to-path conversion"** — Java, Kotlin, Scala, Lua, Elixir, PHP, Haskell, F#
3. **"Strip quotes/extension handling"** — Bash, Erlang, Zig, R, Perl, C++
4. **"Filter stdlib/core modules"** — Perl, Haskell, OCaml, F#
5. **"Try multiple file extensions"** — JavaScript (.js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs, /index.js)

### 3. Are Resolvers Genuinely Different?

**YES.** While patterns exist, each resolver is fundamentally language-specific:

| Aspect | Why Different |
|--------|---------------|
| **Source root conventions** | Java: `src/main/java`, `src/test/java`, `app/src/main/java` • Ruby: `lib` • Go: implicit (from module path) • Elixir: `lib` |
| **Namespace→path rules** | Java: `com.example.Foo` → `com/example/Foo.java` • Elixir: `MyApp.Module` → `my_app/module.ex` (CamelCase→snake_case) • Rust: `crate::pkg::mod` tries both `pkg/mod.rs` and `pkg/mod/mod.rs` |
| **Extension handling** | Java: `.java` only • Kotlin: `.kt` AND `.kts` • JS: `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `/index.js` • Lua: `.lua` AND `init.lua` |
| **Stdlib filtering** | Perl: ~8 modules + prefixes • Haskell: ~8 prefixes • OCaml: ~20 modules • F#: 3 prefixes |
| **Special logic** | Go: extract module path from `go.mod` → needs cache • Dart: `package:` prefix parsing • Bash: shell quote stripping |

**Factoring these would be counterproductive** — a generic DSL (config-driven) would be harder to understand than 22 straightforward functions.

### 4. Natural Split Points

The file has **clear logical breaks** but splitting creates problems:

**Option A: One File Per Language** ❌
- Creates 22+ files in `desloppify/languages/_framework/treesitter/`
- Directory becomes unmanageable (~50 files instead of ~10)
- Import coordination complexity increases
- Doesn't reduce cognitive load (still need to understand each resolver)

**Option B: Group By Family** (3–4 files) ⚠️
```
_import_resolvers_relative.py  → Ruby, C++, Bash, Erlang, Zig, Dart, R, Swift
_import_resolvers_module.py    → Java, Kotlin, Scala, C#, PHP, Haskell, OCaml, F#, Lua, JS
_import_resolvers_special.py   → Go, Rust, Elixir
_import_resolvers.py (facade)  → registry + re-exports
```
Downside: Groupings are somewhat artificial (overlap in patterns). Benefits: reduced file size (~200–250 LOC each), but doesn't improve code clarity.

**Option C: Keep Single File + Add Structure** ✅ BEST
- Group resolvers visually with section comments
- Add a registry comment: `"Language → Resolver"` mapping
- Keep all resolvers discoverable in **one import**
- Keep the file searchable and maintainable

### 5. Is 658 LOC Problematic?

**SHORT ANSWER: No, it's reasonable.**

**Analysis:**
- **Functional content:** 565 LOC (22 × ~25 LOC average = very digestible)
- **Each function is self-contained:** no cross-dependencies, no state
- **Import/registry structure works well:** one file, one import from `_specs.py`
- **Historical context:** split from ~774 LOC `_imports.py` which combined resolvers + import graph logic
- **Discoverability:** grep finds the resolver you need instantly

**Actual pain points (if any):**
1. **Finding a resolver by language** — requires grep or scrolling
2. **Constants scattered** — `_PERL_SKIP_MODULES` at line 395, but Perl resolver at line 403
3. **One utility function** (`_camel_to_snake`) only used by Elixir; adds minor clutter

### 6. Historical Context (Split from `_imports.py`)

The split was **good engineering**:
- **Before:** ~774 LOC in `_imports.py` mixed resolvers + import graph building
- **After:** Cleanly separated into:
  - `_import_cache.py` (61 LOC) — Go module caching
  - `_import_resolvers.py` (658 LOC) — Per-language resolvers  ← This file
  - `_import_graph.py` (100 LOC) — Graph construction orchestrator
  - `_imports.py` (66 LOC) — Facade/re-exports

**This split was appropriate** because it separated concerns: caching, language-specific resolution, and orchestration.

### 7. Assessment & Verdict

| Criterion | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Actual file size** | 658 LOC is medium-sized, not problematic |
| **Code organization** | Good (one resolver per language, clear signature) |
| **Cognitive complexity** | Low (each resolver is ~25 LOC, independent logic) |
| **Maintainability** | Good (single file = easy import, one place to add a new language) |
| **Discoverability** | Adequate (grep finds it quickly) |
| **Refactoring opportunity** | LOW — splitting doesn't reduce complexity, just spreads it |

**Final Verdict:** **658 LOC is REASONABLE for this module. Further splitting would create file sprawl without clarity gains.**

### Recommendations

If you want to improve the file **without splitting**:

1. **Add section comments** grouping resolvers by family (relative-path vs. module-path vs. special)
2. **Add a registry comment at the top** mapping language → resolver function name
3. **Move `_camel_to_snake` to `_import_cache.py`** (or inline it in `resolve_elixir_import`)
4. **Group stdlib constants** after all resolvers (move lines 395–561 to end of file)
5. **Add docstring to each section** explaining the pattern (e.g., "Relative-path resolvers: start with source file dir")

These changes improve **navigation** without splitting the codebase.

    52→    if not normalized:
    53→        return False
    54→    for prefix in PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES:
    55→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    56→            return True
    57→    return False
    58→
    59→
    60→def importer_can_access_private(importer_module: str) -> bool:
    61→    """Return True when importer module is allowed to reference private APIs."""
    62→    normalized = importer_module.strip()
    63→    if not normalized:
    64→        return False
    65→    for prefix in PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES:
    66→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    67→            return True
    68→    return False
    69→
    70→
    71→def iter_soft_deprecated_module_paths() -> Iterable[str]:
    72→    """Yield python-module relative paths for deprecated compatibility modules."""
    73→    for module in sorted(SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES):
    74→        parts = module.split(".")
    75→        yield "/".join(parts) + ".py"

1→"""Import guards for deprecated compatibility facades."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import ast
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→
     8→_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
     9→_PACKAGE_ROOT = _PROJECT_ROOT / "desloppify"
    10→_ALLOWED_COMPAT_MODULES: set[str] = set()
    11→
    12→
    13→def _runtime_python_files() -> list[tuple[Path, str]]:
    14→    files: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
    15→    for path in _PACKAGE_ROOT.rglob("*.py"):
    16→        rel = path.relative_to(_PROJECT_ROOT).as_posix()
    17→        if "/tests/" in rel:
    18→            continue
    19→        if rel in _ALLOWED_COMPAT_MODULES:
    20→            continue
    21→        files.append((path, rel))
    22→    return files
    23→
    24→
    25→def _compat_import_violations(path: Path, rel: str) -> list[str]:
    26→    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(), filename=str(path))
    27→    violations: list[str] = []
    28→
    29→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
    30→        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
    31→            for alias in node.names:
    32→                if alias.name in {"desloppify.utils", "desloppify.file_discovery"}:
    33→                    violations.append(f"{rel}:{node.lineno} import {alias.name}")
    34→        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
    35→            module = node.module or ""
    36→            if module in {"desloppify.utils", "desloppify.file_discovery"}:
    37→                violations.append(f"{rel}:{node.lineno} from {module} import ...")
    38→                continue
    39→            if module == "desloppify":
    40→                for alias in node.names:
    41→                    if alias.name in {"utils", "file_discovery"}:
    42→                        violations.append(
    43→                            f"{rel}:{node.lineno} from desloppify import {alias.name}"
    44→                        )
    45→    return violations
    46→
    47→
    48→def test_runtime_code_avoids_deprecated_compat_facades():
    49→    violations: list[str] = []
    50→    for path, rel in _runtime_python_files():
    51→        violations.extend(_compat_import_violations(path, rel))
    52→    assert not violations, "runtime imports deprecated compat facades:\n" + "\n".join(
    53→        sorted(violations)
    54→    )
    55→
