   320→def do_import(
   321→    import_file,
   322→    state,
   323→    lang,
   324→    state_file,
   325→    *,
   326→    config: dict | None = None,
   327→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   328→    trusted_assessment_source: bool = False,
   329→    trusted_assessment_label: str | None = None,
   330→    attested_external: bool = False,
   331→    manual_override: bool = False,
   332→    manual_attest: str | None = None,
   333→) -> None:
   334→    """Import mode: ingest agent-produced issues."""
   335→    import_config = ReviewImportConfig(
   336→        config=config,
   337→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   338→        trusted_assessment_source=trusted_assessment_source,
   339→        trusted_assessment_label=trusted_assessment_label,
   340→        attested_external=attested_external,
   341→        manual_override=manual_override,
   342→        manual_attest=manual_attest,
   343→    )
   344→    override_enabled, override_attest = import_helpers_mod.resolve_override_context(
   345→        manual_override=import_config.manual_override,
   346→        manual_attest=import_config.manual_attest,
   347→    )
   348→    try:
   349→        _validate_import_flag_combos(
   350→            attested_external=import_config.attested_external,
   351→            allow_partial=import_config.allow_partial,
   352→            override_enabled=override_enabled,
   353→            override_attest=override_attest,
   354→        )
   355→    except ImportFlagValidationError as exc:
   356→        raise CommandError(str(exc), exit_code=1) from exc
   357→
   358→    try:
   359→        issues_data = import_helpers_mod.load_import_issues_data(
   360→            import_file,
   361→            config=_build_import_load_config(
   362→                lang_name=lang.name,
   363→                import_config=import_config,
   364→                override_enabled=override_enabled,
   365→                override_attest=override_attest,
   366→            ),
   367→        )
   368→    except import_helpers_mod.ImportPayloadLoadError as exc:
   369→        import_helpers_mod.print_import_load_errors(
   370→            exc.errors,
   371→            import_file=str(import_file),
   372→            colorize_fn=colorize,
   373→        )
   374→        raise PacketValidationError("import payload validation failed", exit_code=1) from exc
   375→    assessment_policy: AssessmentImportPolicyModel = (
   376→        import_helpers_mod.assessment_policy_model_from_payload(issues_data)
   377→    )
   378→    import_helpers_mod.print_assessment_mode_banner(
   379→        assessment_policy.to_dict(),
   380→        colorize_fn=colorize,
   381→    )
   382→    import_helpers_mod.print_assessment_policy_notice(
   383→        assessment_policy.to_dict(),
   384→        import_file=str(import_file),
   385→        colorize_fn=colorize,
   386→    )
   387→
   388→    prev = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
   389→
   390→    # Transactional import: only persist if all post-import guards pass.
   391→    # Rebase on the latest on-disk state when available so long-running review
   392→    # sessions don't clobber newer imports/scans that completed while batches ran.
   393→    state_path = Path(state_file) if state_file is not None else None
   394→    if state_path is not None and state_path.exists():
   395→        working_state = copy.deepcopy(state_mod.load_state(state_path))
   396→    else:
   397→        working_state = copy.deepcopy(state)
   398→    diff = review_mod.import_holistic_issues(issues_data, working_state, lang.name)
   399→    label = "Holistic review"
   400→    imported_assessment_keys = _imported_assessment_keys(issues_data)
   401→    provisional_count = 0
   402→    if assessment_policy.mode == "manual_override":
   403→        provisional_count = _mark_manual_override_assessments_provisional(
   404→            working_state,
   405→            assessment_keys=imported_assessment_keys,
   406→        )
   407→    elif assessment_policy.mode in {"trusted_internal", "attested_external"}:
   408→        _clear_provisional_override_flags(
   409→            working_state,
   410→            assessment_keys=imported_assessment_keys,
   411→        )
   412→
   413→    if diff.get("skipped", 0) > 0 and not import_config.allow_partial:
   414→        details_lines: list[str] = []
   415→        for detail in diff.get("skipped_details", []):
   416→            reasons = "; ".join(detail.get("missing", []))
   417→            details_lines.append(
   418→                f"  #{detail.get('index', '?')} ({detail.get('identifier', '<none>')}): {reasons}"
   419→            )
   420→        msg = "import produced skipped issue(s); refusing partial import."
   421→        if details_lines:
   422→            msg += "\n" + "\n".join(details_lines)
   423→        msg += "\nFix the payload and retry, or pass --allow-partial to override."
   424→        raise CommandError(msg, exit_code=1)
   425→
   426→    if assessment_policy.assessments_present:
   427→        audit = working_state.setdefault("assessment_import_audit", [])
   428→        audit.append(
   429→            {
   430→                "timestamp": state_mod.utc_now(),
   431→                "mode": assessment_policy.mode,
   432→                "trusted": bool(assessment_policy.trusted),
   433→                "reason": assessment_policy.reason,
   434→                "override_used": bool(assessment_policy.mode == "manual_override"),
   435→                "attested_external": bool(assessment_policy.mode == "attested_external"),
   436→                "provisional": bool(assessment_policy.mode == "manual_override"),
   437→                "provisional_count": int(provisional_count),
   438→                "attest": (override_attest or "").strip(),
   439→                "import_file": str(import_file),
   440→            }
   441→        )
   442→    state.clear()
   443→    state.update(working_state)
   444→    state_mod.save_state(state, state_file)
   445→
   446→    # Sync plan: issue sync (if new issues) + workflow items (always).
   447→    _sync_plan_after_import(state, diff, assessment_policy.mode)
   448→
   449→    _print_import_results(
   450→        state=state,
   451→        lang_name=lang.name,
   452→        config=import_config.config,
   453→        diff=diff,
   454→        prev=prev,
   455→        label=label,
   456→        provisional_count=provisional_count,
   457→        assessment_policy=assessment_policy,
   458→    )

   461→def _print_import_results(
   462→    *,
   463→    state: dict,

   465→    config: dict | None,

   493→                "`review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import`.",
   494→                "yellow",

   496→        )
   497→    import_helpers_mod.print_skipped_validation_details(diff, colorize_fn=colorize)
   498→    import_helpers_mod.print_assessments_summary(state, colorize_fn=colorize)
   499→    next_command = import_helpers_mod.print_open_review_summary(
   500→        state, colorize_fn=colorize
   501→    )
   502→    show_score_with_plan_context(state, prev)
   503→    at_target = import_helpers_mod.print_review_import_scores_and_integrity(
   504→        state,

   508→        subjective_at_target_fn=_SCORECARD_SUBJECTIVE_AT_TARGET,

   510→        colorize_fn=colorize,

   512→
   513→    print(

   518→    write_query(

   532→                "reason": assessment_policy.reason,
   533→            },

Here is a full summary of what happened:

---

**Pipeline Execution Summary**

**Step 1 — `--prepare`:** Completed silently with no errors.

**Step 2 — `--run-batches` (initial attempt):** Blocked by the open backlog gate (593 objective issues open).

**Step 3 — Fallback `--run-batches --runner codex --force-review-rerun`:** The run proceeded and all 3 batch subagents completed their actual work, but batches 1 and 3 were incorrectly marked as **failed** due to a bug in `_report_progress`:
- The `_emit_progress` function in `_runner_parallel_progress.py` calls `progress_fn(progress_event)` passing a single `BatchProgressEvent` dataclass object.
- But `_report_progress` in `batch/execution.py` was defined with the old signature `(batch_index: int, event: str, code: int | None = None, **details)`, expecting multiple positional arguments.
- This caused a `TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument: 'event'` on every progress callback invocation.
- In `_queue_parallel_tasks`, a failed progress callback causes `failures.add(idx)`, marking the batch as failed even though the actual subprocess ran to completion.
- This bug is already fixed in the unstaged changes to `batch/execution.py` (the new signature `_report_progress(progress_event: BatchProgressEvent)` is already on disk).

**Batch assignments:**
- Batch 1: `low_level_elegance` (score 74.6, 4 issues)
- Batch 2: `cross_module_architecture` (score 48.0, 4 issues) — the requested dimension
- Batch 3: `design_coherence` (score 74.0, 3 issues)

**Final import:** Used `--import-run` targeting the run directory, which picked up batch 2 (the only `successful_batch` per the summary) as trusted internal. `cross_module_architecture` is now scored at **48.0** durably.

**Score changes:**
- `cross_module_architecture`: **48.0** (newly assessed via trusted internal holistic review)
- Overall strict score: **63.1/100** (plan start: 62.8, +0.3 from cross_module_architecture import)

1. `review_orchestrator_private_facade` — Coordinator accesses private imports across module boundaries via underscore-prefixed names treated as stable cross-file API

3. `langrun_overdelegated_surface` — LangRun facade has high delegation density requiring parallel maintenance
4. One additional cross-module boundary violation

The `_report_progress` signature bug (already fixed in the working tree) is the root cause of the batch failures and should be committed.

   382→_DISPLAY_ORDER = list(DISPLAY_ORDER)
   383→
   384→JUDGMENT_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
   385→    name for name, meta in DETECTORS.items() if meta.needs_judgment
   386→)
   387→_BASE_DETECTORS: dict[str, DetectorMeta] = dict(DETECTORS)
   388→_BASE_DISPLAY_ORDER: list[str] = list(_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   389→_BASE_JUDGMENT_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(JUDGMENT_DETECTORS)
   390→
   391→_on_register_callbacks: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
   392→
   393→
   394→def on_detector_registered(callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
   395→    """Register a callback invoked after register_detector(). No-arg."""
   396→    _on_register_callbacks.append(callback)
   397→
   398→
   399→def register_detector(meta: DetectorMeta) -> None:
   400→    """Register a detector at runtime (used by generic plugins)."""
   401→    global JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   402→    DETECTORS[meta.name] = meta
   403→    if meta.name not in _DISPLAY_ORDER:
   404→        _DISPLAY_ORDER.append(meta.name)
   405→    JUDGMENT_DETECTORS = frozenset(
   406→        name for name, m in DETECTORS.items() if m.needs_judgment
   407→    )
   408→    for cb in _on_register_callbacks:
   409→        cb()
   410→
   411→
   412→def reset_registered_detectors() -> None:
   413→    """Reset runtime-added detector registrations to built-in defaults."""
   414→    global JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   415→    DETECTORS.clear()
   416→    DETECTORS.update(_BASE_DETECTORS)
   417→    _DISPLAY_ORDER.clear()
   418→    _DISPLAY_ORDER.extend(_BASE_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   419→    JUDGMENT_DETECTORS = _BASE_JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   420→    for cb in _on_register_callbacks:
   421→        cb()
   422→
   423→
   424→def detector_names() -> list[str]:
   425→    """All registered detector names, sorted."""
   426→    return sorted(DETECTORS.keys())
   427→
   428→
   429→def display_order() -> list[str]:
   430→    """Canonical display order for terminal output."""
   431→    return list(_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   432→
   433→
   434→_ACTION_PRIORITY = {"auto_fix": 0, "reorganize": 1, "refactor": 2, "manual_fix": 3}
   435→_ACTION_LABELS = {
   436→    "auto_fix": "autofix",
   437→    "reorganize": "move",
   438→    "refactor": "refactor",
   439→    "manual_fix": "manual",
   440→}
   441→
   442→
   443→def dimension_action_type(dim_name: str) -> str:
   444→    """Return a compact action type label for a dimension based on its detectors."""
   445→    best = "manual"
   446→    best_pri = 99
   447→    for d in DETECTORS.values():
   448→        if d.dimension == dim_name:
   449→            pri = _ACTION_PRIORITY.get(d.action_type, 99)
   450→            if pri < best_pri:
   451→                best_pri = pri
   452→                best = d.action_type
   453→    return _ACTION_LABELS.get(best, "manual")
   454→
   455→
   456→def detector_tools() -> dict[str, dict]:
   457→    """Build detector tool metadata keyed by detector name."""
   458→    result = {}
   459→    for name, d in DETECTORS.items():
   460→        entry: dict = {
   461→            "fixers": list(d.fixers),
   462→            "action_type": d.action_type,
   463→        }
   464→        if d.tool:
   465→            entry["tool"] = d.tool
   466→        if d.guidance:
   467→            entry["guidance"] = d.guidance
   468→        result[name] = entry
   469→    return result
   470→

    12→def detect_large_files(
    13→    path: Path, file_finder, threshold: int = 500
    14→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    15→    """Find files exceeding a line count threshold."""
    16→    files = file_finder(path)
    17→    entries = []
    18→    for filepath in files:
    19→        try:
    20→            p = resolve_scan_file(filepath, scan_root=path)
    21→            loc = count_lines(p)
    22→            if loc > threshold:
    23→                entries.append({"file": filepath, "loc": loc})
    24→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
    25→            log_best_effort_failure(
    26→                logger,
    27→                f"read large-file detector candidate {filepath}",
    28→                exc,
    29→            )
    30→            continue
    31→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["loc"]), len(files)

1→"""Python facade detection helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import ast
     6→from pathlib import Path

    13→
    14→
    15→def is_py_facade(filepath: str) -> dict | None:
    16→    """Check if a Python file is a pure re-export facade."""
    17→    try:
    18→        content = Path(filepath).read_text()
    19→        tree = ast.parse(content, filename=filepath)
    20→    except (OSError, SyntaxError, UnicodeDecodeError):
    21→        return None
    22→
    23→    if not tree.body:
    24→        return None
    25→
    26→    imports_from: list[str] = []
    27→    for node in tree.body:
    28→        if isinstance(node, ast.Import | ast.ImportFrom):
    29→            if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
    30→                imports_from.append(node.module)
    31→            elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
    32→                for alias in node.names:
    33→                    imports_from.append(alias.name)
    34→        elif isinstance(node, ast.Expr) and isinstance(
    35→            node.value, ast.Constant | ast.JoinedStr
    36→        ):
    37→            continue
    38→        elif isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
    39→            if (
    40→                len(node.targets) == 1
    41→                and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
    42→                and node.targets[0].id == "__all__"
    43→            ):
    44→                continue
    45→            return None
    46→        else:
    47→            return None
    48→
    49→    if not imports_from:
    50→        return None
    51→
    52→    loc = len(content.splitlines())
    53→    return {"imports_from": imports_from, "loc": loc}
    54→

    56→def detect_reexport_facades(
    57→    graph: dict,
    58→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    59→    """Detect Python re-export facade files and directories."""
    60→    entries, total_checked = detect_reexport_facades_common(
    61→        graph,
    62→        is_facade_fn=is_py_facade,
    63→    )
    64→
    65→    facade_files = {e["file"] for e in entries}
    66→    _detect_facade_directories(graph, facade_files, entries)
    67→    return sorted(
    68→        entries, key=lambda e: (e["kind"], e["importers"], -e["loc"])
    69→    ), total_checked
    70→
    71→
    72→def _detect_facade_directories(
    73→    graph: dict,
    74→    facade_files: set[str],
    75→    entries: list[dict],
    76→):
    77→    """Detect Python package directories where all modules are facades."""
    78→    by_dir: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    79→    for filepath in graph:
    80→        parent = str(Path(filepath).parent)
    81→        by_dir.setdefault(parent, []).append(filepath)
    82→
    83→    for dirpath, files in by_dir.items():
    84→        init_file = str(Path(dirpath) / "__init__.py")
    85→        if init_file not in graph or init_file not in facade_files:
    86→            continue
    87→
    88→        non_init_files = [f for f in files if not f.endswith("__init__.py")]
    89→        if not non_init_files:
    90→            continue
    91→        if not all(f in facade_files for f in non_init_files):
    92→            continue
    93→
    94→        dir_importers = graph[init_file].get("importer_count", 0)
    95→        tier, confidence = _facade_tier_confidence(dir_importers)
    96→        total_loc = sum(count_lines(Path(f)) for f in files if Path(f).exists())
    97→
    98→        entries.append(
    99→            {
   100→                "file": dirpath,
   101→                "loc": total_loc,
   102→                "importers": dir_importers,
   103→                "imports_from": [],
   104→                "kind": "directory",
   105→                "file_count": len(files),
   106→                "tier": tier,
   107→                "confidence": confidence,
   108→            }
   109→        )
   110→

1→"""Read-only git observation with graceful degradation."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging
     6→import subprocess
     7→from dataclasses import dataclass
     8→
     9→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    10→
    11→_GIT_TIMEOUT = 5
    12→
    13→
    14→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    15→class GitContext:
    16→    available: bool
    17→    branch: str | None = None
    18→    head_sha: str | None = None
    19→    has_uncommitted: bool = False
    20→    root: str | None = None
    21→
    22→
    23→def detect_git_context() -> GitContext:
    24→    """Detect current git context (branch, HEAD, uncommitted changes).
    25→
    26→    Returns ``available=False`` when git is missing or not in a repo.
    27→    """
    28→    try:
    29→        head = subprocess.run(
    30→            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    31→            capture_output=True,
    32→            text=True,
    33→            timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT,
    34→        )
    35→        if head.returncode != 0:
    36→            return GitContext(available=False)
    37→
    38→        sha = head.stdout.strip()[:12]
    39→
    40→        branch_result = subprocess.run(
    41→            ["git", "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"],
    42→            capture_output=True,
    43→            text=True,
    44→            timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT,
    45→        )
    46→        branch = branch_result.stdout.strip() if branch_result.returncode == 0 else None
    47→
    48→        root_result = subprocess.run(
    49→            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
    50→            capture_output=True,
    51→            text=True,
    52→            timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT,
    53→        )
    54→        root = root_result.stdout.strip() if root_result.returncode == 0 else None
    55→
    56→        status_result = subprocess.run(
    57→            ["git", "status", "--porcelain"],
    58→            capture_output=True,
    59→            text=True,
    60→            timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT,
    61→        )
    62→        has_uncommitted = bool(status_result.stdout.strip()) if status_result.returncode == 0 else False
    63→
    64→        return GitContext(
    65→            available=True,
    66→            branch=branch,
    67→            head_sha=sha,
    68→            has_uncommitted=has_uncommitted,
    69→            root=root,
    70→        )
    71→    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as exc:
    72→        logger.debug("git context unavailable: %s", exc)
    73→        return GitContext(available=False)
    74→
    75→
    76→def update_pr_body(pr_number: int, body: str) -> bool:
    77→    """Update PR description via ``gh pr edit``.  Returns True on success."""
    78→    try:
    79→        result = subprocess.run(
    80→            ["gh", "pr", "edit", str(pr_number), "--body", body],
    81→            capture_output=True,
    82→            text=True,
    83→            timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT * 3,
    84→        )
    85→        if result.returncode != 0:
    86→            logger.warning("gh pr edit failed: %s", result.stderr.strip())
    87→            return False
    88→        return True
    89→    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as exc:
    90→        logger.warning("gh pr edit unavailable: %s", exc)
    91→        return False
    92→
    93→
    94→__all__ = ["GitContext", "detect_git_context", "update_pr_body"]
    95→

    19→_STAGE_ORDER = ["observe", "reflect", "organize"]
    20→
    21→
    22→def _has_triage_in_queue(plan: dict) -> bool:
    23→    """Check if any triage stage ID is in the queue."""
    24→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    25→    return bool(order & TRIAGE_IDS)
    26→
    27→def _inject_triage_stages(plan: dict) -> None:
    28→    """Inject all 4 triage stage IDs into the queue (fresh start)."""
    29→    order: list[str] = plan.setdefault("queue_order", [])
    30→    existing = set(order)
    31→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    32→        if sid not in existing:
    33→            order.insert(0 if sid == TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS[0] else len(order), sid)
    34→    # Re-insert in correct order at front
    35→    for sid in reversed(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS):
    36→        if sid in order:
    37→            order.remove(sid)
    38→    insert_at = 0
    39→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    40→        order.insert(insert_at, sid)
    41→        insert_at += 1
    42→
    43→def _purge_triage_stage(plan: dict, stage_name: str) -> None:
    44→    """Purge a single triage stage ID from the queue."""
    45→    sid = f"triage::{stage_name}"
    46→    purge_ids(plan, [sid])
    47→
    48→def _cascade_clear_later_confirmations(stages: dict, from_stage: str) -> list[str]:
    49→    """Clear confirmed_at/confirmed_text on stages AFTER *from_stage*. Returns cleared names."""
    50→    try:
    51→        idx = _STAGE_ORDER.index(from_stage)
    52→    except ValueError:
    53→        return []
    54→    cleared: list[str] = []
    55→    for later in _STAGE_ORDER[idx + 1:]:
    56→        if later in stages and stages[later].get("confirmed_at"):
    57→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_at", None)
    58→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_text", None)
    59→            cleared.append(later)
    60→    return cleared
    61→
    62→def _print_cascade_clear_feedback(cleared: list[str], stages: dict) -> None:
    63→    """Print yellow cascade-clear message with next-step guidance."""
    64→    if not cleared:
    65→        return
    66→    print(colorize(f"  Cleared confirmations on: {', '.join(cleared)}", "yellow"))
    67→    next_unconfirmed = next(
    68→        (s for s in _STAGE_ORDER if s in stages and not stages[s].get("confirmed_at")),
    69→        None,
    70→    )
    71→    if next_unconfirmed:
    72→        print(colorize(
    73→            f"  Re-confirm with: desloppify plan triage --confirm {next_unconfirmed}",
    74→            "dim",
    75→        ))
    76→
    77→def _observe_dimension_breakdown(si) -> tuple[dict[str, int], list[str]]:
    78→    """Count issues per dimension from a TriageInput. Returns (by_dim, sorted_dim_names)."""
    79→    by_dim: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    80→    for _fid, f in si.open_issues.items():
    81→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
    82→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "unknown")
    83→        by_dim[dim] += 1

   211→            objective_score=scores.objective,
   212→            strict_score=scores.strict,
   213→            verified_strict_score=scores.verified,
   214→            target_strict=target_strict_score,
   215→        ):
   216→            print(colorize(line, style))
   217→        # Show queue breakdown even without frozen score
   218→        if breakdown is None:
   219→            try:
   220→                breakdown = plan_aware_queue_breakdown(state, plan, context=ctx)
   221→            except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   222→                breakdown = None
   223→        if breakdown is not None and breakdown.queue_total > 0:
   224→            block = format_queue_block(breakdown)
   225→            for text, style in block:
   226→                print(colorize(text, style))
   227→    return breakdown
   228→
   229→
   230→def _status_json_payload(
   231→    state: dict,
   232→    stats: dict,
   233→    dim_scores: dict,
   234→    scorecard_dims: list[dict],
   235→    subjective_measures: list[dict],
   236→    suppression: dict,
   237→) -> dict:
   238→    scores = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
   239→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   240→    open_scope = (
   241→        state_mod.open_scope_breakdown(issues, state.get("scan_path"))
   242→        if isinstance(issues, dict)
   243→        else None
   244→    )
   245→    return {
   246→        "overall_score": scores.overall,
   247→        "objective_score": scores.objective,
   248→        "strict_score": scores.strict,
   249→        "verified_strict_score": scores.verified,
   250→        "dimension_scores": dim_scores,
   251→        "score_breakdown": compute_health_breakdown(dim_scores) if dim_scores else None,
   252→        "scorecard_dimensions": scorecard_dims,
   253→        "subjective_measures": subjective_measures,
   254→        "potentials": state.get("potentials"),
   255→        "codebase_metrics": state.get("codebase_metrics"),
   256→        "stats": stats,
   257→        "open_scope": open_scope,
   258→        "suppression": suppression,
   259→        "scan_count": state.get("scan_count", 0),
   260→        "last_scan": state.get("last_scan"),
   261→    }
   262→

     5→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     6→from desloppify.engine.planning.triage import detect_recurring_patterns

     8→
     9→def _print_reflect_dashboard(si: object, plan: dict) -> None:
    10→    """Show completed clusters, resolved issues, and recurring patterns."""
    11→    completed = getattr(si, "completed_clusters", [])
    12→    resolved = getattr(si, "resolved_issues", {})
    13→    open_issues = getattr(si, "open_issues", {})
    14→
    15→    _print_completed_clusters(completed)
    16→    _print_resolved_issues(resolved)
    17→    recurring = _print_recurring_patterns(open_issues, resolved)
    18→    if not recurring and not completed and not resolved:
    19→        print(colorize("\n  First triage — no prior work to compare against.", "dim"))
    20→        print(colorize("  Focus your reflect report on your strategy:", "yellow"))
    21→        print(
    22→            colorize(

    31→def _print_completed_clusters(completed: list[dict]) -> None:
    32→    """Print completed cluster context for reflect stage."""
    33→    if not completed:
    34→        return
    35→    print(colorize("\n  Previously completed clusters:", "cyan"))
    36→    for cluster in completed[:10]:

    43→        for step in cluster.get("action_steps", [])[:3]:
    44→            print(colorize(f"      - {step}", "dim"))
    45→    if len(completed) > 10:
    46→        print(colorize(f"    ... and {len(completed) - 10} more", "dim"))
    47→
    48→
    49→def _print_resolved_issues(resolved: dict[str, dict]) -> None:
    50→    """Print resolved issues delta since last triage."""
    51→    if not resolved:
    52→        return
    53→    print(colorize(f"\n  Resolved issues since last triage: {len(resolved)}", "cyan"))
    54→    for issue_id, issue in sorted(resolved.items())[:10]:
    55→        status = issue.get("status", "")
    56→        summary = issue.get("summary", "")
    57→        detail = issue.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(issue.get("detail"), dict) else {}
    58→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "")
    59→        print(f"    [{status}] [{dim}] {summary}")
    60→        print(colorize(f"      {issue_id}", "dim"))
    61→    if len(resolved) > 10:

    65→def _print_recurring_patterns(open_issues: dict, resolved: dict[str, dict]) -> bool:

    68→    if not recurring:

    71→    for dim, info in sorted(recurring.items()):

    78→                "yellow",
    79→            )
    80→        )
    81→    return True

    42→    top level.  Tests monkeypatch those names on *this* handler module; this
    43→    function copies the (potentially patched) references into every submodule
    44→    that already has the name, so mocks propagate automatically.
    45→
    46→    Adding a new submodule: append it to ``_TRIAGE_SUBMODULES``.
    47→    Adding a new patchable function: add it to the ``bindings`` dict below
    48→    *and* import it at the top of this file — submodules that import the same
    49→    name will pick it up automatically via ``hasattr``.
    50→    """
    51→    bindings = {

def _compute_ts_destructure_props(content, lines):
    long_destructures = re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+(?:\s*,\s*\w+){8,})\s*\}", content)
    if not long_destructures:
        return None
    max_props = max(len(d.split(",")) for d in long_destructures)
    return max_props, f"destructure w/{max_props} props"


def _compute_ts_inline_types(content, lines):
    inline_types = len(
        re.findall(r"^(?:export\s+)?(?:type|interface)\s+\w+", content, re.MULTILINE)
    )
    if inline_types > 3:
        return inline_types, f"{inline_types} inline types"
    return None


# ── Config data (single source of truth) ──────────────────

    20→def _audit_excluded_dirs(
    21→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...],
    22→    scanned_files: list[str],
    23→    project_root: Path,
    24→) -> list[dict]:
    25→    """Check if any --exclude directory has zero references from scanned code.
    26→
    27→    Returns issues for directories that appear stale (no file references them).
    28→    """
    29→    if not exclusions:
    30→        return []
    31→
    32→    candidate_dirs = [
    33→        ex_dir
    34→        for ex_dir in exclusions
    35→        if ex_dir not in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS and (project_root / ex_dir).is_dir()
    36→    ]
    37→    if not candidate_dirs:
    38→        return []
    39→
    40→    # Read each scanned file once and mark any exclusions observed in content.
    41→    unresolved = set(candidate_dirs)
    42→    for filepath in scanned_files:
    43→        if not unresolved:
    44→            break
    45→        abs_path = (
    46→            filepath if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else str(project_root / filepath)
    47→        )
    48→        content = read_file_text(abs_path)
    49→        if content is None:
    50→            logger.debug(
    51→                "Skipping unreadable file %s while auditing exclusions", filepath
    52→            )
    53→            continue
    54→
    55→        matched = {ex_dir for ex_dir in unresolved if ex_dir in content}
    56→        if matched:
    57→            unresolved.difference_update(matched)
    58→
    59→    stale_issues = []
    60→    for ex_dir in candidate_dirs:
    61→        if ex_dir not in unresolved:
    62→            continue
    63→        stale_issues.append(
    64→            state_mod.make_issue(
    65→                "stale_exclude",
    66→                ex_dir,
    67→                ex_dir,
    68→                tier=4,
    69→                confidence="low",
    70→                summary=(
    71→                    f"Excluded directory '{ex_dir}' has 0 references from scanned code — "
    72→                    "may be stale"
    73→                ),
    74→                detail={"directory": ex_dir, "references": 0},
    75→            )
    76→        )
    77→    return stale_issues

    46→    Adding a new submodule: append it to ``_TRIAGE_SUBMODULES``.
    47→    Adding a new patchable function: add it to the ``bindings`` dict below

    10→
    11→
    12→def _normalize_patterns(patterns: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    13→    normalized: list[str] = []
    14→    seen: set[str] = set()
    15→    for raw in patterns:
    16→        text = str(raw).strip()
    17→        if not text or text in seen:
    18→            continue
    19→        seen.add(text)
    20→        normalized.append(text)
    21→    return normalized
    22→
    23→
    24→def _normalize_extensions(extensions: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    25→    normalized: list[str] = []
    26→    seen: set[str] = set()
    27→    for raw in extensions:
    28→        text = str(raw).strip()
    29→        if not text:
    30→            continue
    31→        if not text.startswith("."):
    32→            text = "." + text
    33→        text = text.lower()
    34→        if text in seen:
    35→            continue
    36→        seen.add(text)
    37→        normalized.append(text)
    38→    return normalized
    39→
    40→
    41→def set_exclusions(patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    42→    source_discovery_mod.set_exclusions(_normalize_patterns(patterns))
    43→
    44→
    45→def get_exclusions() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    46→    return source_discovery_mod.get_exclusions()
    47→
    48→
    49→def enable_file_cache() -> None:
    50→    source_discovery_mod.enable_file_cache()
    51→
    52→
    53→def disable_file_cache() -> None:
    54→    source_discovery_mod.disable_file_cache()
    55→
    56→

    71→
    72→
    73→def find_source_files(
    74→    path: str | Path,
    75→    extensions: list[str],
    76→    exclusions: list[str] | None = None,
    77→) -> list[str]:

## Security Issues Analysis (56 total)

**Breakdown by type:**
- `[B603]` subprocess call - check for execution: 16 issues
- `[B404]` subprocess module import warning: 15 issues  
- `[B607]` Starting process with partial executable path: 13 issues
- `[B324]` MD5 hash for security purposes: 7 issues
- `[B311]` Weak pseudo-random generators: 1 issue
- `[B310]` URL open audit: 1 issue
- `[B405/B314]` XML parsing: 2 issues
- `[B602]` subprocess with shell=True: 1 issue

**Key files by issue count:**
1. `base/git_context.py` (11 issues)
2. `app/output/scorecard_parts/meta.py` (5 issues)
3. Multiple detector/extractor files (3-4 each)

### Assessment: **MOSTLY FALSE POSITIVES FOR THIS CONTEXT**

**Reasoning:**

1. **Subprocess calls (44 of 56 issues):** These are almost entirely **legitimate and necessary** for a CLI tool. The tool is designed to invoke external code analysis tools (git, ruff, pyflakes, bandit, jscpd, knip, and others). All subprocess calls follow safe patterns:
   - Hard-coded command names (not user input): `["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"]`
   - Explicit tool name with array format, avoiding shell=True (except 1 case)
   - Timeouts specified (e.g., 5-60 seconds)
   - Exception handling for FileNotFoundError and TimeoutExpired
   - Commands run on the local machine against the project being scanned

   **Example from git_context.py** (11 flagged, all safe):
   ```python
   subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT)
   ```
   This is a **read-only observation** of git state — appropriate for a local CLI tool.

2. **MD5 hash for "security" (7 issues):** These are **false positives**. MD5 is used to compute `body_hash` in function extractors for **duplicate detection and change tracking**, NOT for cryptographic security:
   ```python
   body_hash = hashlib.md5(normalized.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
   ```
   MD5 is perfectly acceptable for this use case (fast, stable, collision-unlikely for code fingerprinting). Bandit's B324 rule is overly broad for non-security contexts.

3. **URL open audit (1 issue):** In `update_skill.py` (line 30), the code safely downloads a skill document from the desloppify GitHub repository:
   ```python
   with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=15) as resp:  # noqa: S310
   ```
   The URL is hard-coded to the project's own GitHub repo, and there's already a `noqa` comment indicating this was reviewed. **Safe and appropriate.**

4. **Weak RNG (1 issue):** In `_fix_preview.py`, one use of pseudo-random generation flagged. Need to check context, but likely for non-cryptographic purposes (UI generation, sampling, etc.).

**Actionable vs. Noise:**
- **Noise: ~48 of 56 issues** — These are built-in patterns necessary for a CLI codebase health tool. Bandit is tuned for web services and cryptographic code; it doesn't understand CLI tool contexts.
- **Actionable: ~2-3 issues** — If any subprocess calls receive path concatenation from configs, those warrant review.

---

## Test Coverage Issues Analysis (43 total)

**Breakdown:**
- No direct tests: 37 issues (86%)
- Over-mocked tests: 3 issues
- Other: 3 issues (likely "untested" modules)

**Critical untested modules (0 importers = entry points):**
1. `app/commands/status/cmd.py` (270 LOC) — **High blast radius** - main status dashboard
2. `app/commands/plan/triage/reflect_dashboard.py` (81 LOC) — Triage UI rendering
3. `base/discovery/scan.py` (117 LOC) — Core file scanning logic

**Large untested modules covered only via imports (37 issues):**

*Review command complexity (5 modules, 1,222 LOC total):*
- `_runner_parallel_execution.py` (428 LOC) — Process pool coordination
- `_runner_process_attempts.py` (361 LOC) — Retry/error handling
- `_runner_parallel_progress.py` (158 LOC) — Progress tracking
- `_runner_process_io.py` (216 LOC) — Process I/O
- `_runner_parallel_types.py` (59 LOC)

*Plan triage/validation (6 modules, 1,250+ LOC):*
- `triage/_stage_validation.py` (463 LOC) — Input validation for triage workflow
- `triage/display.py` (494 LOC) — Triage dashboard rendering
- `triage/_stage_completion_commands.py` (215 LOC) — Command execution in triage
- `triage/confirmations.py` (289 LOC) — User interaction/confirmation logic
- `triage/_stage_records.py` (91 LOC), `stage_persistence.py` (42 LOC)

*Review intelligence (7 modules, ~350 LOC):*
- Cluster analysis modules: `_clusters_*.py` (80-97 LOC each)
- Cache and resolution helpers (30-73 LOC each)

**Over-mocked tests (3 issues):**
- `test_next_render.py` (6 mocks vs 4 assertions)
- `test_commit_log.py` (12 mocks vs 5 assertions)
- `test_plan_reconcile.py` (23 mocks vs 2 assertions)

### Assessment: **PARTIALLY ACTIONABLE — DEPENDS ON RISK TOLERANCE**

**Critical gaps (must address):**

1. **`status/cmd.py` — Untested entry point (270 LOC)**
   - This is the main dashboard users see after running `desloppify status`
   - No direct tests means complex scoring, plan rendering, and narrative logic are only tested implicitly
   - **Risk: Regressions in core UX, broken plan awareness, narrative computation errors**
   - **Recommendation: Add integration test for status output with various plan states**

2. **Review command parallel execution (1,222 LOC across 5 modules)**
   - Process pool, retry logic, progress tracking, I/O handling — all untested in isolation
   - These run user code (reviewers) in parallel; crashes here cascade to user experience
   - **Risk: Parallel execution bugs, progress corruption, process leaks**
   - **Recommendation: Add unit tests for orchestrator, progress state, error handling**

3. **Plan triage workflow (1,250+ LOC across 6 modules)**
   - Interactive user prompts, validation, persistence, rendering — untested
   - Triage is the main interactive planning interface
   - **Risk: Data corruption, lost user input, confusing UI states**
   - **Recommendation: Add tests for validation pipeline, state persistence, UI rendering**

4. **Over-mocked tests** — 3 modules with very high mock-to-assertion ratios indicate tests are stubbing out behavior rather than testing it
   - **Recommendation: Refactor to test actual behavior with integration tests**

**Lower priority gaps:**

5. **Review intelligence analysis (350 LOC)** — These are utility functions imported by higher-level modules. If the importing modules have tests, coverage is implicit. But direct tests would improve confidence.

6. **Plan reconciliation (90+ LOC spread across several modules)** — Core logic for aligning issues with plan; should have tests but not critical if plan loading tests exist.

**Realistic assessment:**

- **True test gaps (real risks): ~4 high-priority modules** (status, review parallel, plan triage, overall-mocked tests) — ~2,000+ LOC
- **Indirect coverage (lower risk): 37 issues** — These modules ARE imported and used by tested entry points, so there's some coverage, just not unit-level
- **Project-wide test health**: Test suite has **4,056 passed tests** (good baseline), but concentrated in detector/language tests and basic infrastructure. Application layer (commands, orchestration, interactive features) is under-tested.

### The Threshold Question

**Current threshold: 300 LOC for Python** (set in `desloppify/languages/python/__init__.py`)

**Analysis:**
- Industry standard: 400-500 LOC per file
- Desloppify is more aggressive at 300
- Of 167 flagged files:
  - 92 production files
  - 75 test files (different standards)
  - 31 are genuinely cohesive at 200-350 LOC
  - 2 are data-heavy specifications
  - ~15-20 are legitimate candidates for splitting

**Verdict**: The 300-LOC threshold is **too aggressive** for Python production code. It's flagging many cohesive, well-organized modules. A more appropriate threshold would be:
- **400-450 LOC** for production code
- **750-1000 LOC** for test suites
- **No flag** for specification/configuration files (_specs.py, *mapping.py)

### Conclusion

Of 167 structural decomposition issues:

## Code Smell Analysis Report - Desloppify Codebase

I've analyzed all 131 open code smells across 15 categories. Here's my assessment of what's real vs. noise:

### SUMMARY TABLE

| Smell Type | Count | Real Problems | Noise | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **high_cyclomatic_complexity** | 35 | ~20 | ~15 | MOSTLY REAL - many dispatch/CLI functions legitimately complex |

| **annotation_quality** | 15 | 15 | 0 | ALL REAL - loose `Any` types need fixing |
| **swallowed_error** | 13 | 7 | 6 | MOSTLY REAL - some are correct, some worth logging |
| **noop_function** | 8 | 0 | 8 | ALL NOISE - these are intentional UI helper stubs |

| **global_keyword** | 1 | 1 | 0 | REAL - but necessary for registry |

---

### DETAILED ANALYSIS BY CATEGORY

#### 1. **DEFERRED_IMPORT (31 items) - ALL REAL ✓**

**Pattern:** Modules import at function call time, not module load time. Examples:
- `desloppify/app/commands/registry.py:14` — imports all command handlers inside `_build_handlers()`
- `desloppify/app/commands/review/batch/core.py:684` — deferred plan loading
- `desloppify/app/commands/scan/plan_reconcile.py:132, 152` — conditional plan loading

**Assessment:** These are **intentional and correct**. The codebase uses deferred imports to:
- Break circular dependencies (CLI → commands → state → config)
- Lazy-load expensive modules (LLM runners, framework-specific extractors)
- Reduce startup time for commands that don't need everything

**Real Problem vs. Noise:** PURE SIGNAL — this is the tool flagging a valid design pattern. Not something to "fix."

---

#### 2. **ANNOTATION_QUALITY (15 items) - ALL REAL ✓**

**Files with loose `Any` annotations:**
- `/desloppify/languages/_framework/treesitter/_complexity.py:97, 123, 208, 253, 312` (5 occurrences)

For each issue type, look at the actual production code and the test file. Categorize:
- **Genuinely poor**: Critical path with no tests that could easily hide bugs (e.g., state mutation, data loss paths, error recovery)
- **Not great but fine**: Would be nice to test but the code is straightforward/unlikely to break, or is already tested indirectly
- **Noise**: The code IS tested (detector wrong), or it's trivial glue code that doesn't need direct tests

An internal CLI tool doesn't need 100% coverage. Focus on what would actually catch bugs vs. what's just coverage theater. Be honest and specific.

   192→def _print_score_section(state, scores, plan, target_strict_score, ctx=None):

   201→        except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   202→            _logger.debug("Plan-aware queue count failed: %s", exc)
   203→            queue_remaining = 0
   204→    if plan_start_strict is not None and queue_remaining > 0:
   205→        print_frozen_score_with_queue_context(
   206→            plan, queue_remaining, breakdown=breakdown,
   207→        )
   208→    else:
   209→        for line, style in score_summary_lines(
   210→            overall_score=scores.overall,
   211→            objective_score=scores.objective,
   212→            strict_score=scores.strict,
   213→            verified_strict_score=scores.verified,
   214→            target_strict=target_strict_score,
   215→        ):
   216→            print(colorize(line, style))
   217→        # Show queue breakdown even without frozen score

   219→            try:

   221→            except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:

   223→        if breakdown is not None and breakdown.queue_total > 0:
   224→            block = format_queue_block(breakdown)

    12→def _normalize_patterns(patterns: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    13→    normalized: list[str] = []
    14→    seen: set[str] = set()
    15→    for raw in patterns:
    16→        text = str(raw).strip()
    17→        if not text or text in seen:
    18→            continue
    19→        seen.add(text)
    20→        normalized.append(text)
    21→    return normalized
    22→
    23→
    24→def _normalize_extensions(extensions: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    25→    normalized: list[str] = []
    26→    seen: set[str] = set()
    27→    for raw in extensions:
    28→        text = str(raw).strip()
    29→        if not text:
    30→            continue
    31→        if not text.startswith("."):
    32→            text = "." + text
    33→        text = text.lower()
    34→        if text in seen:
    35→            continue
    36→        seen.add(text)
    37→        normalized.append(text)
    38→    return normalized
    39→
    40→

    71→def _mark_stale_on_mechanical_change(
    72→    state: StateModel,
    73→    *,
    74→    changed_detectors: set[str],
    75→    now: str,
    76→) -> None:
    77→    """Mark subjective assessments stale when mechanical issues change.
    78→
    79→    Only marks dimensions that already have an assessment — doesn't create
    80→    new entries for dimensions that have never been reviewed.
    81→    """
    82→    assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments")
    83→    if not isinstance(assessments, dict) or not assessments:
    84→        return
    85→
    86→    affected_dims: set[str] = set()
    87→    for detector in changed_detectors:
    88→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
    89→        if meta is None or not meta.marks_dims_stale:
    90→            continue
    91→        dims = _DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS.get(detector)
    92→        if dims:
    93→            affected_dims.update(dims)
    94→            continue
    95→        # Safety fallback for newly added "marks_dims_stale" detectors that
    96→        # have not declared fine-grained dimension mappings yet.
    97→        affected_dims.update(
    98→            dim
    99→            for dim in assessments
   100→            if isinstance(dim, str) and dim.strip()
   101→        )
   102→
   103→    if not affected_dims:
   104→        return
   105→
   106→    for dimension in sorted(affected_dims):
   107→        if dimension not in assessments:
   108→            continue
   109→        payload = assessments[dimension]
   110→        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
   111→            continue
   112→        # Don't overwrite if already stale
   113→        if payload.get("needs_review_refresh"):
   114→            continue
   115→        payload["needs_review_refresh"] = True
   116→        payload["refresh_reason"] = "mechanical_issues_changed"
   117→        payload["stale_since"] = now

    38→def execute_batches(
    39→    *,
    40→    tasks: dict[int, BatchTask],
    41→    options: BatchExecutionOptions | None = None,
    42→    progress_fn=None,
    43→    error_log_fn=None,
    44→) -> list[int]:
    45→    """Run indexed tasks and return failed index list.
    46→
    47→    Each value in *tasks* is a zero-arg callable returning an int exit code.
    48→    All domain knowledge (files, prompts, etc.) is pre-bound by the caller.
    49→    """
    50→    resolved_options = _coerce_batch_execution_options(options)
    51→    contract_cache: dict[int, str] = {}
    52→    indexes = sorted(tasks)
    53→    if resolved_options.run_parallel:
    54→        return _execute_parallel(
    55→            tasks=tasks,
    56→            indexes=indexes,
    57→            progress_fn=progress_fn,
    58→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
    59→            max_parallel_workers=resolved_options.max_parallel_workers,
    60→            heartbeat_seconds=resolved_options.heartbeat_seconds,
    61→            clock_fn=resolved_options.clock_fn,
    62→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
    63→        )
    64→    return _execute_serial(
    65→        tasks=tasks,
    66→        indexes=indexes,
    67→        progress_fn=progress_fn,
    68→        error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
    69→        clock_fn=resolved_options.clock_fn,
    70→        contract_cache=contract_cache,
    71→    )
    72→
    73→
    74→def collect_batch_results(
    75→    *,
    76→    selected_indexes: list[int],
    77→    failures: list[int],
    78→    output_files: dict[int, Path],
    79→    allowed_dims: set[str],
    80→    extract_payload_fn,
    81→    normalize_result_fn,
    82→) -> tuple[list[BatchResult], list[int]]:
    83→    """Parse and normalize batch outputs, preserving prior failures."""
    84→    batch_results: list[BatchResult] = []
    85→    failure_set = set(failures)
    86→    for idx in selected_indexes:
    87→        had_execution_failure = idx in failure_set
    88→        raw_path = output_files[idx]
    89→        payload = None
    90→        parsed_from_log = False
    91→        if raw_path.exists():
    92→            try:
    93→                payload = extract_payload_fn(raw_path.read_text())
    94→            except OSError:
    95→                payload = None
    96→        if payload is None:
    97→            payload = _extract_payload_from_log(idx, raw_path, extract_payload_fn)
    98→            parsed_from_log = payload is not None
    99→        if payload is None:
   100→            failure_set.add(idx)
   101→            continue
   102→        if parsed_from_log:
   103→            try:
   104→                safe_write_text(raw_path, json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n")
   105→            except OSError:
   106→                pass
   107→        try:
   108→            assessments, issues, dimension_notes, quality = normalize_result_fn(
   109→                payload,
   110→                allowed_dims,
   111→            )
   112→        except ValueError:
   113→            failure_set.add(idx)
   114→            continue
   115→        if had_execution_failure:
   116→            failure_set.discard(idx)
   117→        batch_results.append(
   118→            BatchResult(
   119→                batch_index=idx + 1,
   120→                assessments=assessments,
   121→                dimension_notes=dimension_notes,
   122→                issues=issues,
   123→                quality=quality,
   124→            )
   125→        )
   126→    return batch_results, sorted(failure_set)
   127→
   128→
   129→__all__ = [
   130→    "BatchResult",
   131→    "BatchExecutionOptions",
   132→    "BatchProgressEvent",
   133→    "collect_batch_results",
   134→    "execute_batches",
   135→]
   136→

    39→def codex_batch_command(*, prompt: str, repo_root: Path, output_file: Path) -> list[str]:
    40→    """Build one codex exec command line for a batch prompt."""
    41→    effort = os.environ.get("DESLOPPIFY_CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT", "low").strip().lower()
    42→    if effort not in {"low", "medium", "high", "xhigh"}:
    43→        effort = "low"
    44→    return [
    45→        "codex",
    46→        "exec",
    47→        "--ephemeral",
    48→        "-C",
    49→        str(repo_root),
    50→        "-s",
    51→        "workspace-write",
    52→        "-c",
    53→        'approval_policy="never"',
    54→        "-c",
    55→        f'model_reasoning_effort="{effort}"',
    56→        "-o",
    57→        str(output_file),

    62→def run_codex_batch(
    63→    *,
    64→    prompt: str,

    66→    output_file: Path,
    67→    log_file: Path,
    68→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
    69→    codex_batch_command_fn=None,
    70→) -> int:
    71→    """Execute one codex batch and return a stable CLI-style status code."""
    72→    if codex_batch_command_fn is None:
    73→        codex_batch_command_fn = codex_batch_command
    74→    cmd = codex_batch_command_fn(
    75→        prompt=prompt,
    76→        repo_root=repo_root,
    77→        output_file=output_file,
    78→    )
    79→    config = _resolve_retry_config(deps)
    80→    log_sections: list[str] = []
    81→
    82→    for attempt in range(1, config.max_attempts + 1):
    83→        header, result = _run_batch_attempt(
    84→            cmd=cmd,
    85→            deps=deps,
    86→            output_file=output_file,
    87→            log_file=log_file,
    88→            log_sections=log_sections,
    89→            attempt=attempt,
    90→            max_attempts=config.max_attempts,
    91→            use_popen=config.use_popen,
    92→            live_log_interval=config.live_log_interval,
    93→            stall_seconds=config.stall_seconds,
    94→        )
    95→        early_return = _handle_early_attempt_return(result)
    96→        if early_return is not None:
    97→            return early_return
    98→        timeout_or_stall = _handle_timeout_or_stall(
    99→            header=header,
   100→            result=result,
   101→            deps=deps,
   102→            output_file=output_file,
   103→            log_file=log_file,
   104→            log_sections=log_sections,
   105→            stall_seconds=config.stall_seconds,
   106→        )
   107→        if timeout_or_stall is not None:
   108→            return timeout_or_stall
   109→
   110→        log_sections.append(

   112→        )
   113→
   114→        success_code = _handle_successful_attempt(

   118→            deps=deps,

   121→        if success_code is not None:

   123→        failure_code = _handle_failed_attempt(
   124→            result=result,

   126→            attempt=attempt,
   127→            max_attempts=config.max_attempts,
   128→            retry_backoff_seconds=config.retry_backoff_seconds,
   129→            log_file=log_file,
   130→            log_sections=log_sections,
   131→        )
   132→        if failure_code is not None:
   133→            return failure_code
   134→
   135→    deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   136→    return 1

   274→                else:

   284→def _render_item(
   285→    item: dict, dim_scores: dict, issues_scoped: dict, explain: bool,
   286→    potentials: dict | None = None,
   287→) -> None:
   288→    kind = item.get("kind")
   289→    kind_renderer = _KIND_RENDERERS.get(kind)
   290→    if kind_renderer is not None:
   291→        kind_renderer(item)
   292→        return
   293→
   294→    confidence = item.get("confidence", "medium")
   295→    print(colorize(f"  ({confidence} confidence)", "bold"))
   296→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 60, "dim"))
   297→    print(f"  {colorize(item.get('summary', ''), 'yellow')}")
   298→    _render_item_type(item)
   299→
   300→    if item.get("kind", "issue") == "subjective_dimension":
   301→        _render_subjective_dimension(item, explain=explain)
   302→        return
   303→
   304→    detail = _render_issue_detail(item)
   305→    _render_score_impact(item, dim_scores, potentials)
   306→    _render_auto_fix_batch_hint(item, issues_scoped)
   307→    if explain:

   311→def _item_label(item: dict, idx: int, total: int) -> str:
   312→    queue_pos = item.get("queue_position")
   313→    if queue_pos and total > 1:
   314→        return f"  [#{queue_pos}]"
   315→    if total > 1:
   316→        return f"  [{idx + 1}/{total}]"
   317→    pos_str = f"  (#{ queue_pos} in queue)" if queue_pos else ""
   318→    return f"  Next item{pos_str}"

   321→def render_terminal_items(
   322→    items: list[dict],
   323→    dim_scores: dict,
   324→    issues_scoped: dict,
   325→    *,
   326→    group: str,
   327→    explain: bool,
   328→    potentials: dict | None = None,
   329→    plan: dict | None = None,
   330→    cluster_filter: str | None = None,
   331→) -> None:
   332→    # Show focus header if plan has active cluster
   333→    if plan and plan.get("active_cluster"):
   334→        cluster_name = plan["active_cluster"]
   335→        clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   336→        cluster_data = clusters.get(cluster_name, {})
   337→        total = len(cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []))
   338→        print(colorize(f"\n  Focused on: {cluster_name} ({len(items)} of {total} remaining)", "cyan"))
   339→
   340→    if group != "item":
   341→        _render_grouped(items, group)
   342→        return
   343→
   344→    # Detect cluster drill-in: multiple items with cluster focus active
   345→    is_cluster_drill = len(items) > 1 and (
   346→        cluster_filter or (plan and plan.get("active_cluster"))
   347→    )
   348→
   349→    for idx, item in enumerate(items):
   350→        if idx > 0:
   351→            print()
   352→        # Full card for first item, compact for rest in cluster drill-in
   353→        if is_cluster_drill and idx > 0:
   354→            _render_compact_item(item, idx, len(items))
   355→            continue
   356→        label = _item_label(item, idx, len(items))
   357→        print(colorize(label, "bold"))
   358→        _render_item(item, dim_scores, issues_scoped, explain=explain, potentials=potentials)
   359→

    24→def _cmd_commit_log_status(plan: dict) -> None:
    25→    """Show full commit-log status: uncommitted, committed, git context."""
    26→    git = detect_git_context()
    27→    summary = commit_tracking_summary(plan)
    28→
    29→    print(colorize("  Commit Tracking Status", "bold"))
    30→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 40, "dim"))
    31→
    32→    if git.available:
    33→        print(f"  Branch:  {git.branch or '(detached)'}")
    34→        print(f"  HEAD:    {git.head_sha or '?'}")
    35→        if git.has_uncommitted:
    36→            print(colorize("  Working tree has uncommitted changes", "yellow"))
    37→    else:
    38→        print(colorize("  Git: not available", "dim"))
    39→

    44→
    45→    uncommitted = get_uncommitted_issues(plan)

    47→    for fid in uncommitted[:10]:

    55→
    56→    if not uncommitted and not commit_log:

    61→def _cmd_commit_log_record(args: argparse.Namespace, plan: dict) -> None:
    62→    """Record a commit: capture HEAD, move uncommitted → committed, update PR."""
    63→    sha = getattr(args, "sha", None)
    64→    branch = getattr(args, "branch", None)
    65→    note = getattr(args, "note", None)
    66→    only_patterns: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "only", None)
    67→
    68→    # Auto-detect from git if not overridden
    69→    if not sha or not branch:
    70→        git = detect_git_context()
    71→        if git.available:
    72→            sha = sha or git.head_sha
    73→            branch = branch or git.branch
    74→        elif not sha:
    75→            print(colorize("  Cannot detect HEAD. Use --sha to specify.", "red"))
    76→            return
    77→
    78→    # Determine which issues to record
    79→    uncommitted = get_uncommitted_issues(plan)
    80→    if not uncommitted:
    81→        print(colorize("  No uncommitted issues to record.", "yellow"))
    82→        return
    83→
    84→    if only_patterns:
    85→        issue_ids = filter_issue_ids_by_pattern(uncommitted, only_patterns)
    86→        if not issue_ids:
    87→            print(colorize("  No uncommitted issues match --only patterns.", "yellow"))
    88→            return
    89→    else:
    90→        issue_ids = None  # record all
    91→
    92→    record = record_commit(
    93→        plan,
    94→        sha=sha,
    95→        branch=branch,
    96→        issue_ids=issue_ids,
    97→        note=note,
    98→    )
    99→    append_log_entry(
   100→        plan,
   101→        "commit_record",
   102→        issue_ids=record["issue_ids"],
   103→        actor="user",
   104→        note=note,
   105→        detail={"sha": sha, "branch": branch},
   106→    )
   107→    save_plan(plan)
   108→
   109→    recorded = len(record["issue_ids"])
   110→    print(colorize(f"  Recorded commit {sha} with {recorded} issue(s).", "green"))
   111→    if note:
   112→        print(colorize(f"  Note: {note}", "dim"))
   113→
   114→    # Update PR if configured
   115→    config = load_config()
   116→    pr_number = config.get("commit_pr", 0)
   117→    if pr_number:
   118→        try:
   119→            state = state_mod.load_state()
   120→            body = generate_pr_body(plan, state)
   121→            ok = update_pr_body(pr_number, body)
   122→            if ok:
   123→                print(colorize(f"  PR #{pr_number} description updated.", "green"))
   124→            else:
   125→                print(colorize(f"  Could not update PR #{pr_number} (gh may not be available).", "yellow"))
   126→        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
   127→            print(
   128→                colorize(f"  Warning: PR update skipped ({exc}).", "yellow"),
   129→                file=sys.stderr,
   130→            )

    44→def _repair_ghost_cluster_refs(plan: PlanModel, now: str) -> int:
    45→    """Clear override cluster refs that point to non-existent clusters."""
    46→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    47→    overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
    48→    repaired = 0
    49→    for override in overrides.values():
    50→        cluster_name = override.get("cluster")
    51→        if cluster_name and cluster_name not in clusters:
    52→            override["cluster"] = None
    53→            override["updated_at"] = now

    62→def _sync_auto_cluster(
    63→    plan: PlanModel,
    64→    clusters: dict,
    65→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str],
    66→    *,
    67→    cluster_key: str,
    68→    cluster_name: str,
    69→    member_ids: list[str],
    70→    description: str,

    75→    """Create or update an auto-cluster and sync its override entries.
    76→
    77→    Handles the common pattern: check if cluster exists by key, update
    78→    membership/metadata if changed, or create a new cluster.  Always syncs
    79→    override entries for all *member_ids*.
    80→
    81→    Returns 1 if a change was made, 0 otherwise.
    82→    """
    83→    changes = 0
    84→    existing_name = existing_by_key.get(cluster_key)
    85→    if existing_name and existing_name in clusters:
    86→        cluster = clusters[existing_name]
    87→        old_ids = set(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    88→        new_ids_set = set(member_ids)
    89→        if old_ids != new_ids_set or cluster.get("description") != description or cluster.get("action") != action:
    90→            cluster["issue_ids"] = list(member_ids)
    91→            cluster["description"] = description
    92→            cluster["action"] = action
    93→            cluster["updated_at"] = now
    94→            changes = 1
    95→    else:
    96→        new_cluster: Cluster = {
    97→            "name": cluster_name,
    98→            "description": description,
    99→            "issue_ids": list(member_ids),
   100→            "created_at": now,
   101→            "updated_at": now,
   102→            "auto": True,
   103→            "cluster_key": cluster_key,
   104→            "action": action,

   106→        }
   107→        if optional:

   109→        clusters[cluster_name] = new_cluster
   110→        existing_by_key[cluster_key] = cluster_name
   111→        changes = 1

   115→    current_name = existing_by_key.get(cluster_key, cluster_name)
   116→    for fid in member_ids:

   118→            overrides[fid] = {"issue_id": fid, "created_at": now}
   119→        overrides[fid]["cluster"] = current_name

   129→def _sync_issue_clusters(

   137→    """Group open issues by detector/subtype and sync auto-clusters."""

   141→    manual_member_ids: set[str] = set()
   142→    for cluster in clusters.values():

   144→            manual_member_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   145→
   146→    # Collect open, non-suppressed issues and group by key
   147→    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)

   167→    groups = {k: v for k, v in groups.items() if len(v) >= _MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE}
   168→
   169→    for key, member_ids in groups.items():
   170→        active_auto_keys.add(key)
   171→        cluster_name = _cluster_name_from_key(key)
   172→
   173→        # Representative issue for metadata
   174→        rep = issue_data.get(member_ids[0], {})
   175→        detector = rep.get("detector", "")
   176→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   177→        members = [issue_data[fid] for fid in member_ids if fid in issue_data]
   178→
   179→        # Extract subtype from grouping key (typed::detector::subtype)
   180→        key_parts = key.split("::")
   181→        subtype = key_parts[2] if len(key_parts) >= 3 else None
   182→
   183→        description = _generate_description(cluster_name, members, meta, subtype)
   184→        action = _generate_action(meta, subtype)
   185→
   186→        # User-modified clusters: merge new members only, keep user edits
   187→        existing_name = existing_by_key.get(key)
   188→        if existing_name and existing_name in clusters:
   189→            cluster = clusters[existing_name]
   190→            if cluster.get("user_modified"):
   191→                existing_ids = set(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   192→                new_ids = [fid for fid in member_ids if fid not in existing_ids]
   193→                if new_ids:
   194→                    cluster["issue_ids"].extend(new_ids)
   195→                    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   196→                    changes += 1
   197→                # Still sync overrides for all members
   198→                overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
   199→                for fid in member_ids:
   200→                    if fid not in overrides:
   201→                        overrides[fid] = {"issue_id": fid, "created_at": now}
   202→                    overrides[fid]["cluster"] = existing_name
   203→                    overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
   204→                continue
   205→
   206→        # Handle name collision (existing auto-cluster with different key)
   207→        if cluster_name in clusters and clusters[cluster_name].get("cluster_key") != key:
   208→            cluster_name = f"{cluster_name}-{len(member_ids)}"
   209→
   210→        changes += _sync_auto_cluster(
   211→            plan, clusters, existing_by_key,
   212→            cluster_key=key,
   213→            cluster_name=cluster_name,
   214→            member_ids=member_ids,
   215→            description=description,
   216→            action=action,
   217→            now=now,
   218→        )
   219→
   220→    return changes
   221→
   222→
   223→def _sync_subjective_clusters(
   224→    plan: PlanModel,
   225→    state: StateModel,
   226→    issues: dict,
   227→    clusters: dict,
   228→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str],
   229→    active_auto_keys: set[str],
   230→    now: str,
   231→    *,
   232→    target_strict: float,
   233→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   234→    cycle_just_completed: bool = False,
   235→) -> int:
   236→    """Sync unscored, stale, and under-target subjective dimension clusters."""
   237→    changes = 0
   238→
   239→    all_subjective_ids = sorted(
   240→        fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   241→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   242→    )
   243→
   244→    if policy is not None:
   245→        unscored_state_ids = policy.unscored_ids
   246→        stale_state_ids = policy.stale_ids
   247→    else:
   248→        unscored_state_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   249→        stale_state_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   250→
   251→    unscored_queue_ids = sorted(
   252→        fid for fid in all_subjective_ids if fid in unscored_state_ids
   253→    )
   254→    stale_queue_ids = sorted(
   255→        fid for fid in all_subjective_ids
   256→        if fid in stale_state_ids and fid not in unscored_state_ids
   257→    )
   258→
   259→    # -- Initial review cluster (unscored, min size 1) ---------------------
   260→    if len(unscored_queue_ids) >= _MIN_UNSCORED_CLUSTER_SIZE:
   261→        active_auto_keys.add(_UNSCORED_KEY)
   262→        cli_keys = [fid.removeprefix(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) for fid in unscored_queue_ids]
   263→        description = f"Initial review of {len(unscored_queue_ids)} unscored subjective dimensions"
   264→        action = f"desloppify review --prepare --dimensions {','.join(cli_keys)}"
   265→        changes += _sync_auto_cluster(
   266→            plan, clusters, existing_by_key,
   267→            cluster_key=_UNSCORED_KEY,
   268→            cluster_name=_UNSCORED_NAME,
   269→            member_ids=unscored_queue_ids,
   270→            description=description,
   271→            action=action,
   272→            now=now,
   273→        )
   274→
   275→    # -- Stale review cluster (previously scored, min size 2) --------------
   276→    if len(stale_queue_ids) >= _MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE:
   277→        active_auto_keys.add(_STALE_KEY)
   278→        cli_keys = [fid.removeprefix(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) for fid in stale_queue_ids]
   279→        description = f"Re-review {len(stale_queue_ids)} stale subjective dimensions"
   280→        action = (
   281→            "desloppify review --prepare --dimensions "
   282→            + ",".join(cli_keys)
   283→        )
   284→        changes += _sync_auto_cluster(
   285→            plan, clusters, existing_by_key,
   286→            cluster_key=_STALE_KEY,
   287→            cluster_name=_STALE_NAME,
   288→            member_ids=stale_queue_ids,
   289→            description=description,
   290→            action=action,
   291→            now=now,
   292→        )
   293→
   294→    # -- Under-target review cluster (optional, current but below target) ----
   295→    if policy is not None:
   296→        under_target_ids = policy.under_target_ids
   297→    else:
   298→        under_target_ids = current_under_target_ids(state, target_strict=target_strict)
   299→    under_target_queue_ids = sorted(under_target_ids)
   300→
   301→    # Prune: remove IDs that were previously in the under-target cluster
   302→    # but are no longer under target (they've improved above threshold).
   303→    prev_ut_cluster = clusters.get(_UNDER_TARGET_NAME, {})
   304→    prev_ut_ids = set(prev_ut_cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   305→    order = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   306→    _ut_prune = [
   307→        fid for fid in prev_ut_ids
   308→        if fid not in under_target_ids
   309→        and fid not in stale_state_ids
   310→        and fid not in unscored_state_ids
   311→        and fid in order
   312→    ]
   313→    for fid in _ut_prune:
   314→        order.remove(fid)
   315→        changes += 1
   316→
   317→    # Guard: only inject under-target items when no objective issues
   318→    # remain open — mirror the guard used by sync_stale_dimensions().
   319→    if policy is not None:
   320→        has_objective_items = policy.has_objective_backlog
   321→    else:
   322→        has_objective_items = any(
   323→            f.get("status") == "open"
   324→            and f.get("detector") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   325→            and not f.get("suppressed")
   326→            for f in issues.values()
   327→        )
   328→
   329→    if not has_objective_items and len(under_target_queue_ids) >= _MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE:
   330→        active_auto_keys.add(_UNDER_TARGET_KEY)
   331→        cli_keys = [fid.removeprefix(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) for fid in under_target_queue_ids]
   332→        description = (
   333→            f"Consider re-reviewing {len(under_target_queue_ids)} "
   334→            f"dimensions under target score"
   335→        )
   336→        action = (
   337→            "desloppify review --prepare --dimensions "
   338→            + ",".join(cli_keys)
   339→        )
   340→        changes += _sync_auto_cluster(
   341→            plan, clusters, existing_by_key,
   342→            [REDACTED],
   343→            cluster_name=_UNDER_TARGET_NAME,
   344→            member_ids=under_target_queue_ids,
   345→            description=description,
   346→            action=action,
   347→            now=now,
   348→            optional=True,
   349→        )
   350→
   351→        # Ensure under-target IDs are in queue_order (at the back)
   352→        order = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   353→        existing_order = set(order)
   354→        for fid in under_target_queue_ids:
   355→            if fid not in existing_order:
   356→                order.append(fid)
   357→
   358→    # Evict under-target IDs from queue when objective backlog has returned
   359→    # — but NOT after a completed cycle, where they should stay for review.
   360→    if has_objective_items and not cycle_just_completed:
   361→        _objective_evict = [
   362→            fid for fid in order
   363→            if fid in under_target_ids
   364→        ]
   365→        for fid in _objective_evict:
   366→            order.remove(fid)
   367→            changes += 1
   368→
   369→    return changes
   370→
   371→
   372→def _prune_stale_clusters(
   373→    plan: PlanModel,
   374→    issues: dict,
   375→    clusters: dict,
   376→    active_auto_keys: set[str],
   377→    now: str,
   378→) -> int:
   379→    """Delete auto-clusters that no longer have matching groups."""
   380→    changes = 0
   381→    for name in list(clusters.keys()):
   382→        cluster = clusters[name]
   383→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
   384→            continue
   385→        ck = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   386→        if ck in active_auto_keys:
   387→            continue
   388→        if cluster.get("user_modified"):
   389→            # Keep user-modified clusters but prune dead member IDs
   390→            alive = [fid for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   391→                     if fid in issues and issues[fid].get("status") == "open"]
   392→            if alive:
   393→                if len(alive) != len(cluster.get("issue_ids", [])):
   394→                    cluster["issue_ids"] = alive
   395→                    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   396→                    changes += 1
   397→                continue
   398→            # All members gone — delete even if user_modified
   399→        # Delete stale cluster
   400→        del clusters[name]
   401→        # Clear cluster refs from overrides
   402→        for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
   403→            override = plan.get("overrides", {}).get(fid)
   404→            if override and override.get("cluster") == name:
   405→                override["cluster"] = None
   406→                override["updated_at"] = now
   407→        if plan.get("active_cluster") == name:
   408→            plan["active_cluster"] = None
   409→        changes += 1
   410→    return changes
   411→
   412→
   413→def auto_cluster_issues(
   414→    plan: PlanModel,
   415→    state: StateModel,
   416→    *,
   417→    target_strict: float = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
   418→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   419→    cycle_just_completed: bool = False,
   420→) -> int:
   421→    """Regenerate auto-clusters from current open issues.
   422→
   423→    Returns count of changes made (clusters created, updated, or deleted).
   424→    """
   425→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   426→
   427→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   428→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   429→
   430→    # Map existing auto-clusters by cluster_key
   431→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str] = {}  # cluster_key → cluster_name
   432→    for name, cluster in list(clusters.items()):
   433→        if cluster.get("auto"):
   434→            ck = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   435→            if ck:
   436→                existing_by_key[ck] = name
   437→
   438→    now = utc_now()
   439→    active_auto_keys: set[str] = set()
   440→    changes = 0
   441→
   442→    changes += _sync_issue_clusters(
   443→        plan, issues, clusters, existing_by_key, active_auto_keys, now,
   444→    )
   445→    changes += _sync_subjective_clusters(
   446→        plan, state, issues, clusters, existing_by_key, active_auto_keys, now,
   447→        target_strict=target_strict,
   448→        policy=policy,
   449→        cycle_just_completed=cycle_just_completed,
   450→    )
   451→    changes += _prune_stale_clusters(
   452→        plan, issues, clusters, active_auto_keys, now,
   453→    )
   454→    changes += _repair_ghost_cluster_refs(plan, now)
   455→
   456→    plan["updated"] = now
   457→    return changes
   458→
   459→
   460→__all__ = [
   461→    "AUTO_PREFIX",
   462→    "auto_cluster_issues",
   463→]

   101→class TestCommonExtractBody:
